chapters.name: 聪明/有知识/有经验/精明/狡猾/严谨/谨慎/思考

words.tr:
adj. 智力的；
n. 知识分子；
words.ex: He is an intellectual person who loves solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱解决数学问题的智力型人。
words.en: An intellectual is someone who spends a lot of time studying and thinking about complicated ideas.

words.ex: He is intellectually curious about science.
words.ex_cn: 他在智力上对科学充满好奇。
words.en: In a way that relates to the intellect or is characterized by intellectual activity.

words.ex: The professor's lectures were marked by a high degree of intellectuality.
words.ex_cn: 教授的讲座以高度的智力性为标志。
words.en: The capacity for understanding and reasoning; the intellect.

words.ex: The erudite professor knows many ancient languages.
words.ex_cn: 这位博学的教授懂得许多古代语言。
words.en: Having or showing great knowledge or learning.

words.ex: He is a genius in math.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学方面是个天才。
words.en: Someone who is a genius is a person who is exceptionally intelligent or talented, especially in a particular field.

words.tr: adj. 全知的；无所不知的
words.ex: The omniscient narrator knows everything about the characters.
words.ex_cn: 全知的叙述者了解角色的一切。
words.en: Knowing everything; having infinite awareness, understanding, and insight.

words.ex: His knowledge is encyclopedic.
words.ex_cn: 他的知识非常渊博。
words.en: Comprehensive in terms of information or knowledge, resembling or suggesting an encyclopedia.

words.ex: He is an astute businessman who always makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他是个精明的商人，总是做出明智的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as astute, you think they are clever and can see through things quickly and make good judgments.

words.tr:
v. 密谋；激起…的兴趣
n. 阴谋诡计；密谋策划
words.ex: They intrigue to take over the company.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋接管这家公司。
words.en: If something intrigues you, it interests you a lot because it seems strange or mysterious.

words.tr: adj. 精明的；敏锐的；机灵的；
words.ex: He made a shrewd decision to buy the house low.
words.ex_cn: 他精明地决定低价买下这栋房子。
words.en: A shrewd person is able to understand and judge a situation quickly and to use this understanding to their own advantage.

words.tr: adj. 机智的；圆滑的；得体的
words.ex: He was tactful when he said no to her request.
words.ex_cn: 当他拒绝她的请求时，他很得体。
words.en: If you describe someone as tactful, you approve of them because they are careful not to say or do anything that would offend or upset other people.

words.tr: adj. 精明的；老谋深算的
words.ex: He is a canny trader who always makes smart choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精明的交易员，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: A canny person is clever and able to think quickly, especially in business or politics.

words.tr: adj. 一丝不苟的；缜密的
words.ex: He is meticulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他仔细检查作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as meticulous, you mean that they do things very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.ex: Her meticulousness in preparing for the event ensured its success.
words.ex_cn: 她在准备活动时的谨小慎微确保了活动的成功。
words.en: The quality of being very careful and precise.

words.ex: She meticulously cleaned every corner of the room.
words.ex_cn: 她异常细致地打扫了房间的每一个角落。
words.en: If you do something meticulously, you do it very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.ex: He was circumspect before signing the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他在签署合同之前非常谨慎。
words.en: If you are circumspect, you think carefully about something before doing it, because there may be risks involved.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有见识的；判断正确的
words.ex: He made a judicious choice about which book to buy.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个明智的买书决定。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as judicious, you approve of it because you think that it shows good judgment and sense.

words.tr: adj. 不明智的；不慎重的；浅薄的；不聪明的
words.ex: He made an injudicious decision and lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个不明智的决定，失去了工作。
words.en: If you describe a person or something that they have done as injudicious, you are critical of them because they have shown very poor judgment.

words.tr:
adj. 深思熟虑的；故意的；
v. 深思熟虑；
words.ex: He made a deliberate choice to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他深思熟虑后决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you do something that is deliberate, you planned or decided to do it beforehand, and so it happens on purpose rather than by chance.

words.ex: He deliberately broke the rule.
words.ex_cn: 他有意地违反了规则。
words.en: If you do something deliberately, you do it intentionally or after thinking about it carefully.

words.tr: adj. 彻底的；完全的；详尽的；
words.ex: He did a thorough cleaning of the house.
words.ex_cn: 他对房子进行了彻底的清洁。
words.en: A thorough action or activity is one that is done very carefully and in a detailed way so that nothing is forgotten.

words.ex: He cleaned the room thoroughly.
words.ex_cn: 他彻底地打扫了房间。
words.en: In a thorough manner; completely and carefully.

words.ex: His thoroughness in checking the answers ensured no mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他检查答案时的彻底确保了没有错误。
words.en: The quality of being complete with regard to every detail; exactness.

words.tr: adj. 谨慎的；慎重的；精明的
words.ex: He is prudent with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他在花钱时很谨慎。
words.en: If you are prudent, you are careful and avoid taking unnecessary risks.

words.ex: He made an imprudent decision and lost all his money.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个鲁莽的决定，失去了所有钱。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as imprudent, you think it is not sensible or carefully thought out.

words.ex: His imprudence caused the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的鲁莽导致了这场事故。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as imprudence, you mean it is not sensible or carefully thought out.

words.ex: He was cautious when crossing the busy street.
words.ex_cn: 他过繁忙的街道时很小心。
words.en: If you are cautious, you are careful and avoid taking risks.

words.tr:
n. 小心；警告；注意；
v. 警告；劝...小心；
words.ex: He drove with caution on the icy road.
words.ex_cn: 他在结冰的道路上小心驾驶。
words.en: Caution is care that you take in order to avoid possible danger or trouble.

words.ex: He is scrupulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他检查作业时一丝不苟。
words.en: If you are scrupulous, you are careful, thorough, and extremely attentive to details.

words.tr: adv. 小心翼翼地；严谨地
words.ex: She reviewed the contract scrupulously before signing it.
words.ex_cn: 她在签署合同前仔细审阅。
words.en: If someone is scrupulous, they take care to do things properly and correctly.

words.tr:
adj. 精心制作的；详尽的；
v. 精心制作；详尽阐述；
words.ex: She wore an elaborate dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件精心制作的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: To elaborate means to add more details to something that has already been said or written, making it more complex or detailed. As an adjective, it describes something that is very complex and detailed.

words.tr: n. 一丝不苟；小心翼翼；谨小慎微
words.ex: His punctiliousness in preparing the report impressed his superiors.
words.ex_cn: 他在准备报告时的一丝不苟给上级留下了深刻印象。
words.en: The quality of being very careful to behave correctly or to give attention to details.

words.tr: adj. （言行）谨慎的；不显眼的；朴素的
words.ex: He was discreet about his personal life.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的私生活很低调。
words.en: If you are discreet, you are polite and careful in what you do or say, because you want to avoid embarrassing or offending someone.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；不慎重的；鲁莽的
words.ex: He was indiscreet and told everyone the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他不够谨慎，把秘密告诉了所有人。
words.en: If you describe someone as indiscreet, you mean that they do or say things in public which they should only do or say secretly or in private.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.ex: He showed wariness when talking to strangers.
words.ex_cn: 他和陌生人交谈时表现出谨慎。
words.en: Wariness is the feeling or state of being cautious about possible dangers or problems.

words.tr: v. 守卫；“guard”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 谨慎的；有保留的；警戒着的；
words.ex: The soldiers guarded the gate all night.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们整晚守卫着大门。
words.en: If you are guarded, you are careful not to show your feelings or give away information.

words.tr: adj. 讳莫如深的；守口如瓶的；谨慎小心的；狡猾的
words.ex: He was cagey when asked about his plans.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到他的计划时，他很谨慎。
words.en: If you describe someone as cagey, you mean that they are careful not to give too much information or to show their feelings.

words.tr: adj. 经验主义的；以经验为根据的；
words.ex: The scientist used empirical data to support her theory.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家使用经验数据来支持她的理论。
words.en: Empirical evidence or study relies on practical experience rather than theories.

words.tr: adj. 有深刻了解的；富有洞察力的
words.ex: His insightful comment helped us understand the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他富有洞察力的评论帮助我们理解了这个问题。
words.en: If you describe someone or their remarks as insightful, you mean that they show a very good understanding of people and situations.

words.ex: His insight helped the team solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他的洞察力帮助团队解决了问题。
words.en: If you gain insight or an insight into a complex situation or problem, you gain an accurate and deep understanding of it.

words.ex: He calculates the total cost quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速计算出总成本。
words.en: To determine by mathematical methods; compute.

words.ex: The calculation took only five minutes.
words.ex_cn: 这个计算只花了五分钟。
words.en: The process of using mathematics to find a number or amount.

words.tr: adj. 可计算的；可推断出的
words.ex: The risk is calculable and manageable.
words.ex_cn: 这种风险是可以计算和管理的。
words.en: If something is calculable, it can be calculated or estimated.

words.tr: adj. 精明练达的；有远见的；有洞察力的
words.ex: He is a sagacious man who always makes wise choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个睿智的人，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: Having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgment; shrewd.

words.tr: n. 苦心而成的著作；学术作品；刻苦钻研
words.ex: The professor's latest lucubration is a comprehensive study on ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 教授最新的苦心之作是对古代文明的综合研究。
words.en: A lucubration is a piece of writing that is produced by someone who studies or works hard at night, often implying that it is the result of deep thought and effort.

words.ex: He is proficient in playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他弹钢琴很熟练。
words.en: If you are proficient in something, you can do it well because you have learned how to do it.

words.tr: v. 考虑；深思；凝视；思考…的可能性
words.ex: He contemplates quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他正在考虑辞去工作。
words.en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

chapters.name: 复杂/难以理解/困惑/模糊

words.ex: The instructions confuse me.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明让我感到困惑。
words.en: If you confuse two things, you mix them up in your mind so that you think one is the other.

words.tr:
adj. 旋绕的；费解的
v. 盘旋；卷绕；“convolute”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The path through the garden was convoluted.
words.ex_cn: 花园里的小路蜿蜒曲折。
words.en: If you describe something such as a story, explanation, or system as convoluted, you mean that it is complicated and difficult to understand.

words.ex: The lock has an intricate design.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁有复杂的结构。
words.en: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

words.ex: Too many rules can complicate the game.
words.ex_cn: 太多的规则会使游戏变得复杂。
words.en: To make something more difficult to understand or deal with by adding more parts or details.

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

words.ex: The artist lived in obscurity for most of his life.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家一生大部分时间都默默无闻。
words.en: The state of being unknown, inconspicuous, or unimportant.

words.tr: adj. 感觉不到的；极细微的
words.ex: The change was imperceptible to the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个变化肉眼无法察觉。
words.en: Something that is imperceptible is so small or slight that it cannot be seen or noticed.

words.ex: His perception of the sound was very sharp.
words.ex_cn: 他对声音的感知非常敏锐。
words.en: Your perception of something is the way that you think about it or the impression you have of it.

words.tr: adj. 观察敏锐的；有洞察力的
words.ex: She is perceptive and notices small changes.
words.ex_cn: 她很有洞察力，能注意到细微的变化。
words.en: If you describe someone as perceptive, you mean that they are good at noticing or understanding things.

words.tr: adj. 可察觉到的；看得出的；可感知的
words.ex: The change was barely perceptible.
words.ex_cn: 这个变化几乎无法察觉。
words.en: Something that is perceptible can be seen, noticed, or felt.

words.ex: The mysterious box appeared on his doorstep.
words.ex_cn: 那个神秘的盒子出现在他的门口。
words.en: If someone or something is mysterious, it is not fully understood or explained and seems interesting or puzzling.

words.ex: The lights went out mysteriously.
words.ex_cn: 灯光神秘地熄灭了。
words.en: In a way that is difficult to understand or explain; in a manner that suggests mystery.

words.ex: The depth of the ocean is unfathomable.
words.ex_cn: 海洋的深度是深不可测的。
words.en: If something is unfathomable, it is so mysterious or complicated that it is impossible to understand or explain.

words.tr: adj. 神秘的；不可思议的；
words.ex: The uncanny silence in the forest made him nervous.
words.ex_cn: 森林里那神秘的寂静让他感到紧张。
words.en: If you describe something as uncanny, you mean that it is strange and difficult to explain.

words.tr: adj. 难以达到的；无法接近的；
words.ex: The mountain peak is inaccessible in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这座山峰在冬天难以到达。
words.en: If a place is inaccessible, it is very difficult or impossible to reach or enter.

words.tr: adj. 无法解释的；费解的
words.ex: His sudden silence was inexplicable.
words.ex_cn: 他突然的沉默无法解释。
words.en: If something is inexplicable, you cannot explain why it happens or why it is true.

words.ex: The ancient symbol remains an enigma.
words.ex_cn: 这个古代符号仍然是一个谜。
words.en: An enigma is something that is mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.ex: The book contains esoteric ideas that only experts understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了只有专家才能理解的深奥思想。
words.en: Intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with a specialized knowledge or interest.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.ex: The abstruse math problem confused the students.
words.ex_cn: 这个深奥的数学问题让学生们感到困惑。
words.en: Difficult to understand; obscure.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；不易被抓获（觉察、理解或记忆）的；
words.ex: The truth remained elusive.
words.ex_cn: 真相难以捉摸。
words.en: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; difficult to remember or understand.

words.ex: The strange noise confounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 奇怪的声音让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: To confuse and surprise someone, especially by being difficult to understand or deal with.

words.ex: The riddle perplexed the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个谜语让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something perplexes you, it confuses and worries you because you do not understand it or because it causes you difficulty.

words.ex: His answer was vague and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答不明确，难以理解。
words.en: If something written or spoken is vague, it does not explain or express things clearly.

words.ex: The vagueness of his answer made me confused.
words.ex_cn: 他回答的模糊让我感到困惑。
words.en: The quality or state of being unclear, indefinite, or indistinct.

words.ex: He vaguely remembered the name.
words.ex_cn: 他模糊地记得这个名字。
words.en: If you describe something as vaguely, you mean that it is not clear, distinct, or definite.

words.tr: adj. 昏沉的，糊里糊涂的; v. 使……迷惑；使……烂醉（befuddle 的过去分词）
words.ex: He was befuddled by the simple math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他被这个简单的数学题搞糊涂了。
words.en: If someone is befuddled, they cannot understand something or think clearly about it, often because they are tired or have drunk too much alcohol.

words.tr: v. 使迷惑；使...不知所措
words.ex: The strange signs bewilder the children.
words.ex_cn: 这些奇怪的符号让孩子们感到迷惑。
words.en: If something bewilders you, it is so confusing or difficult that you cannot understand it.

words.tr: adj. 令人困惑不解的； v. “puzzle”的现在分词；
words.ex: The puzzle was puzzling even for experts.
words.ex_cn: 这个谜题即使对专家来说也令人困惑不解。
words.en: If something is puzzling, it is difficult to understand or explain because it is not clear or is confusing.

words.tr: v. （故意地）混淆；使混乱；使困惑
words.ex: He tries to obfuscate the truth with complicated words.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用复杂的词语混淆真相。
words.en: To obfuscate something means to deliberately make it unclear or difficult to understand.

words.tr:
v. 使迷惑；使不知所措
n. 迷惑；困惑；为难
words.ex: The tricky question nonplused the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这个棘手的问题让老师不知所措。
words.en: To cause to be at a loss as to what to say, think, or do; perplex.

words.tr:
v. 使困惑；难倒；阻碍
n. 挡板；遮护物；阻碍体
words.ex: The magic trick baffled the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something baffles you, you cannot understand it or explain it.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

words.ex: The sentence has ambiguity because it can mean two things.
words.ex_cn: 这句话有歧义，因为它可以有两种意思。
words.en: If you say that there is ambiguity in something, you mean that it is unclear or confusing, or it can be understood in more than one way.

words.ex: The thick forest was impenetrable.
words.ex_cn: 这片茂密的森林无法穿越。
words.en: Impenetrable is used to describe something that cannot be passed through, entered, or understood.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊其词的；难以解释的
words.ex: His answer was equivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可。
words.en: If you are equivocal, you are deliberately vague in what you say, because you want to avoid speaking the truth or making a decision.

words.ex: Love is an intangible thing.
words.ex_cn: 爱是一种无形的东西。
words.en: Something that is intangible is not able to be touched or seen, but is still important or valuable.

words.ex: The floor is slippery after it rains.
words.ex_cn: 下雨后地板很滑。
words.en: Something that is slippery is smooth, wet, or oily and is therefore difficult to walk on or to hold.

words.tr: adj. 无法触及的；摸不着的；难解的
words.ex: The concept of infinity is often considered impalpable.
words.ex_cn: 无限的概念常常被认为是难以理解的。
words.en: Impalpable means something that cannot be perceived by touch or is very difficult to understand or define.

words.ex: The ancient text contained arcane symbols that no one could understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本古籍中包含着无人能理解的晦涩难解的符号。
words.en: Arcane refers to something that is mysterious or difficult to understand, often because it is known or understood by only a few people.

words.tr: adj. 隐秘的；秘密的；隐晦的
words.ex: He gave a cryptic answer and left.
words.ex_cn: 他给了一个神秘的回答，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something as cryptic, you mean that it is mysterious or difficult to understand.

words.ex: He posted an anonymous comment online.
words.ex_cn: 他在网上发布了一条匿名评论。
words.en: If you remain anonymous when you do something, you do not let people know that you were the person who did it.

words.tr: adj. 无法实现的；难以得到的
words.ex: The prize was unattainable for him.
words.ex_cn: 这个奖对他来说是无法获得的。
words.en: If you say that something is unattainable, you mean that it cannot be achieved or is not available.

words.tr:
adj. 客观的；
n. 目标；目的；
words.ex: He gave an objective opinion about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影给出了一个客观的看法。
words.en: An objective is something that you plan to do or achieve.

words.ex: He judged the case objectively.
words.ex_cn: 他客观地评判了这个案件。
words.en: In a way that is not influenced by personal feelings or opinions.

words.ex: He raised an objection to the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了反对。
words.en: An objection is an expression or feeling of disapproval or opposition; a reason for disagreeing.

words.tr: adj. 令人不快的；令人反感的；讨厌的
words.ex: The movie contains objectionable content.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影包含令人反感的内容。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as objectionable, you consider them to be extremely offensive and unacceptable.

words.ex: The reporter tried to show objectivity in the news story.
words.ex_cn: 记者试图在新闻报道中体现客观性。
words.en: Objectivity is the quality of being objective, which means not influenced by personal feelings or opinions in considering and representing facts.

words.ex: The judge was evenhanded in treating both sides.
words.ex_cn: 法官对双方都公平对待。
words.en: Treating everyone equally and fairly.

words.tr: n. 一视同仁；（对争论双方）持平；公正
words.ex: The judge's evenhandedness in the case was widely praised.
words.ex_cn: 法官在这个案件中的公正性广受赞誉。
words.en: The quality of being fair and impartial.

words.tr: adj. 公正的；不偏不倚的；
words.ex: The judge was impartial in the trial.
words.ex_cn: 法官在审判中是公正的。
words.en: Someone who is impartial is not directly involved in a particular situation, and is therefore able to give a fair opinion or decision about it.

words.ex: He showed partiality toward his favorite student.
words.ex_cn: 他对最喜欢的学生表现出偏袒。
words.en: If you have a partiality for something, you like it very much.

words.ex: The judge showed impartiality in the trial.
words.ex_cn: 法官在审判中表现出公平。
words.en: Impartiality is the quality of being unbiased or not favoring one side over another.

words.ex: The teacher showed fairness in grading all students.
words.ex_cn: 老师在给所有学生评分时展现了公平。
words.en: Fairness is the quality of treating people equally or in a way that is right or reasonable.

words.tr: adj. 现实的；现实主义的；
words.ex: He made a realistic plan to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个现实的存钱计划。
words.en: If you are realistic about a situation, you recognize and accept its true nature and try to deal with it in a practical way.

words.ex: He had a realization that he needed to change his life.
words.ex_cn: 他领悟到自己需要改变生活。
words.en: The act of becoming fully aware of something as a fact; the achievement of something desired or anticipated.

words.ex: The movie shows realism by depicting everyday life honestly.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影通过真实地描绘日常生活展现现实主义。
words.en: Realism is the quality or fact of representing a person, thing, or situation accurately or in a way that is true to life.

words.tr: adj. 务实的；实事求是的；
words.ex: He took a pragmatic approach to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他采取了务实的方法来解决问题。
words.en: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a way that is based on practical rather than theoretical considerations.

words.tr: n. 实用主义；务实思想
words.ex: He shows pragmatism by choosing the cheapest option.
words.ex_cn: 他选择最便宜的选项，体现了务实精神。
words.en: Pragmatism is a way of dealing with problems in a practical way rather than by following theories or principles.

words.tr: adj. 功能的；起作用的；实用的；
words.ex: This chair is functional and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子功能性强且舒适。
words.en: Relating to the way in which something works or operates.

words.ex: The building is functionally divided into offices and meeting rooms.
words.ex_cn: 这栋建筑在功能上被划分为办公室和会议室。
words.en: In a way that relates to the way in which something works or operates.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；功利主义的；
words.ex: The chair is utilitarian and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子实用又舒适。
words.en: Utilitarian means relating to or adhering to the belief that the value of a thing or an action is determined by its utility.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.tr: adj. 合法的；法律认可的；合理的；
words.ex: This contract is legitimate and signed by both parties.
words.ex_cn: 这份合同是合法的，并由双方签署。
words.en: Something that is legitimate is acceptable according to the law.

chapters.name: 正确/真实/正直/可信赖/忠诚

words.ex: This coupon is valid until next month.
words.ex_cn: 这张优惠券到下个月都有效。
words.en: If something such as a document or agreement is valid, it is legally acceptable or officially recognized.

words.ex: The validity of the test results is important.
words.ex_cn: 测试结果的有效性很重要。
words.en: The quality of being logically or factually sound; soundness or cogency.

words.ex: The validation of the data is crucial for the accuracy of the report.
words.ex_cn: 数据的验证对于报告的准确性至关重要。
words.en: Validation is the process of checking or proving the validity or accuracy of something.

words.ex: The mistake will invalidate the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误会使结果无效。
words.en: To invalidate something such as a contract or an election means to make it officially not valid.

words.ex: The truth is that he was late for work.
words.ex_cn: 事实是他上班迟到了。
words.en: The truth is the true facts about something, rather than what is imagined or invented.

words.ex: He showed truthfulness when he told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 当他讲真话时，他表现出了诚实。
words.en: The quality of being honest and not containing or telling any lies.

words.ex: He gave a precise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了准确的答案。
words.en: If you give precise information or precise instructions, you give exact details so that there is no confusion about what should be done.

words.tr: adj. 不确切的；不精确的；
words.ex: His answer was imprecise and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答不确切，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as imprecise, you mean that it is not stated or done accurately or clearly.

words.ex: The watch works with great precision.
words.ex_cn: 这块手表运行得非常精确。
words.en: Precision is the quality of being exact and accurate.

words.ex: The imprecision of the measurements led to inaccurate results.
words.ex_cn: 测量不精确导致结果不准确。
words.en: The quality or state of being imprecise; lack of precision.

words.ex: The veracity of his story was questioned by the police.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事的真实性受到了警方的质疑。
words.en: Veracity refers to the quality of being true or accurate.

words.ex: The movie has verisimilitude because it feels real.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影具有逼真性，因为它感觉真实。
words.en: the quality of seeming to be true or real

words.tr:
n. 混凝土；
adj. 具体的；
words.ex: The workers poured concrete to build the foundation.
words.ex_cn: 工人们浇筑混凝土来建造地基。
words.en: Concrete is a hard, strong construction material made by mixing a cementing material (such as Portland cement) and a mineral aggregate (such as sand and gravel) with sufficient water to cause the cement to set and bind the entire mass. In a broader sense, concrete can also refer to something that is tangible, specific, or real.

words.ex: The correctness of the answer is important.
words.ex_cn: 答案的正确性很重要。
words.en: The quality or state of being correct in accordance with facts or truth.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.tr: n. 难以相信；不像真实
words.ex: The implausibility of the story made it hard to believe.
words.ex_cn: 故事的难以置信使得它很难被相信。
words.en: The quality of being unlikely or difficult to believe.

words.tr: adj. 难以置信的；不像真实的；
words.ex: It seems implausible that he won the lottery twice.
words.ex_cn: 他中了两次彩票，这似乎难以置信。
words.en: If you describe something as implausible, you believe that it is unlikely to be true.

words.tr: adj. 真正的；真实的；真迹的；可靠的；
words.ex: This is an authentic painting by Picasso.
words.ex_cn: 这是一幅毕加索的真迹。
words.en: If something is authentic, it is real, true, or what people say it is.

words.ex: The authenticity of the ancient painting was confirmed by experts.
words.ex_cn: 这幅古画的真实性得到了专家的确认。
words.en: The quality of being genuine or not corrupted from the original.

words.ex: The system requires two-factor authentication for added security.
words.ex_cn: 该系统需要双重身份验证以增加安全性。
words.en: Authentication is the process or action of proving or showing something to be true, genuine, or valid.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.tr: adj. 坦率的；坦诚的；偷拍的
words.ex: He gave a candid answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了坦率的回答。
words.en: If you are candid, you are honest and say what you really think.

words.ex: His trustworthiness makes people want to work with him.
words.ex_cn: 他的可信度让人们愿意和他合作。
words.en: The quality of being deserving of trust or confidence.

words.ex: The witness gave credence to the story by crying.
words.ex_cn: 证人通过哭泣使这个故事显得可信。
words.en: Credence is a belief in or acceptance of something as true.

words.ex: He is known for his probity in business.
words.ex_cn: 他以商业中的正直著称。
words.en: Probity is the quality of having strong moral principles and honesty.

words.tr:
adj. 不锋利的；耿直的
v. 使变钝
words.ex: The knife is blunt and cannot cut paper.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀不锋利，切不动纸。
words.en: If you are blunt, you say exactly what you think without trying to be polite.

words.tr:
adj. 忠实的；坚定的
v. 止住（血等的）流出
words.ex: He is a staunch supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的坚定支持者。
words.en: A staunch person is someone who is very loyal and firm in their beliefs or support for someone or something.

words.ex: He swore fealty to the king.
words.ex_cn: 他向国王宣誓效忠。
words.en: Fealty is a formal and solemn promise of loyalty to a king, queen, or other ruler, especially in the Middle Ages.

words.ex: His rectitude in business dealings was well-known.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业交易中的正直是众所周知的。
words.en: Moral integrity; honesty and correctness of judgement or behaviour.

words.ex: His uprightness and integrity were beyond question.
words.ex_cn: 他的正直和诚信是毋庸置疑的。
words.en: The quality of being honest and morally correct.

chapters.name: 不实际/想象/设想/推测/主观/不合理/无根据

words.tr: adj. 不切实际的；不实用的；
words.ex: It's impractical to walk to work every day if you live 50 kilometers away.
words.ex_cn: 如果你住得离工作地点50公里远，每天步行上班是不切实际的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as impractical, you mean that they are not good at planning or organizing things in a practical way, or that their ideas or methods are not suitable for a particular situation.

words.ex: He is practically always late for class.
words.ex_cn: 他几乎总是上课迟到。
words.en: In a way that is almost true or almost the case; virtually.

words.ex: His idealism drives him to help the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他的理想主义驱使他帮助穷人。
words.en: Idealism is the belief that your ideals can be achieved, often when this does not seem likely to others.

words.ex: He idealizes his father as a perfect hero.
words.ex_cn: 他把父亲理想化为一个完美的英雄。
words.en: To regard or represent as perfect or more nearly perfect than is true.

words.tr: adj. 唐吉诃德式的；不切实际的
words.ex: He made a quixotic effort to fix the broken bridge with sticks and glue.
words.ex_cn: 他用树枝和胶水试图修复那座破桥，这真是异想天开。
words.en: If you describe someone's ideas or plans as quixotic, you mean that they are imaginative or hopeful but unrealistic.

words.tr:
adj. 幻想的；有远见的
n. 空想家；有远见的人
words.ex: He had a visionary idea about flying cars.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个关于飞行汽车的幻想想法。
words.en: A visionary is someone who has strong ideas about how things might be different in the future, especially in a way that leads to changes in society or technology.

words.ex: She has excellent night vision.
words.ex_cn: 她有很好的夜视能力。
words.en: Vision is the ability to see, the area that you can see, the ability to imagine how a country, society, industry, etc. could develop in the future and to plan in a suitable way, or an experience in which you see something that is not really there.

words.ex: The smile on his face was illusory.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上的微笑是虚假的。
words.en: If something is illusory, it is not real or true, although it may seem to be.

words.tr: adj. 不可行的；难以实施的
words.ex: It is unfeasible to finish the project in one day.
words.ex_cn: 一天内完成这个项目是不可能的。
words.en: If you say that something is unfeasible, you mean that it is not possible or practical to do it.

words.tr: adj. 梦幻的；荒诞不经的
words.ex: His chimerical dream of flying without wings never came true.
words.ex_cn: 他那不切实际的、不用翅膀就能飞翔的梦想从未实现。
words.en: If you describe something as chimerical, you mean that it is imagined or hoped for but unlikely to be real or practical.

words.ex: The child told a fanciful story about flying dragons.
words.ex_cn: 孩子讲了一个关于会飞的龙的富于幻想的故事。
words.en: If you describe an idea as fanciful, you mean that it is imaginative rather than reasonable or practical.

words.tr: adj. 可想象的；可能的；可想到的
words.ex: That was the worst thing imaginable.
words.ex_cn: 那是所能想象到的最糟糕的事情。
words.en: If something is imaginable, you are able to imagine it or believe that it could exist or happen.

words.ex: Children have a strong imagination.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们有很强的想象力。
words.en: The ability to form pictures or ideas in your mind of things that are new and exciting, or not real.

words.ex: The dragon is an imaginary creature.
words.ex_cn: 龙是一种想象中的生物。
words.en: An imaginary person, place, or thing is one that does not exist or is not real, but that people think about or talk about.

words.ex: The child gave an imaginative story about flying cats.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子讲了一个关于会飞的猫的富有想象力的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone or their ideas as imaginative, you are praising them because they are easily able to think of or create new or exciting things.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏想象力的；无趣的
words.ex: He gave an unimaginative answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个缺乏创意的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as unimaginative, you are criticizing them because they do not think of new or interesting ideas or things.

words.tr: adj. 推测的；推理的；思索的；投机的
words.ex: He made a speculative guess about the weather.
words.ex_cn: 他对天气做了一个推测性的猜测。
words.en: Based on conjecture rather than knowledge; involving a high risk of loss.

words.ex: His guess about the winner was just speculation.
words.ex_cn: 他对获胜者的猜测只是推测。
words.en: The act of forming opinions about what has happened or what might happen without knowing all the facts.

words.tr: adj. 凭推测的；凭猜测的
words.ex: His conjectural answer was not proven true.
words.ex_cn: 他的推测性答案没有被证明是正确的。
words.en: Based on or involving conjecture; speculative.

words.ex: His conjecture was that the missing key was in the drawer.
words.ex_cn: 他猜测丢失的钥匙在抽屉里。
words.en: A conjecture is a conclusion that is based on information that is not certain or complete.

words.ex: His opinion is subjective and not based on facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点是主观的，不是基于事实的。
words.en: Based on or influenced by personal feelings, tastes, or opinions.

words.ex: His answer shows subjectivity.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答体现了主观性。
words.en: Subjectivity refers to the influence of personal beliefs, feelings, or opinions on one's perception or interpretation of events or facts.

words.tr: n. 假定；推定；冒昧；放肆
words.ex: His presumption that he would win surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他以为自己会赢的这种假设让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A presumption is something that is thought to be true because it is likely, although there is no proof.

words.tr:
adj. 抽象的；非具体的；
n. 摘要；概要；抽象派艺术作品；
words.ex: The painting shows an abstract shape.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画展示了一个抽象的形状。
words.en: An abstract idea or way of thinking is based on general ideas rather than on real things and events.

words.tr: n. 出神；心不在焉；抽象
words.ex: He sat by the window in abstraction, staring at the clouds.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边出神，凝视着云朵。
words.en: An abstraction is a general idea rather than one that is based on a specific real thing or event.

words.tr: adj. 未经证实的；未确证的
words.ex: The report is still unconfirmed by the authorities.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告尚未得到官方证实。
words.en: Not confirmed or verified.

words.ex: I envisage a world without war.
words.ex_cn: 我设想一个没有战争的世界。
words.en: If you envisage something, you imagine that it is true, real, or likely to happen.

words.tr: n. 必然的结果（或结论）；推论
words.ex: The theorem leads to a simple corollary.
words.ex_cn: 这个定理引出了一个简单的推论。
words.en: A corollary is a statement that follows on from another statement, and that is usually easily understood or proved.

words.tr: n. 事先形成的看法；先入之见；成见
words.ex: He had a preconception that all teachers are strict.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个先入为主的观念，认为所有老师都很严格。
words.en: An idea or opinion that is formed before you have enough information or experience, or a bias that prevents objective consideration of an issue.

words.ex: He had a misconception that the earth is flat.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个错误认识，认为地球是平的。
words.en: A misconception is an idea that is not correct because it is based on a misunderstanding or a wrong belief.

words.ex: The teacher gave an unjustified grade.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个不公正的分数。
words.en: If you describe a belief or action as unjustified, you think that there is no good reason for having it or doing it.

words.ex: He gave a justification for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他为迟到提供了一个正当的理由。
words.en: A justification for something is an acceptable reason or explanation for it.

words.tr: adv. 言之有理地；无可非议地
words.ex: He justifiably won the award for his hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他因努力工作而理所当然地赢得了奖项。
words.en: For actions or beliefs that are justifiably held or done, there are good reasons that support them.

words.tr: adj. 难以捍卫的；站不住脚的；不堪一击的
words.ex: His excuse was untenable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口站不住脚。
words.en: If an argument, theory, or position is untenable, it cannot be defended or supported against criticism.

words.ex: His fear is unfounded.
words.ex_cn: 他的恐惧是没有根据的。
words.en: If you describe a rumour, belief, or feeling as unfounded, you mean that it is wrong because it is not based on facts or evidence.

words.ex: His claim is baseless.
words.ex_cn: 他的说法没有根据。
words.en: If you describe an accusation, rumor, or report as baseless, you mean that it is not true and is not based on facts.

words.tr: adj. 无故的；无必要的；无偿的；免费的
words.ex: He made a gratuitous comment about her clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的衣服做了毫无必要的评论。
words.en: If you describe something as gratuitous, you mean that it is unnecessary, and often harmful or upsetting.

words.tr: adj. 不合理的；没有根据的；无端的
words.ex: The teacher gave an unwarranted warning.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个没有理由的警告。
words.en: If you describe something as unwarranted, you are critical of it because there is no need or reason for it.

chapters.name: 偏见/倾向/爱好/恭维/赞美/拍马屁/支持/同意

words.ex: The teacher showed a bias for students who arrived early.
words.ex_cn: 老师对早到的学生有偏爱。
words.en: If someone is biased, they prefer one group of people to another, and behave unfairly as a result.

words.ex: He has a predilection for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: If you have a predilection for something, you have a strong liking for it.

words.tr:
adj. 偏袒的；党派性的
n. 强烈支持者；党羽；游击队员
words.ex: He gave a partisan answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了偏袒的回答。
words.en: A partisan is a strong supporter of a party, cause, or person. It can also refer to a member of an armed group formed to fight secretly against an occupying force.

words.ex: He is a non-partisan judge who treats everyone fairly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位不偏不倚的法官，公平对待每个人。
words.en: Not biased or partisan, especially towards any particular political group.

words.ex: He avoided partisanship in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中避免了党派偏见。
words.en: The state or quality of being partisan, especially in the sense of strong, sometimes blind, allegiance to a particular party, faction, cause, or person.

words.ex: He has a preference for tea over coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他更喜欢茶而不是咖啡。
words.en: A preference is a greater liking for one alternative over another or others.

words.ex: He has a proclivity for solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有解决数学问题的倾向。
words.en: A proclivity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way or to like a particular thing.

words.ex: He has prejudice against people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人有偏见。
words.en: Prejudice is an unreasonable dislike of a particular group of people or things, or a preference for one group of people or things over another.

words.ex: The crowd applauded after the performance.
words.ex_cn: 演出结束后，观众鼓掌了。
words.en: To applaud means to show approval or praise by clapping the hands.

words.tr: adj. 谄媚的；拍马的；说奉承话的
words.ex: He gave a sycophantic smile to please his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他露出谄媚的微笑来讨好老板。
words.en: If you describe someone as sycophantic, you disapprove of them because they flatter people who are more important and powerful than themselves in order to gain an advantage.

words.tr: n. 谄媚；奉承；追随；拍马屁
words.ex: He used sycophancy to please his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他用阿谀奉承来讨好老板。
words.en: Sycophancy is the behavior of trying to please someone in authority by praising them or agreeing with everything they say or do, often in a way that is not sincere.

words.ex: The teacher gave an encomium to the student for her perfect score.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生得了满分而给予了赞美。
words.en: A formal expression of praise; a eulogy.

words.tr:
v. 称赞；恭维
n. 称赞；恭维
words.ex: He gave her a compliment on her dress.
words.ex_cn: 他夸了她的裙子。
words.en: A compliment is a polite expression of praise or admiration.

words.ex: The hotel gave us complimentary breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 酒店免费赠送了我们早餐。
words.en: If something is complimentary, it is given or done free of charge. It can also mean expressing a compliment; praising or approving.

words.ex: He extols the beauty of nature every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天赞美大自然的美。
words.en: If you extol something or someone, you praise them enthusiastically.

words.ex: He tries to ingratiate himself with his boss by bringing coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上送咖啡给老板，试图讨好他。
words.en: If someone tries to ingratiate themselves with you, they do things to try and make you like them.

words.ex: The teacher lauded the student for her hard work.
words.ex_cn: 老师称赞了这名学生努力学习。
words.en: If people laud someone, they praise and admire them.

words.tr: adj. 假情假义的；油腔滑调的
words.ex: His unctuous manner made me uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他油腔滑调的态度让我感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone as unctuous, you are critical of them because they seem to be full of praise, kindness, or interest, but in a way that is not sincere.

words.ex: The actor received acclaim for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而受到赞扬。
words.en: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically and publicly.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.tr: adj. 奉承的；逢迎的；谄媚的
words.ex: He was obsequious to his boss to get a promotion.
words.ex_cn: 他为了得到晋升，对老板阿谀奉承。
words.en: If you describe someone as obsequious, you are criticizing them because they are too eager to help or agree with someone more important than them.

words.ex: They exalt their hero with cheers.
words.ex_cn: 他们用欢呼赞美他们的英雄。
words.en: To exalt someone or something means to praise them very highly.

words.ex: His work finally received the approbation of his peers.
words.ex_cn: 他的工作最终得到了同行的认可。
words.en: Official approval or agreement.

words.ex: He espouses simple ideas about justice.
words.ex_cn: 他拥护关于正义的简单理念。
words.en: If you espouse a particular policy, cause, or belief, you become very interested in it and give your support to it.

words.ex: He felt uncomfortable with the adulation from his fans.
words.ex_cn: 他对于粉丝们的盲目崇拜感到不舒服。
words.en: Excessive admiration or praise.

words.tr:
v. 支持；支撑；
n. 拥护；帮助；
words.ex: My friends support me when I feel sad.
words.ex_cn: 当我感到难过时，我的朋友们支持我。
words.en: If you support someone or their ideas or aims, you agree with them, and perhaps help them because you want them to succeed.

words.tr: adj. 承重力良好的，支撑性良好的
words.ex: The claim is well-supported by evidence.
words.ex_cn: 这一主张得到了充分的证据支持。
words.en: Having a lot of evidence or backing to prove or justify something.

words.ex: He is a supporter of the local team.
words.ex_cn: 他是当地球队的支持者。
words.en: A supporter is someone who supports a particular person, group, or cause.

words.ex: The coach endorses the new player.
words.ex_cn: 教练支持这位新球员。
words.en: If you endorse someone or something, you say publicly that you support or approve of them.

words.tr: n. 支持；认可；名人代言；违章驾驶记录
words.ex: He got an endorsement from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他得到了老板的支持。
words.en: An endorsement is a statement or action which shows that you support or approve of something or someone.

words.ex: The teacher commends her for working hard.
words.ex_cn: 老师表扬她学习努力。
words.en: If you commend someone or something, you praise them formally.

words.ex: The teacher gave me a recommendation for the scholarship.
words.ex_cn: 老师给我写了一封奖学金推荐信。
words.en: A suggestion or proposal as to the best course of action, especially one put forward by an authoritative body.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.tr:
n. 扶墙；拱壁
v. 支持
words.ex: The old wall needs a buttress to stay standing.
words.ex_cn: 这面旧墙需要一个支撑物来保持不倒。
words.en: A buttress is a structure built against or projecting from a wall which serves to support or reinforce the wall. As a verb, to buttress means to support or strengthen something.

words.ex: He tried to instigate a fight at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在聚会上挑起争斗。
words.en: If someone instigates an event or situation, they cause it to happen by their actions or behavior.

chapters.name: 斥责/批评/抨击/矛盾/不一致/不同意

words.ex: The public condemned the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 公众谴责了这位腐败的政客。
words.en: If you condemn something, you say that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: The teacher will critique the student's essay tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会对学生的作文发表评论。
words.en: A critique is a detailed analysis and assessment of something, especially a literary, philosophical, or political theory.

words.ex: He will impugn the witness's honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他将质疑证人的诚实性。
words.en: To impugn means to challenge as false or questionable; to cast doubt upon.

words.ex: He denied the aspersion on his character.
words.ex_cn: 他否认了对他人格的污蔑。
words.en: An aspersion is a remark or statement that criticizes someone or something and damages their reputation.

words.tr: n. 诋毁者；诽谤者；贬低者
words.ex: He ignored every detractor who criticized his idea.
words.ex_cn: 他无视了每一个批评他想法的人。
words.en: A detractor is someone who criticizes something or someone, often unfairly.

words.ex: The angry father lambasted the bully with his belt.
words.ex_cn: 愤怒的父亲用皮带痛打了那个欺凌者。
words.en: If you lambaste someone, you criticize them severely, usually in public.

words.tr: v. 公开指责；告发；揭发
words.ex: He denounces corruption in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中谴责腐败。
words.en: If you denounce a person or an action, you criticize them severely and publicly because you feel strongly that they are wrong or evil.

words.ex: He refuted the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据驳斥了这一说法。
words.en: To prove a statement or theory to be wrong or false; to deny the truth or accuracy of something.

words.tr:
v. 谴责；责难；指责
n. 谴责；责难；指责
words.ex: The teacher censured the student for cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师谴责了那个作弊的学生。
words.en: If you censure someone for something that they have done, you tell them that you strongly disapprove of it.

words.ex: The teacher reprehended the student for his disruptive behavior.
words.ex_cn: 老师因学生扰乱课堂的行为而责备他。
words.en: If you reprehend someone, you criticize them severely for their actions or behavior.

words.ex: The court will indict him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将对他提起盗窃指控。
words.en: If someone is indicted for a crime, they are officially charged with it.

words.ex: The prosecutor read the indictment in court.
words.ex_cn: 检察官在法庭上宣读了起诉状。
words.en: An indictment is a formal accusation that someone has committed a crime.

words.ex: He faced obloquy for speaking the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他因说出真相而遭受非议。
words.en: Obloquy is strong public criticism or verbal abuse.

words.ex: The scientist debunked the myth that sugar makes children hyper.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家揭穿了糖会使孩子多动的谬论。
words.en: If you debunk a widely held belief, you show that it is false. If you debunk something that is widely admired, you show that it is not as good as people think it is.

words.ex: He faced vituperation after lying to the team.
words.ex_cn: 他向团队撒谎后遭到了严厉责骂。
words.en: Vituperation is the act of using harsh, abusive language to criticize or blame someone.

words.tr:
v. 反驳；回嘴
n. 反驳；顶嘴
words.ex: He gave a quick retort when she criticized him.
words.ex_cn: 当她批评他时，他迅速回了一句。
words.en: If you retort, you reply angrily to someone.

words.ex: Many people decry the use of plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 许多人公开反对使用塑料袋。
words.en: If you decry something, you criticize it as being wrong or harmful.

words.ex: The child excoriated his knee when he fell on the rough ground.
words.ex_cn: 孩子摔倒在粗糙的地面上，膝盖擦伤了。
words.en: To excoriate someone or something means to criticize them severely.

words.ex: The subtlety of her smile made everyone curious.
words.ex_cn: 她微笑的微妙之处让所有人都感到好奇。
words.en: The quality of being subtle, especially in a way that is difficult to notice or understand.

words.ex: The difference between the two colors is subtle.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色之间的区别很微妙。
words.en: Something that is subtle is not immediately obvious or noticeable, but is rather indirect or understated.

words.ex: She smiled subtly when she heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 她听到这个消息时微妙地笑了。
words.en: In a way that is so delicate or precise as to be difficult to analyze or describe.

words.ex: He contradicts what she said.
words.ex_cn: 他反驳了她的话。
words.en: If you contradict someone, you say that what they have just said is wrong, or you suggest that it is wrong by saying something different.

words.ex: His words were contradictory.
words.ex_cn: 他的话是矛盾的。
words.en: If two or more facts, ideas, or statements are contradictory, they state or imply that opposite things are true.

words.ex: His smile belieed his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑掩饰了他真实的情感。
words.en: If one thing belies another, it hides the true situation and so creates a false idea or image of someone or something.

words.ex: It's ironic that the fire station burned down.
words.ex_cn: 消防站着火了，这真是讽刺。
words.en: If you say that it is ironic that something happens, you mean that it is odd or amusing because it involves a contrast or is the opposite of what you would expect.

words.ex: He bought a raincoat, and it rained ironically the next day.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一件雨衣，讽刺的是，第二天就下雨了。
words.en: In a way that is contrary to what is expected and is therefore amusing or strange.

words.ex: He felt ambivalent about accepting the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对接受这份工作邀约感到矛盾。
words.en: If you say that someone is ambivalent about something, you mean that they have mixed feelings about it or are unsure whether they want it or not.

words.ex: The speed is inversely proportional to the time.
words.ex_cn: 速度与时间成反比。
words.en: In an inverse manner; in the opposite order, direction, or effect.

words.ex: It is paradoxical that he sleeps all day but stays awake at night.
words.ex_cn: 他白天睡觉却晚上醒着，这很矛盾。
words.en: If something is paradoxical, it involves two facts or qualities which seem to contradict each other.

words.tr: adv. 自相矛盾地；矛盾地；
words.ex: Paradoxically, he is very quiet, but he speaks the most in class.
words.ex_cn: 自相矛盾地，他非常安静，但在课堂上却说得最多。
words.en: In a way that is contrary to expectations or seemingly contradictory.

words.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.
words.ex_cn: 这两份报告之间有差异。
words.en: A discrepancy is a difference between two or more things that should be the same.

words.ex: The survey has a dichotomous answer: yes or no.
words.ex_cn: 这个调查有一个二分的答案：是或否。
words.en: Divided or dividing into two parts or classifications.

words.tr: adj. 分歧的；发散的；趋异的；
words.ex: The two friends had divergent opinions about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这两个朋友对这部电影的看法不同。
words.en: If two things diverge, they are different from each other, or they become different from each other.

words.ex: The two roads diverge after the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 两条路在桥后分岔。
words.en: If one thing diverges from another similar thing, the first thing becomes different from the second or develops differently from it. You can also say that two things diverge.

words.ex: The issue polarized the community into two opposing groups.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题使社区分裂成了两个对立的群体。
words.en: To polarize means to cause something, especially a group or an issue, to divide into two sharply contrasting groups or sets of opinions or beliefs.

words.ex: The pink hat on the man looked like an incongruity.
words.ex_cn: 男人头上的粉红色帽子显得很不协调。
words.en: The state of being incongruous; incompatibility.

words.ex: He is a maverick who always does things his own way.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是按自己方式做事的独行其是者。
words.en: If you describe someone as a maverick, you mean that they are unconventional and independent, and do not think or behave in the same way as other people.

words.tr:
adj. 持不同意见的
n. 意见不同的人；持不同政见者
words.ex: The dissident spoke out against the government.
words.ex_cn: 这位持不同政见者公开反对政府。
words.en: A dissident is a person who opposes official policy, especially that of an authoritarian state.

chapters.name: 多产/丰富/巨大/过剩/浪费

words.ex: There is an abundance of food at the party.
words.ex_cn: 聚会上食物非常丰富。
words.en: A very large quantity of something.

words.ex: The forest has abundant water and trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林水源和树木都很丰富。
words.en: If something is abundant, there is a lot of it or it is very common.

words.ex: The palace showed opulence with golden walls and silk curtains.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿以金墙和丝绸窗帘展现了富裕。
words.en: Opulence is great wealth or luxuriousness.

words.ex: The fecundity of the rabbits helped them grow quickly.
words.ex_cn: 兔子的高繁殖力帮助它们迅速增长。
words.en: The ability to produce an abundance of offspring or new growth; fertility.

words.ex: The new job enriched his life.
words.ex_cn: 这份新工作使他的生活富裕起来。
words.en: To enrich something means to improve its quality, often by adding something to it.

words.ex: Fish abound in this river.
words.ex_cn: 这条河里鱼很多。
words.en: If things abound, or if a place abounds with things, there are very large numbers of them.

words.tr: n. 大量；丰富；慷慨；浪费
words.ex: There is a profusion of flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花园里有大量花朵。
words.en: If there is a profusion of something or it occurs in profusion, there is a very large quantity or variety of it.

words.ex: The elephant is gigantic compared to a dog.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象相比狗来说是巨大的。
words.en: If you describe something as gigantic, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: The elephant was gargantuan compared to the dog.
words.ex_cn: 这只大象比起狗来说巨大无比。
words.en: If you say that something is gargantuan, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.tr: adj. 贪吃的；贪婪的；如饥似渴的
words.ex: He is a voracious eater who finishes all the food on his plate.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个贪吃的人，总会把盘子里的所有食物吃完。
words.en: If you describe a person or their appetite for something as voracious, you mean that they want a lot of something.

words.tr: adj. 慷慨的；丰富的；充足的
words.ex: She gave a bountiful donation to the orphanage.
words.ex_cn: 她向孤儿院慷慨地捐了一笔钱。
words.en: Something that is bountiful is large in quantity or number and is freely given.

words.ex: He wrote copious notes during the lecture.
words.ex_cn: 他在讲座期间写了大量的笔记。
words.en: Something that is copious exists in large amounts.

words.tr:
v. 使饮食过度；吃得过量；过分沉溺
n. 过量；过度
words.ex: He surfeited on pizza and felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多披萨，感到恶心。
words.en: An excessive amount of something, especially food or drink.

words.ex: The extra chair is redundant because we have enough seats.
words.ex_cn: 这把额外的椅子是多余的，因为我们已经有足够的座位了。
words.en: If you are made redundant, your employer tells you to leave because your job is no longer necessary or because there is no more work for you.

words.ex: The company announced redundancy due to low profits.
words.ex_cn: 公司因利润低下宣布裁员。
words.en: Redundancy refers to the state of being not or no longer needed or useful; the inclusion of extra components which are not strictly necessary to functioning, in case of failure in other components; or the dismissal of employees from work for being no longer necessary.

words.ex: He squandered all his money on games.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的钱都浪费在游戏上了。
words.en: If you squander money, resources, or opportunities, you waste them in a foolish or careless way.

words.ex: There is a plethora of choices on the menu.
words.ex_cn: 菜单上有太多的选择。
words.en: A plethora of something is a very large quantity of it, especially an amount that is greater than you need, want, or can cope with.

words.ex: The extra words are superfluous.
words.ex_cn: 这些额外的词是多余的。
words.en: Something that is superfluous is unnecessary or no longer needed.

words.ex: The farm has a surplus of apples this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年农场苹果过剩。
words.en: A surplus is an amount of something that is extra or more than what is needed.

chapters.name: 不重要/微不足道/小的/脆弱/无用/缺点/贫瘠/匮乏

words.tr: adj. 非物质的；无形的；不重要的
words.ex: The color is immaterial to the function.
words.ex_cn: 颜色对功能无关紧要。
words.en: If you say that something is immaterial, you mean that it is not important or not relevant.

words.tr: v. 成为现实；成有形；实现；现身
words.ex: The dream did not materialize.
words.ex_cn: 这个梦想没有实现。
words.en: To materialize means to become actual fact; to happen or to appear in physical form.

words.ex: He cares only about money and things, showing strong materialism.
words.ex_cn: 他只关心金钱和物质，表现出强烈的实利主义。
words.en: Materialism is the belief that only physical matter exists, and that everything, including thought, feeling, mind, and will, can be explained in terms of matter and physical phenomena.

words.tr: adj. 无关紧要的；不重要的；
words.ex: The mistake was insignificant and didn't affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误无关紧要，没有影响结果。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as insignificant, you mean that they are small or unimportant, and therefore not worth considering seriously.

words.tr: adj. 重大的；重要的；影响明显的；
words.ex: This discovery is a significant step forward.
words.ex_cn: 这一发现是一个重大的进步。
words.en: Something that is significant is important or large enough to be noticed or to have an effect.

words.ex: The mistake was trivial and didn't affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误不重要，没有影响结果。
words.en: If you describe something as trivial, you mean that it is not important or significant, or is not worth serious consideration.

words.tr: n. 琐碎；琐事；微不足道
words.ex: He ignored the triviality of the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了这个错误的微不足道。
words.en: The quality or state of being trivial or of little importance.

words.ex: The water supply is insufficient for the whole village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对整个村庄来说是不充分的。
words.en: If something is insufficient, it is not enough for a particular purpose.

words.ex: We have sufficient food for the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们有足够的食物用于这次旅行。
words.en: If something is sufficient for a particular purpose, there is enough of it for the purpose.

words.ex: He answered the questions insufficiently.
words.ex_cn: 他回答问题不够充分。
words.en: In a manner that is not enough or adequate.

words.tr: adj. 不重要的；无关紧要的
words.ex: His comment was inconsequential to the decision.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论对决定无关紧要。
words.en: If you describe something as inconsequential, you mean that it is not important.

words.ex: His opinion is subordinate to the manager's.
words.ex_cn: 他的意见比经理的次要。
words.en: If someone is your subordinate, they have a less important position than you in the organization that you both work for.

words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.ex: He had a meager meal after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后吃了一顿很少的饭。
words.en: If you describe an amount or quantity of something as meager, you are critical of it because it is very small or not enough.

words.ex: The keyboard is a peripheral device.
words.ex_cn: 键盘是一个外围设备。
words.en: A peripheral activity or issue is one that is not very important compared with other activities or issues.

words.tr:
adj. 微不足道的；无关紧要的
v. 闹着玩；玩弄；“trifle”的现在分词
words.ex: He ignored the trifling mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了这个微不足道的错误。
words.en: If you describe something as trifling, you mean that it is unimportant or insignificant.

words.tr: adj. 边缘的；页边的；微不足道的；不重要的
words.ex: The village is on the marginal area of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于城市的边缘地区。
words.en: If you describe something as marginal, you mean that it is small or not very important.

words.ex: He gave a paltry amount of money to charity.
words.ex_cn: 他捐给慈善机构的钱微不足道。
words.en: If you describe an amount of money as paltry, you mean that it is very small.

words.tr: adj. 不讨人喜欢的；不吸引人的；
words.ex: He has an unprepossessing appearance, but he is very kind.
words.ex_cn: 他外表不讨人喜欢，但他非常善良。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unprepossessing, you mean that they look rather plain or ordinary, and not at all impressive or attractive.

words.ex: The minuscule dot was hard to see with the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 那个极小的点用肉眼很难看到。
words.en: If you describe something as minuscule, you mean that it is very small.

words.tr:
adj. 极小的；特小的；微小的
n. 小的人；指小词缀；爱称
words.ex: The diminutive cat sat on the small mat.
words.ex_cn: 那只小巧的猫坐在小垫子上。
words.en: A diminutive person or object is very small.

words.tr: adj. 最低限度的；极少的；最小的；
words.ex: He made minimal changes to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对计划做了最低限度的修改。
words.en: Something that is minimal is very small in quantity, value, or degree.

words.ex: The plan was flawed and didn't work.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划有缺陷，没有成功。
words.en: If something is flawed, it is not perfect or it has mistakes.

words.tr: adj. 无瑕疵的；无缺点的；
words.ex: Her performance was flawless.
words.ex_cn: 她的表演毫无瑕疵。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is flawless, you mean that they are extremely good and that there are no faults or problems with them.

words.ex: It was futile to try to fix the broken clock.
words.ex_cn: 试图修理坏掉的钟表是徒劳的。
words.en: If you say that something is futile, you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.

words.ex: He saw the futility of trying to fix it himself.
words.ex_cn: 他看到了自己试图修理它的无用。
words.en: The quality of being futile or ineffective.

words.ex: Their agreement was tenuous and easily broken.
words.ex_cn: 他们的协议很脆弱，容易破裂。
words.en: If you describe something such as a connection, a reason, or someone's position as tenuous, you mean that it is very uncertain or weak.

words.tr: adj. 虚弱的；衰弱的；无力的；
words.ex: The old man gave a feeble smile.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人露出虚弱的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as feeble, you mean that they are weak.

words.ex: The illness had enfeebled her to the point of immobility.
words.ex_cn: 疾病使她衰弱到几乎不能动弹的地步。
words.en: To make someone or something very weak.

words.ex: The slow internet frustrates me.
words.ex_cn: 慢速的网络让我感到沮丧。
words.en: If something frustrates you, it upsets or angers you because you are unable to deal with the problems it creates.

words.tr: adv. 令人泄气地；使人沮丧地（frustrate 的副词形式）
words.ex: The math problem was frustratingly hard.
words.ex_cn: 这道数学题难得让人沮丧。
words.en: In a manner that causes feelings of frustration.

words.tr: v. 使变质；损害；使失效
words.ex: The poison vitiated the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒物使水源变质。
words.en: To vitiate something means to impair or reduce the quality, value, or effectiveness of it.

words.ex: There is a paucity of water in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很少。
words.en: If you say that there is a paucity of something, you mean that there is not enough of it.

words.ex: His speech was full of vacuousness.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了空洞。
words.en: The quality of being vacuous; emptiness or lack of intelligence.

words.tr: adj. 空虚的；茫然的；空洞的
words.ex: His vacuous smile made no sense.
words.ex_cn: 他空洞的微笑毫无意义。
words.en: If you describe someone's mind or smile as vacuous, you are critical of them because they lack intelligence, understanding, or seriousness.

words.ex: Children are vulnerable to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If someone or something is vulnerable, they are weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

words.tr: adj. 无能的；软弱的；不中用的
words.ex: His feckless attempts to solve the problem only made it worse.
words.ex_cn: 他试图解决问题的无效尝试反而使问题变得更糟。
words.en: If you describe someone as feckless, you mean that they lack determination or strength, and are unable to do anything properly.

words.tr:
n. 污染；腐坏；玷污
v. 污染；使腐坏；玷污
words.ex: The water has a taint from the factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这种水因工厂废料而受到污染。
words.en: If something is tainted, it is affected by something bad or undesirable.

words.tr:
n. 瑕疵；污点；缺点
v. 玷污；损害
words.ex: The apple has a small blemish on its skin.
words.ex_cn: 这个苹果的表皮上有一个小瑕疵。
words.en: A blemish is a small mark or flaw that spoils the appearance of something.

words.ex: His efforts were bootless.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力是徒劳的。
words.en: If you describe something as bootless, you mean that it is useless or does not achieve anything.

words.tr: n. 脆弱性；脆性；易碎性
words.ex: The fragility of the glass made it easy to break.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃的易碎性让它很容易破碎。
words.en: The quality of being easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: There is a dearth of clean water in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄缺乏干净的水。
words.en: A dearth of something is a lack or scarcity of it.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏的；不足的；稀有的；
words.ex: Water is scarce in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很缺乏。
words.en: If something is scarce, there is not enough of it.

words.ex: He scarcely ate anything at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚餐几乎没吃任何东西。
words.en: You use scarcely to emphasize that something is only just true or only just the case.

words.ex: The scarcity of water caused problems in the village.
words.ex_cn: 水的缺乏给村庄带来了问题。
words.en: A scarcity of something is a situation in which there is not enough of it.

words.ex: The food supply was inadequate for the number of people.
words.ex_cn: 食物供应对人数来说是不充分的。
words.en: If something is inadequate, there is not enough of it or it is not good enough.

words.ex: The inadequacy of food caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 食物的不足导致了许多问题。
words.en: If there is an inadequacy in something, it is not enough or not good enough.

words.ex: He lives in penury after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后生活贫困。
words.en: Penury is the state of being extremely poor.

words.ex: He lived in indigence after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后生活贫困。
words.en: Indigence is the state of being extremely poor.

words.ex: His knowledge of history is superficial.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史的了解是表面的。
words.en: If you describe someone as superficial, you disapprove of them because they do not think deeply, and have little understanding of anything serious or important.

words.ex: He looked superficially at the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他只是表面地看了看这个问题。
words.en: In a way that appears to be true or real only until examined more closely.

words.ex: He gave a concise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了简明的回答。
words.en: Something that is concise says everything that is necessary without using any unnecessary words.

words.ex: He wrote with concision to save time.
words.ex_cn: 他简洁地写作以节省时间。
words.en: Concision refers to the quality of being concise, that is, expressing much in few words.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；肤浅的；易做到的
words.ex: He gave a facile answer to the hard question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个难题给出了一个简单的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's arguments or suggestions as facile, you are criticizing them because their ideas are too simple and indicate a lack of careful, intelligent thinking.

words.tr: adj. 言简意赅的；简明扼要的；凝练的
words.ex: He gave a laconic reply: 'Yes.'
words.ex_cn: 他简短地回答：‘是的。’
words.en: If you describe someone as laconic, you mean that they use very few words to say something, so that they seem casual or unfriendly.

words.ex: The brevity of his speech surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他讲话的短暂让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Brevity is the use of only a few words to say something, or the quality of being short in time.

words.ex: He gave a succinct answer.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个简洁的回答。
words.en: Something that is succinct expresses facts or ideas clearly and in few words.

words.ex: The report's succinctness made it easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 报告的简洁性使其易于理解。
words.en: The quality of being expressed clearly and in a few words.

words.ex: He ignored the frivolous complaint and focused on the real issue.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了这个无关紧要的投诉，专注于真正的问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as frivolous, you mean they behave in a silly or light-hearted way, rather than being serious and sensible.

words.ex: The pond is shallow, so you can see the bottom.
words.ex_cn: 这个池塘很浅，所以你能看到底部。
words.en: If something is shallow, it does not extend far down from the top surface.

words.tr: adj. 令人信服的； v. “compel”的现在分词；
words.ex: His story was compelling and made everyone listen.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事令人信服，让所有人都认真聆听。
words.en: A compelling argument or reason is one that makes you believe it or accept it because it is so strong.

words.ex: The momentous decision changed his life.
words.ex_cn: 这个重要的决定改变了他的一生。
words.en: If you refer to a decision, event, or change as momentous, you mean that it is very important, often because of the effects that it will have in the future.

words.tr: adj. 极好的；令人震惊的； v. “stun”的现在分词；
words.ex: She wore a stunning dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件极好的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Extremely impressive or attractive.

words.ex: The loud noise stunned him.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让他震惊了。
words.en: To stun someone means to shock or surprise them very much.

words.ex: The situation required an exigent response.
words.ex_cn: 这种情况需要紧急应对。
words.en: Requiring immediate action or attention; urgent.

words.ex: There is an exigency, so we must act now.
words.ex_cn: 情况紧急，我们必须立刻行动。
words.en: An exigency is a pressing or urgent situation or need that requires immediate action or attention.

words.ex: The enormity of the crime shocked the whole city.
words.ex_cn: 这桩罪行的极恶震惊了整个城市。
words.en: If you refer to the enormity of something that you consider to be a problem or difficulty, you are referring to its very great size, extent, or seriousness.

words.ex: The magnitude of this decision will affect everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定的重要性会影响每个人。
words.en: Magnitude refers to the great size or extent of something, or the importance of something.

words.ex: The salient point in the report is the cost increase.
words.ex_cn: 报告中最显著的要点是成本上升。
words.en: The most noticeable or important.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；决定性的；
words.ex: It is crucial to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水至关重要。
words.en: If you describe something as crucial, you mean it is extremely important.

words.ex: The profundity of his insights left the audience speechless.
words.ex_cn: 他见解的深刻让观众无言以对。
words.en: Profundity refers to the quality of being profound, which means having deep insight or understanding, or being very intense or extreme.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.tr: adj. 紧迫的； v. 按；“press”的现在分词；
words.ex: The pressing issue is finding clean water.
words.ex_cn: 紧迫的问题是找到干净的水。
words.en: If something is pressing, it needs to be dealt with immediately because it is important or urgent.

words.tr: n. 炸弹；爆炸性事件；令人吃惊的事
words.ex: The soldier dropped a bombshell on the enemy base.
words.ex_cn: 士兵向敌方基地扔了一颗炸弹。
words.en: A bombshell is a sudden and surprising piece of news or event that has a big effect on people.

words.tr: adj. 必需的；基本的；本质的；
words.ex: Water is essential for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必需的。
words.en: Something that is essential is extremely important or absolutely necessary to a particular subject, situation, or activity.

words.tr: adv. 本质上；基本上；根本上；
words.ex: He is essentially a kind person.
words.ex_cn: 他本质上是个善良的人。
words.en: You use essentially to indicate that what you are saying is mainly true, although there may be some exceptions or qualifications.

words.tr: adj. 无关紧要的; n. 无关紧要的东西
words.ex: The color is inessential to the function.
words.ex_cn: 颜色对于功能来说是不必要的。
words.en: If you describe something as inessential, you mean that it is not absolutely necessary.

words.ex: Water is indispensable for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必不可少的。
words.en: Absolutely necessary or essential.

words.tr: adj. 未充分发展的；初步的；基本的；
words.ex: His knowledge of math is rudimentary.
words.ex_cn: 他对数学的了解是初步的。
words.en: Rudimentary means relating to the basic or simplest aspects of a subject, or being in the earliest stages of development.

words.tr: adj. 必需的；必备的；必不可少的；
words.ex: A passport is a requisite for international travel.
words.ex_cn: 护照是国际旅行所必需的。
words.en: Something that is necessary for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The report gave a sketchy description of the event.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告对事件的描述不完备。
words.en: If something is sketchy, it is incomplete or not detailed, and possibly unreliable.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；潜在的； v. “underlie”的现在分词；
words.ex: The underlying cause of the problem is poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题的根本原因是贫困。
words.en: An underlying thing is the thing that is the most important or basic, although it is not easily noticed or stated directly.

words.ex: He felt nostalgia when he saw his old toy.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到自己的旧玩具时，感到怀旧。
words.en: A sentimental longing or wistful affection for the past, typically for a period or place with happy personal associations.

words.tr: adj. 有...气味的；令人想起...的
words.ex: The garden is redolent of roses.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园弥漫着玫瑰的香气。
words.en: Strongly reminiscent or suggestive of something.

words.tr: adj. 暗示的；影射的；性暗示的
words.ex: His look was suggestive of sadness.
words.ex_cn: 他的眼神暗示着悲伤。
words.en: Something that is suggestive of something else is likely to make you think about or remember it.

words.ex: They plant trees to commemorate the fallen soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 他们种树以纪念阵亡的士兵。
words.en: To commemorate an important event or person means to remember them by means of a special action, ceremony, or specially created object.

words.tr: n. 死记硬背；机械的做法；生搬硬套
words.ex: He learned the poem by rote.
words.ex_cn: 他通过死记硬背学会了这首诗。
words.en: Rote is the process of learning something by repeating it many times without thinking about it or understanding it.

words.ex: He dismissed her advice and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会她的建议，走开了。
words.en: If you dismiss someone, you send them away or allow them to leave.

words.ex: His dismissal made him very sad.
words.ex_cn: 他的被解雇让他非常难过。
words.en: The act of officially removing someone from their job, or the act of sending someone away or allowing them to leave.

words.ex: He ignored the warning sign.
words.ex_cn: 他忽视了警告标志。
words.en: If you ignore someone or something, you pay no attention to them.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；
v. 不全信；不重视；
words.ex: The store gave a 20% discount on all shoes.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有鞋子提供了20%的折扣。
words.en: A reduction in the usual price of something, or the act of reducing the price.

words.tr: v. 轻描淡写；打折扣地说；少说
words.ex: He understated the cost of the repair.
words.ex_cn: 他轻描淡写了维修的费用。
words.en: If you understate something, you describe it in a way that suggests it is less important or serious than it really is.

words.tr: n. 保守的说法；不充分的叙述；掩饰；低调
words.ex: His description of the accident was an understatement.
words.ex_cn: 他对事故的描述是轻描淡写的。
words.en: If you say that a statement is an understatement, you mean that it does not fully express the extent to which something is true.

words.ex: His oversight caused the project to fail.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致项目失败。
words.en: An oversight is a mistake that is made by not noticing something or by forgetting to do something.

words.tr: adj. 没注意到的；未觉察的；忘却的；
words.ex: He was oblivious to the noise around him.
words.ex_cn: 他对周围的噪音毫无察觉。
words.en: If you are oblivious to something or oblivious of it, you are not aware of it.

words.ex: He overlooked the mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了报告中的错误。
words.en: If you overlook a fact or problem, you do not notice it, or do not realize how important it is.

words.ex: He tries to downplay his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他试图淡化自己的错误。
words.en: To downplay something means to make it seem less important or less bad than it really is.

words.tr: adj. 渴望的；含情脉脉的；渐渐衰弱的
words.ex: The plant is languishing in the dark corner.
words.ex_cn: 这株植物在昏暗的角落里枯萎着。
words.en: If someone is languishing, they are in a situation where they are not being successful or are not being looked after properly.

words.ex: He inadvertently dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他非故意地打翻了玻璃杯。
words.en: If you do something inadvertently, you do it without realizing it, or by accident.

words.ex: He tried to extenuate his mistake by saying he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他试图以自己累了为由减轻自己的错误。
words.en: To lessen or to try to lessen the seriousness or extent of (guilt or an offense) by providing partial excuses.

words.ex: He underrates his own talent.
words.ex_cn: 他低估了自己的才华。
words.en: To underrate something or someone means to fail to recognize their true value or importance.

words.ex: The mirror deflects the light to the wall.
words.ex_cn: 镜子把光线反射到墙上。
words.en: If you deflect something such as criticism or attention, you act in a way that prevents it from being directed towards you or affecting you.

words.tr: adv. 不知不觉；无意地；糊里糊涂地；
words.ex: He unwittingly revealed the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他不知不觉地泄露了秘密。
words.en: Without being aware of what is happening or being done.

words.tr:
v. 丢弃；放弃；扔掉
n. 投弃；抛弃；投弃货物
words.ex: The pilot had to jettison extra fuel to land safely.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员不得不抛掉多余的燃料以安全着陆。
words.en: To jettison something means to throw it away or get rid of it, usually because it is not wanted or needed.

words.ex: His neglect of the project caused delays.
words.ex_cn: 他对项目的疏忽导致了延误。
words.en: If you neglect someone or something, you fail to give them the attention or care that they need.

words.ex: He will forgo dessert to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 为了保持健康，他将放弃甜点。
words.en: If you forgo something, you decide to do without it, even though you would like it.

words.tr: n. 否认；自我克制；放弃
words.ex: His abnegation of the truth made everyone sad.
words.ex_cn: 他对真相的否认让每个人都感到难过。
words.en: The act of renouncing or rejecting something, often used in the context of self-denial or the refusal of certain rights or privileges.

words.tr: v. 撤回声明；放弃信仰
words.ex: He recanted his statement after seeing the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他在看到证据后撤回了他的话。
words.en: If you recant, you say publicly that you no longer hold a set of beliefs that you had in the past.

words.tr: v. 使无效；抵消；废除；取消
words.ex: The judge will nullify the contract.
words.ex_cn: 法官将宣布该合同无效。
words.en: To nullify something means to make it have no effect or value.

words.ex: He decided to discard his old habits.
words.ex_cn: 他决定抛开旧习惯。
words.en: To discard something means to get rid of it because you no longer want it or need it.

words.ex: He abandoned his car in the snow.
words.ex_cn: 他把车抛弃在雪地里。
words.en: If you abandon a place, thing, or person, you leave the place, thing, or person permanently or for a long time, especially when you should not do so.

words.ex: He had to relinquish his seat to an old man.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不把座位让给一位老人。
words.en: If you relinquish something, such as power or control, you give it up, often unwillingly.

words.tr: v. 割让（领土）；放弃（权力）
words.ex: He will cede his land to the government.
words.ex_cn: 他将把土地让给政府。
words.en: To give up control or possession of something, especially land or territory, often as a result of war or negotiation.

words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.tr: v. 强烈吸引住；使着迷；
words.ex: The magic show fascinated the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演深深吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If something fascinates you, it interests and delights you so much that your thoughts tend to concentrate on it.

words.ex: The magic show captivates the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If you are captivated by someone or something, you find them fascinating and attractive.

words.tr: adj. 诱导的；归纳的；感应的
words.ex: The scientist used inductive reasoning to form a hypothesis.
words.ex_cn: 科学家使用归纳推理来形成一个假设。
words.en: Inductive reasoning involves making broad generalizations from specific observations.

words.ex: The allure of money made him take the risky job.
words.ex_cn: 金钱的诱惑让他接受了这份高风险的工作。
words.en: The quality of being powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating.

words.tr:
adj. 撩拨人的；让人非常着急的
v. （以可望而不可即之物）逗引；使干着急；“tantalize”的现在分词
words.ex: The smell of fresh bread was tantalizing.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的香味令人垂涎。
words.en: If you describe something as tantalizing, you mean that it is very attractive, interesting, or desirable.
