words.ex: He resisted the temptation to eat cake.
words.ex_cn: 他抵制了吃蛋糕的诱惑。
words.en: If you feel you want to do something or have something, even though you know you really should avoid it, you can refer to this feeling as temptation.

words.ex: He has an addiction to video games.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏上瘾了。
words.en: Addiction is the condition of being unable to stop using or doing something as a habit, especially something harmful.

words.ex: The game is addictive and hard to stop playing.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏令人上瘾，很难停止玩。
words.en: If a substance or activity is addictive, it makes you want more of it so that you become dependent on it.

words.tr: adj. 欺骗的；消遣的；令人陶醉的; v. 欺骗；使愉快地度过；迷住（beguile 的 ing ...
words.ex: The beguiling smile made him trust her.
words.ex_cn: 那迷人的微笑让他信任了她。
words.en: Something that is beguiling is charming and attractive, often in a way that is deceptive.

words.ex: He immersed the cloth in water.
words.ex_cn: 他把布浸在水里。
words.en: To immerse something or someone means to put them into a liquid so that they are completely covered by it. It can also mean to involve oneself deeply in a particular activity or interest.

words.ex: The shop tries to entice customers with cheap prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店试图以低价吸引顾客。
words.en: If you entice someone, you attract them to a particular place or activity by making it seem attractive or interesting.

words.ex: He obsesses over small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他 obsesses 于微小的错误。
words.en: If something or someone obsesses you, you think or worry about them all the time and you cannot think about anything else.

words.ex: Parents shouldn't indulge their children's bad habits.
words.ex_cn: 父母不应该放任孩子的坏习惯。
words.en: To indulge means to allow yourself or someone else to have something enjoyable, especially more than is good for you.

words.tr:
v. （使）获得；
adj. 安全的；稳定的；
words.ex: He worked hard to secure a job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以获得一份工作。
words.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

words.ex: He is fanatical about football.
words.ex_cn: 他对足球非常狂热。
words.en: If you describe someone as fanatical, you mean that they are extremely enthusiastic about a particular activity, subject, or belief, often to an extent that is considered excessive or unreasonable.

chapters.name: 避免/避开/否认/拒绝/停止/禁止

words.ex: This tool can obviate the need for manual work.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具可以避免手动工作的需要。
words.en: To obviate means to remove a need or difficulty, especially so that action to deal with it becomes unnecessary.

words.tr: v. 绕行；设法避开；智胜；围住
words.ex: He circumvented the traffic by taking a small road.
words.ex_cn: 他通过走一条小路绕过了交通拥堵。
words.en: If someone circumvents a rule or restriction, they avoid having to obey it, usually in a clever and dishonest way.

words.ex: She wore a red skirt to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条红色短裙去参加派对。
words.en: A skirt is a piece of clothing that hangs from the waist and covers part or all of the legs. It can also refer to the edge or border of something, or to the act of moving along the edge of something.

words.ex: They live on the outskirts of the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在城市的郊区。
words.en: The outskirts of a city or town are the parts of it that are farthest away from its center.

words.tr:
n. 旁路；
v. 绕过；
words.ex: The city built a bypass around the old town.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市建了一条绕过老城区的旁路。
words.en: If you bypass a place or a system, you avoid it or go around it instead of going through it.

words.ex: He tries to eschew sugar for health reasons.
words.ex_cn: 他为了健康尽量避免吃糖。
words.en: If you eschew something, you deliberately avoid doing it or becoming involved in it.

words.ex: He tried to evade the police by driving fast.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过高速驾驶来逃避警察。
words.en: If you evade something, you find a way of not doing something that you really ought to do.

words.tr:
n. 树篱；防范措施
v. 用树篱围住；限制；避免
words.ex: He planted a hedge around his garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在花园周围种了一排树篱。
words.en: A hedge is a row of bushes or small trees which have been planted along the edge of a garden, field, or road to separate it from another area or to protect it. As a verb, to hedge means to avoid committing oneself or to limit or qualify something by conditions or exceptions.

words.tr: v. 拒绝；断绝关系；否认；驳斥
words.ex: He repudiate the false claim.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这个虚假的声明。
words.en: If you repudiate something or someone, you show that you strongly disagree with them and do not want to be connected with them in any way.

words.ex: He felt sad after the rejection.
words.ex_cn: 在遭到拒绝后，他感到很难过。
words.en: The act of refusing to accept, believe in, or agree with something.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.ex: No one can gainsay the truth.
words.ex_cn: 没有人能否认这个事实。
words.en: If there is no gainsaying something, it is not possible to deny that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: The repudiation of the old policy surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 对旧政策的批判让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The act of refusing to accept, acknowledge, or support something; rejection.

words.tr:
v. 断然拒绝
n. 粗暴回绝；生硬的拒绝
words.ex: He rebuffed her offer with a shake of his head.
words.ex_cn: 他摇了摇头，拒绝了她的提议。
words.en: If you rebuff someone or rebuff a suggestion that they make, you refuse to do what they suggest.

words.ex: He disavow any connection to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 他否认与这起犯罪有任何关联。
words.en: If you disavow something, you say that you are not responsible for it or you do not agree with it.

words.tr:
v. 击退；回绝；憎恶
n. 拒斥；击退；严拒
words.ex: The soldiers repulse the enemy attack.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们击退了敌人的进攻。
words.en: If you repulse someone, you reject them or make them feel disgusted.

words.ex: The smell of the garbage is repulsive.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾的气味令人厌恶。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as repulsive, you mean that they are horrible and disgusting and you want to avoid them.

words.tr: v. （使）停滞；不发展；因不流动而变得污浊
words.ex: The economy began to stagnate after the crisis.
words.ex_cn: 经济在危机后开始停滞。
words.en: If something such as a business or project stagnates, it stops developing or making progress.

words.ex: He tried to retract his words after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵后试图收回他的话。
words.en: If you retract something that you have said or written, you say that you did not mean it.

words.ex: The doctor made a retraction of the false statement.
words.ex_cn: 医生撤回了那条虚假声明。
words.en: A retraction is a statement in which you say that something which you previously said or wrote is not true.

words.tr: n. 禁止；放逐；剥夺人权
words.ex: The law includes a proscription against lying under oath.
words.ex_cn: 法律中包含对作伪证的禁止。
words.en: The act of proscribing; prohibition or interdiction.

words.tr: adj. 放逐的；剥夺人权的；禁止的
words.ex: The teacher gave a proscriptive rule: no talking during the test.
words.ex_cn: 老师制定了一条禁止性规则：考试期间不准说话。
words.en: If something is proscriptive, it involves the act of proscribing or forbidding something, often in a formal or legal context.

words.tr:
v. 中断；暂停；
n. 停顿下来；
words.ex: The storm halted the flight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴中断了航班。
words.en: to bring or come to a stop; a temporary or permanent stop

words.ex: The people tried to overthrow the corrupt government.
words.ex_cn: 人民试图推翻腐败的政府。
words.en: To overthrow a government or a leader means to remove them from power, often by force.

chapters.name: 解释/阐明/证明/揭露/泄露/开放/开明

words.ex: He interprets the poem as a love story.
words.ex_cn: 他把这首诗解释为一个爱情故事。
words.en: If you interpret something in a particular way, you decide that this is its meaning or significance.

words.ex: He misinterprets her words as anger.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了她的话，以为是生气。
words.en: To interpret wrongly; misunderstand.

words.ex: The teacher gave a simple interpretation of the poem.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这首诗做了一个简单的解释。
words.en: An interpretation of something is an explanation or understanding of it.

words.ex: He made a misinterpretation of the instructions.
words.ex_cn: 他对说明产生了误解。
words.en: A misinterpretation is a wrong understanding or explanation of something.

words.ex: The verification of the password took only a few seconds.
words.ex_cn: 密码的验证只花了几秒钟。
words.en: Verification is the process of establishing the truth, accuracy, or validity of something.

words.tr: adj. 可核实的；能证实的
words.ex: The result must be verifiable by anyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个结果必须能被任何人验证。
words.en: Capable of being verified or confirmed by evidence or testimony.

words.tr: adj. 无法核实的；无法检验的；不能证实的
words.ex: The claim is unverifiable without evidence.
words.ex_cn: 没有证据，这个说法无法验证。
words.en: If something is unverifiable, there is no way to prove whether it is true or not.

words.ex: He felt vindication when the truth came out.
words.ex_cn: 当真相大白时，他感到被证实了。
words.en: Vindication is the act of proving that someone is not guilty of a crime or that something is true.

words.ex: Can you clarify your answer?
words.ex_cn: 你能澄清一下你的答案吗？
words.en: To clarify something means to make it easier to understand by explaining it more clearly.

words.ex: He adduce evidence to prove his point.
words.ex_cn: 他提出证据来证明自己的观点。
words.en: To cite as evidence or proof; to bring forward in argument or as proof.

words.tr: v. 解释；把…逐字译出；作句法分析
words.ex: He construes her silence as a yes.
words.ex_cn: 他把她的沉默理解为同意。
words.en: If you construe something in a particular way, you interpret it in that way.

words.ex: He misconstrued her smile as anger.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了她的微笑，以为是生气。
words.en: If you misconstrue something that has been said or something that happens, you interpret it wrongly.

words.ex: The witness corroborated his story with photos.
words.ex_cn: 证人用照片证实了他的说法。
words.en: To corroborate something that has been said or reported means to provide evidence or information that supports it.

words.ex: The witness gave corroboration for the story.
words.ex_cn: 证人对这个说法提供了佐证。
words.en: Corroboration is evidence or information that supports a statement, theory, or finding.

words.tr: adj. 不证自明的；不言而喻的
words.ex: It is self-evident that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
words.ex_cn: 水在100摄氏度沸腾是显而易见的。
words.en: Something that is self-evident is so obvious that there is no need for proof or explanation.

words.ex: It is evident that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is evident, it is easy to see, perceive, or understand.

words.ex: The police found evidentiary proof at the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 警察在犯罪现场找到了证据。
words.en: Relating to or providing evidence.

words.ex: His sadness manifested in his quiet eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲伤表现在他安静的眼神中。
words.en: To manifest something means to show it clearly and visibly.

words.ex: The lamp illuminate the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 这盏灯照亮了黑暗的房间。
words.en: To illuminate something means to shine light on it and to make it brighter and more visible.

words.ex: The painting depicts a quiet village at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一个宁静的村庄在日落时分的景象。
words.en: To depict someone or something means to show or represent them in a work of art such as a drawing or painting.

words.ex: The movie's depiction of ancient life is very realistic.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影对古代生活的描写非常真实。
words.en: A depiction of something is a picture or a written description of it.

words.ex: He will delineate the plan clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地描述这个计划。
words.en: To delineate something means to describe or portray it precisely.

words.ex: This problem is solvable with simple math.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题用简单的数学就能解决。
words.en: If a problem or puzzle is solvable, it can be solved or answered.

words.tr: v. 确定无罪；免除（罪责）
words.ex: The new evidence helped to exonerate him.
words.ex_cn: 新的证据帮助他洗清了罪名。
words.en: If someone is exonerated, they are proved to be not guilty of a crime or responsible for something bad that happened.

words.ex: The teacher elucidated the math problem with a simple diagram.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的图表阐明了这道数学题。
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by explaining or giving reasons.

words.ex: The letter revealed his secret.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他的秘密。
words.en: To reveal something means to make known something that was previously secret or unknown.

words.tr: n. 揭露；被揭示的真相；
words.ex: The letter was a revelation about his secret life.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他隐秘的生活。
words.en: A revelation is a surprising and previously unknown fact that has been disclosed to others.

words.ex: He made a disclosure about the secret plan.
words.ex_cn: 他透露了这个秘密计划。
words.en: The act of making something known or the fact that is made known.

words.ex: He won't divulge the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他不会泄露这个秘密。
words.en: If you divulge a piece of secret or private information, you tell it to someone.

words.tr:
adj. 开明的；有见识的；启迪的
v. 启发；开导；“enlighten”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is an enlightened teacher who helps students think clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位开明的老师，帮助学生清晰思考。
words.en: If you describe someone or their attitudes as enlightened, you mean that they have sensible, modern attitudes and ways of dealing with things.

words.ex: His openness helped the team trust him.
words.ex_cn: 他的开放态度让团队信任他。
words.en: The quality or state of being open, especially in terms of being honest and not hiding one's thoughts or feelings.

words.tr: adj. 直言无讳的；坦率的；
words.ex: He is an outspoken teacher who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位直言不讳的老师，总是说真话。
words.en: Someone who is outspoken expresses their opinions frankly and honestly, even if they are likely to shock or offend people.

chapters.name: 错误/假的/误导/欺骗/歪曲/掩盖

words.tr: n. 不准确；不精确；错误
words.ex: The inaccuracy of the clock caused delays.
words.ex_cn: 钟的不准确导致了延误。
words.en: The quality or state of being inaccurate; error.

words.ex: The accuracy of the clock is very high.
words.ex_cn: 这个钟的精确性很高。
words.en: The quality or state of being correct or precise.

words.tr: adv. 准确地；精确地；正确地；
words.ex: He measured the length accurately.
words.ex_cn: 他准确地测量了长度。
words.en: In a way that is correct or exact.

words.ex: His answer was erroneous because he added wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案是错误的，因为他加错了。
words.en: If you describe someone's beliefs or opinions as erroneous, you mean that they are incorrect and based on false information.

words.ex: He erroneously thought the answer was 5.
words.ex_cn: 他错误地认为答案是5。
words.en: In a way that is incorrect or based on false information.

words.tr: n. 不正确）；错误（有误差
words.ex: The erroneousness of his answer was clear.
words.ex_cn: 他答案的不正确性很明显。
words.en: The state or quality of being erroneous; incorrectness.

words.tr: adj. 纯粹的；[材] 非合金的
words.ex: He has unalloyed joy when he sees his daughter smile.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到女儿微笑时，他感到纯粹的快乐。
words.en: Not mixed or diluted with any different or extra elements; complete and absolute.

words.tr: adj. 似是而非的；貌似有理的
words.ex: His argument is specious and misleading.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点看似有理但具有误导性。
words.en: Something that is specious seems to be good, sound, or correct but is actually wrong or false.

words.tr: adj. 迷惑的；误导的；虚妄的
words.ex: The promise of quick riches is often delusive.
words.ex_cn: 迅速致富的承诺往往是欺瞒的。
words.en: Something that is delusive gives a false impression or leads you to believe something that is not true.

words.ex: The deceptive smile hid his true intentions.
words.ex_cn: 那欺骗性的微笑隐藏了他真正的意图。
words.en: If something is deceptive, it encourages you to believe something which is not true.

words.ex: His deception fooled everyone at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他的欺骗骗过了派对上的所有人。
words.en: Deception is the act of deceiving someone or the state of being deceived.

words.ex: He misleads his friends with false stories.
words.ex_cn: 他用虚假的故事误导他的朋友。
words.en: If you say that someone has misled you, you mean that they have made you believe something which is not true, either by telling you a lie or by giving you a wrong idea or impression.

words.ex: He wore a scary mask at the Halloween party.
words.ex_cn: 他在万圣节派对上戴了一个可怕的面具。
words.en: A mask is a piece of cloth or other material that you wear over your face to hide or protect it.

words.tr: adj. 错误的； v. “misguide”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: His misguided decision cost him his job.
words.ex_cn: 他错误的决定让他丢了工作。
words.en: If you describe an opinion or plan as misguided, you are critical of it because you think it is based on an incorrect idea or judgment.

words.ex: He is credulous and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很轻信，相信他听到的每一个故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as credulous, you have a low opinion of them because they are too ready to believe what people tell them and are easily deceived.

words.ex: He looked incredulous when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他一脸难以置信。
words.en: If someone is incredulous, they are unable to believe something because it is very surprising or shocking.

words.ex: His credulousness made him believe the fake news.
words.ex_cn: 他的轻信让他相信了假新闻。
words.en: The tendency to be too ready to believe that something is real or true.

words.ex: The car deviated from the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车偏离了道路。
words.en: To deviate means to do something that is different from the usual or common way of behaving.

words.tr: v. 以甜言蜜语哄骗；勾引
words.ex: He tried to cajole his sister into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗妹妹把钱借给他。
words.en: If you cajole someone into doing something, you persuade them to do it by flattery or by making promises.

words.ex: He fabricates excuses to avoid work.
words.ex_cn: 他编造借口来逃避工作。
words.en: To fabricate means to invent or produce something false in order to deceive someone.

words.ex: His argument is fallacious because it ignores the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点是错误的，因为它忽略了事实。
words.en: If an idea, argument, or reason is fallacious, it is wrong because it is based on a fallacy.

words.tr:
n. 骗局；恶作剧；戏弄
v. 愚弄
words.ex: The news was a hoax to scare people.
words.ex_cn: 这则新闻是个骗局，为了吓唬人。
words.en: A hoax is a plan to deceive someone, such as telling the police there is a bomb somewhere when there is not, or a trick in which someone tells people a lie.

words.tr: adj. 质地薄的；肮脏的；低劣的
words.ex: The sleazy curtain let in too much light.
words.ex_cn: 那层薄薄的窗帘透进了太多光。
words.en: If you describe something as sleazy, you mean that it is of low quality or morally questionable, especially because it is associated with sex or crime.

words.ex: Her constant mendacity made it difficult to trust her.
words.ex_cn: 她不断的谎言让人难以信任她。
words.en: The quality of being untruthful; lying.

words.ex: He is gullible and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易受骗，相信每一个他听到的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as gullible, you mean they are easily tricked because they are too trusting.

words.tr: adj. 无害的；无冒犯之意的
words.ex: The comment was innocuous and didn't upset anyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个评论无害，没有惹恼任何人。
words.en: Something that is innocuous is not harmful or offensive.

words.tr:
n. 妥协；
v. 危及；
words.ex: They reached a compromise after hours of talk.
words.ex_cn: 经过数小时的讨论，他们达成了妥协。
words.en: A compromise is an agreement between two people or groups in which each side gives up some of the things they want so that both sides are happy at the end.

words.tr: adj. 不让步的；不妥协的；强硬的
words.ex: He is uncompromising about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他在诚实方面毫不妥协。
words.en: If you describe someone as uncompromising, you mean that they are determined not to change their opinions or aims in any way.

words.ex: He believes in an egalitarian society where everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他相信一个人人平等的平等主义社会。
words.en: Egalitarian is used to describe something that is based on the principle that all people are equal and deserve equal rights and opportunities.

words.tr: v. 使中立；中和；使无效
words.ex: The government tried to neutralize the conflict by talking to both sides.
words.ex_cn: 政府试图通过与双方交谈来使冲突中立化。
words.en: To neutralize something means to stop it from having any effect or to make it ineffective.

words.tr:
n. 平衡；天平；秤；
v. （使）相抵；（使）平衡；
words.ex: She maintains a good balance between work and rest.
words.ex_cn: 她在工作和休息之间保持良好的平衡。
words.en: Balance is the ability to remain steady when you are standing up. Also, it refers to the state of having your weight spread equally so that you do not fall. In finance, it refers to the amount of money you have in a bank account.

words.ex: The judge made an unbalanced decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官做出了一个不公正的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as unbalanced, you mean that they appear disturbed and upset or they seem to be slightly mad.

words.tr:
v. 抵消；使平衡
n. 衡重体；平衡力
words.ex: The weight acts as a counterbalance to the arm.
words.ex_cn: 这个重量作为手臂的平衡物。
words.en: A counterbalance is a weight or force that balances or counteracts another.

words.ex: He likes eclecticism in music, from jazz to rock.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢音乐上的折衷主义，从爵士到摇滚。
words.en: Eclecticism is a conceptual approach that does not hold rigidly to a single paradigm or set of assumptions, but instead draws upon multiple theories, styles, or ideas to gain complementary insights into a subject, or applies different theories in particular cases.

words.ex: The company will compensate you for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 公司会因延误而补偿你。
words.en: If you compensate for a lack of something or for something you have done wrong, you do something to show that you are sorry or that you are trying to make things better.

words.ex: The rain offset the heat yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天的雨抵消了炎热。
words.en: If one thing is offset by another, the effect of the first thing is reduced by the second, so that any advantage or disadvantage is cancelled out.

words.tr: adj. 和平主义的；和平的
words.ex: His irenic tone helped calm the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他平和的语气帮助平息了争论。
words.en: Promoting peace; conciliatory.

words.tr:
n. 僵局；和棋；僵持状态
v. 使陷入僵局
words.ex: The two players are in a stalemate.
words.ex_cn: 两位选手陷入了僵局。
words.en: A situation in which further action or progress by opposing parties seems impossible.

words.tr:
n. 顺序；条理；命令；订单；(生物学的)目；
v. 订购；命令；点餐；整理；
words.ex: The books are in alphabetical order.
words.ex_cn: 这些书是按字母顺序排列的。
words.en: If you order someone to do something, you tell them to do it in a way that they have to obey. Order can also refer to the way things are arranged or a request to make or supply something.

words.ex: The room was in complete disorder.
words.ex_cn: 房间一片混乱。
words.en: A disorder is a state of confusion or untidiness, or a medical problem that affects the mind or body.

words.ex: The classroom is orderly and clean.
words.ex_cn: 教室整洁有序。
words.en: If something is done in an orderly fashion or manner, it is done in a well-organized and controlled way.

words.ex: The doctor tried to stabilize the patient's heart rate.
words.ex_cn: 医生试图稳定病人的脉搏。
words.en: To stabilize something means to make it stable or to prevent it from changing or declining.

words.tr: adj. 非稳定的; v. 使失去平衡（destabilize 的过去分词）
words.ex: The war destabilized the whole region.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争使整个地区变得不稳定。
words.en: To make something or someone unstable or less secure.

words.ex: The instability of the bridge made people afraid to cross it.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥的不稳定让人们不敢过桥。
words.en: Instability is the state of being unstable, especially in a political or economic context, where it refers to a lack of stability or the tendency to change or fail suddenly.

words.tr: adj. 不可改变的；永恒不变的
words.ex: The password is immutable and cannot be changed.
words.ex_cn: 密码是不可更改的。
words.en: If you say that something is immutable, you mean that it cannot be changed at all.

chapters.name: 理智/理性/冷漠/平静/温和/谦虚

words.tr: v. 组成；创作；“compose”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The team is composed of five players.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队由五名队员组成。
words.en: If someone is composed, they are calm and able to control their feelings.

words.ex: The cerebral cortex controls thinking and memory.
words.ex_cn: 大脑皮层控制思考和记忆。
words.en: Relating to the brain or the intellect.

words.ex: His speech was coherent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲连贯且易于理解。
words.en: If something is coherent, it is well planned, so that it is clear and sensible and all its parts go well with each other.

words.tr: adj. 不装腔作势的；低调谦逊的；
words.ex: He is an unassuming man who never talks about his achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个不装腔作势的人，从不谈论自己的成就。
words.en: If you describe someone as unassuming, you approve of them because they are quiet and do not try to appear important.

words.ex: His assumption was that the train would be on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是火车会准时。
words.en: An assumption is something that you assume to be the case, even without proof.

words.ex: There was a lull in the rain before the storm came back.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨再次来临前，雨下了一阵间歇。
words.en: A lull is a short period of quiet or calm in an otherwise noisy or hectic situation. To lull means to cause someone to feel calm or to fall asleep.

words.tr: adj. 不感兴趣的；不关心的；
words.ex: He was indifferent to the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏兴趣的；漠不关心的；
words.ex: He was apathetic about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影缺乏兴趣。
words.en: If you describe someone as apathetic, you are criticizing them because they do not seem to be interested in or enthusiastic about doing anything.

words.ex: The car remained static at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在红灯前静止不动。
words.en: Something that is static does not move or change.

words.tr: adj. 易驾驭的；温顺的；易处理的
words.ex: The dog is so tractable that it follows commands effortlessly.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗非常驯良，能轻松地服从命令。
words.en: If you say that a person, problem, or device is tractable, you mean that they can be easily controlled or dealt with.

words.ex: The problem is intractable and no one can solve it.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题很难处理，没人能解决。
words.en: If you describe a problem or a person as intractable, you mean that it is very difficult to deal with or to change.

words.ex: The intractability of the problem surprised the scientists.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题的难以解决让科学家们感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being difficult to control or deal with.

words.ex: The cat sat in quiescence under the tree.
words.ex_cn: 猫在树下安静地坐着。
words.en: A state of inactivity or dormancy.

words.ex: The volcano is quiescent now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Someone or something that is quiescent is quiet and inactive.

words.tr: adj. 可管理的；可应付的；可处理的；
words.ex: The project is manageable if we work together.
words.ex_cn: 如果我们一起合作，这个项目是可以管理的。
words.en: If you describe something as manageable, you mean that it is easy to control or deal with.

words.tr: adj. 难处理的，处理不了的；难管理的；难操纵的
words.ex: The pile of papers was unmanageable.
words.ex_cn: 那堆文件多得无法处理。
words.en: If you describe something as unmanageable, you mean that it is difficult to control or deal with because it is too big, complex, or powerful.

words.ex: He remained impassive when he heard the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个坏消息时，他依然面无表情。
words.en: If someone is impassive, they do not show any emotion.

words.ex: He is a temperate person who never shouts.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个温和的人，从不大喊大叫。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as temperate, you mean that it is calm and reasonable, not extreme or emotional.

words.ex: The movie was tame and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影枯燥无味。
words.en: If you describe an animal as tame, you mean that it is not afraid of humans and is not dangerous. If you describe a person or their behavior as tame, you mean that they are not very exciting or interesting.

words.tr:
adj. 乏味无趣的；四平八稳的；不得罪人的；止痛的
n. 止痛药
words.ex: The meeting was anodyne and made everyone sleepy.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议乏味无趣，让所有人都犯困。
words.en: An anodyne is something that soothes, comforts, or relieves pain.

words.tr: adj. 无动于衷的；坚定的；不动心的
words.ex: She remained unmoved by his pleas.
words.ex_cn: 对他的恳求，她无动于衷。
words.en: If you are unmoved by something, you are not emotionally affected by it.

words.ex: He is phlegmatic even when things go wrong.
words.ex_cn: 即使事情出错，他依然冷静。
words.en: A phlegmatic person does not usually get emotional or excited about things.

words.ex: She sits in the garden with serenity.
words.ex_cn: 她坐在花园里，内心平静。
words.en: The state of being calm, peaceful, and untroubled.

words.ex: He is amenable to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意接受新想法。
words.en: If you are amenable to something, you are willing to do it or accept it.

words.ex: The clement teacher gave students extra time.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师给了学生更多时间。
words.en: Mild or merciful in disposition or character; lenient; compassionate.

words.tr: adj. 温文儒雅的；彬彬有礼的
words.ex: He is an urbane man who speaks politely.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个举止文雅、说话有礼貌的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as urbane, you mean that they are polite, confident, and comfortable in social situations.

words.ex: He is an easygoing man who likes to smile.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个随和的人，喜欢微笑。
words.en: Someone who is easygoing is relaxed and not easily upset or worried.

words.tr: adj. 卑屈的；恭顺的；次要的；从属的
words.ex: He is subservient to his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的老板唯命是从。
words.en: If you are subservient, you do whatever someone wants you to do.

words.ex: The small spider is harmless.
words.ex_cn: 这只小蜘蛛是无害的。
words.en: If someone or something is harmless, they are not dangerous and do not cause any harm.

words.tr: adj. 不多的；适度的；谦虚的；
words.ex: He made a modest profit last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年的利润不多。
words.en: If you say that someone is modest, you approve of them because they do not talk much about their abilities or achievements.

words.ex: His modesty made everyone like him.
words.ex_cn: 他的谦虚让所有人都喜欢他。
words.en: Modesty is the quality of not being too proud or confident about yourself or your abilities.

words.ex: He showed humility after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得奖品后表现出了谦逊。
words.en: Humility is the quality of being humble and not thinking that you are better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 不虚饰的；朴素的；不夸耀的
words.ex: He lives in a small house and wears unostentatious clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一所小房子里，穿得很朴素。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour or appearance as unostentatious, you mean that it is simple and not intended to impress people.

words.ex: His ostentatiousness made people uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他的炫耀让人感到不舒服。
words.en: The quality of being ostentatious; pretentious or showy display designed to impress.

chapters.name: 恼怒/愤怒/焦虑/急躁/鲁莽/难以驾驭

words.tr: v. 使烦恼；“trouble”的现在分词； adj. 令人烦恼的；令人不安的；
words.ex: The loud noise is troubling me.
words.ex_cn: 这噪音让我感到烦恼。
words.en: Causing distress or anxiety; worrying.

words.ex: The unfair verdict caused public outrage.
words.ex_cn: 不公正的判决引发了公众的愤怒。
words.en: An outrage is an extremely strong reaction of anger, shock, or indignation.

words.ex: He is irascible when he wakes up late.
words.ex_cn: 他起床晚时容易发怒。
words.en: If you describe someone as irascible, you mean that they become angry very easily.

words.ex: His irascibility made him angry over small things.
words.ex_cn: 他的易怒使他为小事发脾气。
words.en: Irascibility is the quality of being easily angered or having a bad temper.

words.tr: v. 激怒；使急躁；使疼痛
words.ex: Loud noises irritate my baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音会激怒我的宝宝。
words.en: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

words.ex: He felt resentment after being ignored by his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他被朋友忽视后感到怨恨。
words.en: Resentment is a feeling of anger or bitterness about something that you believe is unfair.

words.ex: He slammed the door in exasperation.
words.ex_cn: 他因恼怒而砰地关上了门。
words.en: Exasperation is a feeling of intense irritation or annoyance.

words.ex: The loud noise exasperates me.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让我感到烦躁。
words.en: If someone or something exasperates you, they annoy you and make you feel frustrated or impatient.

words.ex: He burst into rage when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他勃然大怒。
words.en: Rage is a feeling of intense anger that is difficult to control.

words.ex: We sat under the umbrage of the big tree.
words.ex_cn: 我们坐在大树的树荫下。
words.en: A feeling of pique or resentment at some often fancied slight or insult.

words.ex: He felt indignant when they blamed him for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他们把错误归咎于他时，他感到愤愤不平。
words.en: If you are indignant, you are shocked and angry, because you think that something is unjust or unfair.

words.tr: adj. 难堪的；使烦恼的；擦伤人的; n. （Galling）人名；（德）加林
words.ex: It was galling to wait so long for nothing.
words.ex_cn: 等了这么久却一无所获，真让人气愤。
words.en: If you say that something is galling, you mean it is annoying or irritating, often because it makes you feel helpless or inadequate.

words.tr: v. 使恼怒；使生气；使不悦
words.ex: The loud noise displeases her.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的声音让她不高兴。
words.en: If something or someone displeases you, they make you feel annoyed or angry.

words.ex: The car moved at a rapid speed.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车以迅速的速度行驶。
words.en: A rapid change or event happens very quickly.

words.ex: The car moved rapidly down the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车迅速地沿着道路行驶。
words.en: If something happens rapidly, it happens very quickly.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；彻底的；激进的；
words.ex: The government made radical changes to the education system.
words.ex_cn: 政府对教育系统进行了根本性的改革。
words.en: A radical change or difference is very big and important.

words.ex: He supports radicalism to change the system.
words.ex_cn: 他支持激进主义来改变制度。
words.en: Radicalism is the belief or behavior of people who advocate thorough or complete political or social reform.

words.ex: The movie ended with suspense, and no one knew what happened next.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影以悬念结束，没人知道接下来发生了什么。
words.en: Suspense is a state of excitement or anxiety about something that is going to happen very soon, especially something that could be either good or bad.

words.tr: adj. 匆匆的；粗略的；仓促的
words.ex: He gave the report a cursory look.
words.ex_cn: 他粗略地看了看这份报告。
words.en: A cursory glance or examination is a quick one that is not very thorough.

words.tr: adj. 令人烦恼的；令人不安的；令人担忧的
words.ex: The dark clouds look worrisome.
words.ex_cn: 乌云看起来令人担忧。
words.en: If you describe something as worrisome, you mean that it causes you to feel anxious or concerned.

words.tr:
v. 加速（坏事的发生）
n. 沉淀物；冷凝物
adj. 轻率的；仓促的
words.ex: The scandal precipitated the politician's resignation.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻加速了这位政治家的辞职。
words.en: To cause something to happen suddenly or unexpectedly; to cause a substance to be deposited in solid form from a solution.

words.tr:
adj. 鲁莽的；狂妄的；轻率的
n. 狂妄的人（尤指女子）
words.ex: The madcap boy ran through the park with no hat.
words.ex_cn: 那个疯疯癫癫的男孩没戴帽子跑过了公园。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as madcap, you mean that they are full of energy and enthusiasm, but slightly crazy or uncontrolled.

words.ex: He felt trepidation before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到恐惧。
words.en: A feeling of fear or anxiety about something that may happen.

words.tr: n. 不慎重；轻率；言行失检
words.ex: His indiscretion caused a big problem at work.
words.ex_cn: 他的轻率行为在工作中引起了大问题。
words.en: Indiscretion refers to behavior or speech that is not discreet; it can also mean a lack of good judgment or care in what one says or does.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；难驾驭的；难以治愈的
words.ex: The refractory material can withstand high temperatures.
words.ex_cn: 这种耐火材料能承受高温。
words.en: Stubbornly resistant to authority or control; difficult to melt or work; resistant to heat.

words.tr:
v. 使惊慌失措；使慌张
n. 慌张；慌乱
words.ex: He got flustered when the teacher asked him a question.
words.ex_cn: 当老师问他问题时，他变得慌乱了。
words.en: If you fluster someone, you make them feel nervous and confused by rushing them or by making it difficult for them to concentrate on what they are doing.

words.tr: adj. 令人不安的；令人忧虑的; v. 使不安；使忧虑（disquiet 的 ing 形式）
words.ex: The dark clouds are disquieting.
words.ex_cn: 乌云令人不安。
words.en: If you say that something is disquieting, you mean that it causes feelings of worry or anxiety.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；鲁莽的；大胆创新的
words.ex: He made an audacious plan to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个大胆的计划，独自攀登那座山。
words.en: If you describe someone as audacious, you mean that they take risks in order to achieve something and show a willingness to challenge conventional ideas.

chapters.name: 激发/激励/使繁荣/激化/增加/夸大

words.ex: Her story inspires me to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 她的故事激励我更加努力。
words.en: If someone or something inspires you to do something new or unusual, they make you want to do it.

words.ex: The factory galvanize iron sheets to prevent rust.
words.ex_cn: 工厂对铁片进行镀锌以防止生锈。
words.en: To galvanize someone means to cause them to take action, for example by making them feel very excited, afraid, or angry.

words.ex: The bright light stimulated her eyes.
words.ex_cn: 强烈的光线刺激了她的眼睛。
words.en: To stimulate something means to encourage it to begin or develop further.

words.tr: v. 增添活力；振奋；使活跃
words.ex: The fresh air invigorates me every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早晨的新鲜空气让我精神焕发。
words.en: If something invigorates you, it makes you feel more energetic and alive.

words.tr:
n. 鞭策；
v. 刺激；
words.ex: The competition served as a spur to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 竞争成了推动他更努力工作的鞭策。
words.en: A spur is something that makes you want to do something or that encourages you to do it. It can also refer to a sharp device worn on the heel of a rider's boot to urge a horse forward.

words.tr: vt. 鼓动，激励；使更快发生；加速（spur 的现在分词）
words.ex: The new policy is spurring more people to use public transport.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策正在促使更多人使用公共交通。
words.en: To spur someone means to encourage them to do something or to encourage them to try harder to achieve something.

words.ex: His speech was hortatory, urging everyone to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲是劝勉性的，鼓励大家更加努力工作。
words.en: If someone makes a hortatory speech or statement, they are encouraging or urging people to do something.

words.tr: v. 赋予能量；使精力充沛；激励
words.ex: Coffee helps me energize in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 咖啡帮助我在早上恢复活力。
words.en: To energize someone means to give them the enthusiasm, determination, and energy to do something.

words.ex: He tried to incite a riot with his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过演讲煽动暴乱。
words.en: To incite someone to do something means to encourage or persuade them to do it, often in a way that is negative or harmful.

words.ex: He tries to foment trouble between the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在邻居之间挑起纠纷。
words.en: If someone foments trouble or violent opposition, they cause it to develop.

words.tr: v. 繁荣兴旺；茁壮成长；
words.ex: The business flourishes in the new market.
words.ex_cn: 这家企业在新市场中繁荣兴旺。
words.en: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

words.tr: v. 使有生气；使活跃；使快活
words.ex: The music enlivened the party.
words.ex_cn: 音乐让派对更热闹了。
words.en: To make something more interesting, exciting, or cheerful.

words.tr:
adj. 有生命的；有活力的
v. 使具活力；做成动画
words.ex: The cartoon characters are animate and full of energy.
words.ex_cn: 这些卡通角色是有生命的，充满活力。
words.en: To animate something means to give it life or to make it lively and energetic.

words.tr: adj. 泛滥的；猖獗的；蔓生的
words.ex: Rumors are rampant in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 谣言在这个小镇上四处流传。
words.en: If you describe something bad, such as a crime or disease, as rampant, you mean that it is very common and is increasing in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr: v. 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；
words.ex: Plants thrive in sunny places.
words.ex_cn: 植物在阳光充足的地方茁壮成长。
words.en: To thrive means to grow or develop well or vigorously.

words.ex: Parents should foster good habits in children.
words.ex_cn: 父母应该培养孩子的好习惯。
words.en: To foster something means to encourage and promote its development.

words.ex: Smoking can exacerbate asthma.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会使哮喘加重。
words.en: If something exacerbates a problem or bad situation, it makes it worse.

words.ex: She works out to augment her strength.
words.ex_cn: 她锻炼以增强力量。
words.en: If you augment something, you make it larger, stronger, or more effective by adding something to it.

words.ex: The augmentation of data helps the model learn better.
words.ex_cn: 数据的增加帮助模型学得更好。
words.en: The act or process of making or becoming greater in size or amount.

words.ex: He exaggerates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸张自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you exaggerate, you indicate that something is, for example, worse or more important than it really is.

words.ex: His story was an exaggeration of the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事是对事实的夸张。
words.en: An exaggeration is a statement that represents something as better or worse than it really is.

words.ex: The storm will intensify tonight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴今晚会加强。
words.en: To make or become more intense or intensive.

words.ex: They will extend the deadline by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他们将截止日期延长一周。
words.en: To extend something means to make it longer or larger, or to spread it over a larger area.

words.ex: He tries to aggrandize himself by lying about his achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他通过吹嘘自己的成就来抬高自己。
words.en: To increase the power, status, or wealth of someone or something.

words.ex: He overstates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸大自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you say that someone is overstating something, you mean they are describing it in a way that makes it seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.ex: His claim was an overstatement of the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的说法是对事实的夸大。
words.en: An overstatement is an exaggerated statement or claim that is not supported by the facts.

words.tr: adj. 夸大的；言过其实的
words.ex: He gave a bombastic speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as bombastic, you are criticizing them for trying to impress other people by saying things that sound impressive but have little meaning.

words.ex: The car will accelerate when you press the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当你踩油门时，汽车会加速。
words.en: To accelerate means to start to go faster or to make something start to go faster.

words.tr: n. 就职；即位；正式加入
words.ex: The king's accession was celebrated by the whole nation.
words.ex_cn: 国王的登基受到了全国的庆祝。
words.en: The act of attaining or gaining access to a position, right, or status.

words.ex: He wants to expedite the process.
words.ex_cn: 他想加快这个过程。
words.en: To expedite something means to make it happen or be done more quickly.

words.ex: He made an expeditious decision to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速做出了离开的决定。
words.en: If you describe something as expeditious, you mean that it is done quickly and efficiently.

words.ex: The speaker will amplify the sound for everyone to hear.
words.ex_cn: 扬声器会放大声音，让每个人都能听到。
words.en: To amplify something means to make it louder, stronger, or more detailed.

words.tr: v. 扩大；膨胀；更充分地阐述；
words.ex: The company plans to expand its business to other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司计划将其业务扩大到其他国家。
words.en: To increase in size, number, or importance, or to make something increase in this way.

words.tr: n. 自然增加；增加之物；增值
words.ex: The accretion of sand formed a small beach.
words.ex_cn: 沙子的堆积形成了一个小海滩。
words.en: Accretion is the process of growth or increase, typically by the gradual accumulation of additional layers or matter.

words.ex: His speech impediment made it hard for him to talk clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他的口吃使他难以清晰地说话。
words.en: An impediment is something that makes it difficult to do or achieve something.

words.ex: Rain can hinder our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨天会妨碍我们去徒步旅行的计划。
words.en: If something hinders you, it makes it more difficult for you to do something or make progress.

words.ex: The smoke began to stifle her breathing.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾开始让她窒息。
words.en: To stifle something means to prevent it from happening, continuing, or developing.

words.ex: The rain impeded his progress on the road.
words.ex_cn: 雨水阻碍了他在路上的进展。
words.en: If something impedes someone or something, it delays their movement or progress or prevents them from achieving something.

words.tr: adj. 畅通无阻的；未受阻的
words.ex: The car moved unimpeded down the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在道路上畅通无阻地行驶。
words.en: If something moves or happens unimpeded, it continues without being stopped or interrupted by anything.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

words.ex: He is encumbered by too many debts.
words.ex_cn: 他被太多的债务拖累。
words.en: To encumber someone or something means to weigh them down or to block or hinder them.

words.tr: adj. 不受妨碍的；没有负担的
words.ex: She felt unencumbered by the responsibilities of her former job.
words.ex_cn: 她感觉摆脱了以前工作中的责任负担。
words.en: If you are unencumbered by something, you are not burdened or hindered by it, allowing you to move or act freely.

words.tr:
v. 阻碍；妨碍
n. （带盖）篮子
words.ex: Rain hampered our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨妨碍了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If something hampers you, it makes it difficult for you to do something.

words.tr:
n. 凝块；泥团；密集的一群
v. 凝结成块
words.ex: The blood began to clot after the cut.
words.ex_cn: 伤口流血后开始凝固。
words.en: A clot is a sticky lump that forms when blood dries up or becomes thick. If blood clots, it becomes thick and forms a lump.

words.tr:
n. 小困难或障碍；划破处；钩丝处
v. 被钩住；划破；抢先获得
words.ex: He found a snag in the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他在计划中发现了一个问题。
words.en: A snag is a small problem or difficulty that you did not expect.

words.ex: He tried to suppress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: To suppress something means to prevent it from being expressed, known, or continuing.

words.ex: The leaf occluded the pipe.
words.ex_cn: 叶子堵住了管道。
words.en: To occlude means to block or stop up a passage, opening, or vessel.

words.tr:
v. 阻挠；妨碍；挫败
n. 横坐板
words.ex: The rain thwarted our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨水破坏了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If you thwart someone or thwart their plans, you prevent them from doing or getting what they want.

words.tr:
v. 钩住；拴住；急拉；搭便车
n. 故障；障碍；勾住；急拉
words.ex: The hook hitched the rope to the tree.
words.ex_cn: 钩子钩住了系在树上的绳子。
words.en: If you hitch, or hitch a ride, you hitchhike. If you hitch something to something else, you fasten it there.

words.tr:
v. 畏缩不前；犹豫；妨碍
n. 阻碍，妨碍
words.ex: He balks at paying high prices.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意支付高价。
words.en: If you balk at something, you hesitate to do it or agree to it, often because it is unpleasant or difficult.

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

words.tr: adj. 不勉强的；非强迫的；不受约束的
words.ex: The boy ran unconstrained through the field.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在田野里无拘无束地奔跑。
words.en: If someone is unconstrained, they are free to act as they wish without being restricted by anything.

words.ex: The snake constricts its prey.
words.ex_cn: 蛇缠住它的猎物。
words.en: If something constricts you, it limits your actions so that you cannot do what you want to do.

words.tr: v. 厚厚地覆盖；使…窒息；闷死
words.ex: He tried to smother the fire with a blanket.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用毯子把火闷灭。
words.en: To smother someone or something means to kill them by covering their face so that they cannot breathe, or to put out a fire by covering it.

words.ex: The law circumscribes what companies can do.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制了公司能做的事情。
words.en: To circumscribe something means to limit its size, activity, or scope, often by setting boundaries or restrictions.

words.tr: adj. 延期的； v. “defer”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The payment is deferred until next month.
words.ex_cn: 付款被推迟到下个月。
words.en: Postponed or delayed.

words.tr: adj. 令人窒息的；使人呼吸困难的；憋气的（suffocate 的 ing 形式）
words.ex: The smoke made the room suffocating.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾让房间令人窒息。
words.en: If you say that something is suffocating, you mean that it makes you feel uncomfortable because there is not enough fresh air and it is difficult to breathe.

words.ex: The company values innovation in its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司重视产品的创新。
words.en: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things.

words.tr: adj. 以实验为基础的；实验性的；
words.ex: The scientist used an experimental method to test the theory.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家使用了一种以实验为基础的方法来检验这个理论。
words.en: Relating to or based on experiment.

words.tr:
n. （长篇）小说；
adj. 新颖的；新奇的；
words.ex: He wrote a novel about a brave girl.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一部关于一个勇敢女孩的小说。
words.en: A novel is a long written story about imaginary people and events.

words.ex: The toy store sells many novelty items for children.
words.ex_cn: 玩具店出售许多为儿童设计的新奇物品。
words.en: The quality of being new, original, or unusual; something new, original, or unusual.

words.ex: The rain precedes the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨先于风暴来临。
words.en: If one event or period of time precedes another, it happens before it.

words.ex: The court followed the precedent set in 1995.
words.ex_cn: 法院遵循了1995年确立的先例。
words.en: A precedent is an action or decision that is used as an example when someone wants to do a similar thing in the future.

words.ex: The storm caused unprecedented damage.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴造成了前所未有的破坏。
words.en: If something is unprecedented, it has never happened before.

words.tr: adj. 有独创性的；巧妙的；
words.ex: The child came up with an ingenious way to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子想出了一个有独创性的方式来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Something that is ingenious is very clever and involves new ideas, methods, or equipment.

words.ex: She wore a chic dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条别致的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as chic, you mean that they are stylish and fashionable.

words.ex: He uses an unorthodox method to teach math.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种非传统的方法教数学。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour, beliefs, or customs as unorthodox, you mean that they are different from what is generally accepted.

words.tr: adj. 偏离规则的；反常的
words.ex: The temperature was anomalous for this season.
words.ex_cn: 这个季节的温度异常。
words.en: Deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.ex: He is an eccentric man who wears socks with sandals.
words.ex_cn: 他是个古怪的人，穿着袜子配凉鞋。
words.en: If you say that someone is eccentric, you mean that they behave in a strange way, and have habits or opinions that are different from those of most people.

words.ex: His eccentricity makes him unique.
words.ex_cn: 他的古怪使他与众不同。
words.en: The quality of being eccentric; behaviour that is unusual, peculiar, or odd.

words.ex: He was accused of heresy for rejecting the church's teachings.
words.ex_cn: 他因拒绝教会的教义而被指控为异端。
words.en: Heresy is a belief or opinion that is contrary to the orthodox religious doctrine, especially in Christianity.

words.ex: His iconoclastic ideas changed the way people think about art.
words.ex_cn: 他打破旧习的想法改变了人们对艺术的看法。
words.en: If you describe someone or their ideas as iconoclastic, you mean that they deliberately challenge established beliefs or institutions.

words.tr: n. 攻击传统观念的人；
words.ex: He is an iconoclast who challenges old beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他是个挑战传统观念的人。
words.en: An iconoclast is someone who criticizes or attacks cherished beliefs or institutions.

words.tr: adj. 非典型的；不规则的
words.ex: He has an atypical way of solving problems.
words.ex_cn: 他解决问题的方式很不寻常。
words.en: Not representative of a type, group, or class; unusual or irregular.

words.tr: adj. 古怪的；离奇的；诡诈的
words.ex: He wears quirky hats every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都戴些古怪的帽子。
words.en: Something or someone that is quirky is unusual or unpredictable in an interesting or appealing way.

words.ex: He was called a heretic for his strange beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 因为他奇怪的信仰，他被称为异端。
words.en: A heretic is someone whose beliefs or actions are considered wrong by most people, because they disagree with beliefs that are generally accepted.

words.ex: He wore an outlandish hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇异的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as outlandish, you mean that it is very unusual, strange, or exaggerated.

chapters.name: 平凡/平庸/乏味/过时/老旧/粗糙

words.ex: This is a commonplace event in big cities.
words.ex_cn: 这在大城市里是件普通的事。
words.en: Something that is commonplace is ordinary and not very interesting.

words.ex: He commonly eats breakfast at 7 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 他一般在早上七点吃早餐。
words.en: If something is commonly the case, it is usually or often the case.

words.ex: It is uncommon to see snow in this city.
words.ex_cn: 在这个城市看到雪是不常见的。
words.en: If you describe something as uncommon, you mean that it does not happen often or is not often seen.

words.tr: adv. 罕见地；极其，非凡地
words.ex: He is uncommonly quiet today.
words.ex_cn: 他今天异常安静。
words.en: If you describe something as uncommonly, you mean that it is unusually or exceptionally so.

words.ex: He used common sense to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他用常识解决了这个问题。
words.en: Common sense is the natural ability to make good judgments and to behave in a practical and sensible way.

words.tr:
n. 常规；例行公事；
adj. 常规的；例行公事的；
words.ex: He follows a morning routine every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都遵循固定的惯例。
words.en: A routine is a sequence of actions regularly followed; a fixed program.

words.ex: He routinely checks his email every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上例行检查邮件。
words.en: If something is routinely done, it is done as a normal part of a job or process.

words.ex: His daily routine is mundane and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活平凡而无聊。
words.en: Something that is mundane is very ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.tr: adj. 公式的；俗套的；刻板的
words.ex: His answer was too formulaic.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答太公式化了。
words.en: If you describe a way of saying or doing something as formulaic, you are criticizing it because it is not original and has been used many times before in similar situations.

words.ex: The teacher will formulate a new rule for class.
words.ex_cn: 老师将制定一条新的课堂规则。
words.en: If you formulate something such as a plan or proposal, you invent it, thinking about the details carefully.

words.tr: adj. 部分形成的；半成形的
words.ex: He gave a half-formulated answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个未完全想好的回答。
words.en: Partially developed or expressed; not fully formed or articulated.

words.tr: adj. 陈腐的；陈词滥调的；老生常谈的
words.ex: His jokes are hackneyed and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话陈腐又无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as hackneyed, you mean that it is unoriginal and has been used so often that it is no longer interesting.

words.ex: The movie had a banal plot that everyone had seen before.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的剧情平庸得让人看过了无数次。
words.en: If you describe something as banal, you do not like it because you think that it is so ordinary that it is not at all effective or interesting.

words.ex: The movie was full of banality and had no original ideas.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影充满了陈词滥调，没有任何新意。
words.en: The quality of being banal; unoriginality.

words.ex: The bread is stale because it was left out too long.
words.ex_cn: 面包不新鲜了，因为它放得太久。
words.en: If food or air is stale, it is no longer fresh and therefore unpleasant.

words.ex: The bread has staleness after three days.
words.ex_cn: 面包放了三天后变 stale 了。
words.en: The state of being no longer fresh or new; lacking in originality or interest.

words.tr: adj. 使疲倦的；令人厌烦的；乏味的
words.ex: The wearisome task of filling out forms took hours.
words.ex_cn: 填写表格这项乏味的任务花了好几个小时。
words.en: If you describe something as wearisome, you mean that it is very tiring and boring or frustrating.

words.ex: He used a cliche to describe the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个陈词滥调来形容日落。
words.en: A cliché is an idea or phrase that has been used so much that it is no longer interesting or effective.

words.ex: The pedestrian crossed the street at the zebra crossing.
words.ex_cn: 行人在斑马线处过马路。
words.en: A pedestrian is a person who is walking in a city, town, or village, especially along a pavement or in a pedestrian area.

words.tr: adj. 俗气的；华而不实的；虚有其表的
words.ex: The decoration was meretricious and lacked any real artistic merit.
words.ex_cn: 装饰俗气，缺乏真正的艺术价值。
words.en: Something that is meretricious is attractive in a showy or cheap way, often without having any real value or quality.

words.tr: adj. 俗丽而不值钱的；花里胡哨的
words.ex: She wore a tawdry dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着一件俗丽的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as tawdry, you mean that it is showy and bright but of very poor quality.

words.tr: adj. 枯燥的；乏味的；平淡无奇的
words.ex: His prosaic speech bored everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他平淡无奇的演讲让所有人都感到无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as prosaic, you mean that it is ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.tr: adj. 陈腐的；无聊的；平庸的
words.ex: His bromidic remarks bored everyone at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他那些陈词滥调让会议上的每个人都感到无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as bromidic, you mean that it is boring and unoriginal because it contains commonly used ideas or sayings.

words.ex: The long meeting was tedious.
words.ex_cn: 这场漫长的会议很沉闷。
words.en: If you describe something such as a job, task, or situation as tedious, you mean it is boring and rather frustrating.

words.tr: adj. 陈腐的；陈词滥调式的
words.ex: His speech was platitudinous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲陈词滥调，令人厌烦。
words.en: If you describe something said or written as platitudinous, you mean that it is dull and boring because it contains very obvious and simple ideas that have been repeated many times before.

words.ex: Wearing those old shoes is unfashionable now.
words.ex_cn: 现在穿那双旧鞋不时髦了。
words.en: If you describe something as unfashionable, you mean that it is not popular or fashionable at the present time.

words.tr: adj. 老式的；老派的；守旧的
words.ex: He wears an old-fashioned hat.
words.ex_cn: 他戴着一顶过时的帽子。
words.en: If you describe something as old-fashioned, you mean that it is no longer modern, current, or fashionable.

words.tr: adj. 时代错误的；落伍的；过时的
words.ex: Wearing a horse-drawn carriage in modern times is anachronistic.
words.ex_cn: 在现代穿马车是过时的。
words.en: Something that is anachronistic is out of its proper time in history, or seems to belong to a different time.

words.tr: n. 时代错误；不合时代的事；过时的事或人
words.ex: The knight in the movie uses a smartphone, which is an anachronism.
words.ex_cn: 电影中的骑士使用智能手机，这是不合时宜的。
words.en: An anachronism is something that is out of place in terms of time or chronology, such as an object, a custom, or an idea that belongs to a different time period than the one in which it is placed.

words.ex: The word 'thou' is archaic in modern English.
words.ex_cn: ‘thou’这个词在现代英语中是过时的。
words.en: Very old or old-fashioned.

words.ex: The old library had a fusty smell.
words.ex_cn: 那间旧图书馆有一股发霉的味道。
words.en: If you describe something as fusty, you mean that it is old-fashioned and not interesting or exciting.

words.ex: The old law was antiquated by the new government.
words.ex_cn: 旧法律被新政府废除了。
words.en: To make something old-fashioned or obsolete.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；老式的； v. “outmode”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This phone is outmoded and needs to be replaced.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，需要更换。
words.en: If you describe something as outmoded, you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.

words.ex: This phone is outdated and doesn't work well.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机过时了，用起来不好。
words.en: If you describe something as outdated, you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.

words.ex: The tribe lives in a primitive hut.
words.ex_cn: 这个部落住在原始的小屋里。
words.en: Belonging to a very early period in the history of the world, or to a time before modern things existed.

words.ex: The sandpaper feels coarse to the touch.
words.ex_cn: 这张砂纸摸起来很粗糙。
words.en: Coarse things have a rough texture because they consist of thick threads or large pieces.

chapters.name: 说教/教条/劝诫/健谈/唠叨/传播

words.tr: adj. 教诲的；说教的；好教训人的
words.ex: The teacher gave a didactic speech to help students learn.
words.ex_cn: 老师发表了一篇富有教育意义的演讲来帮助学生学习。
words.en: Something that is didactic is intended to teach people something, especially a moral lesson.

words.ex: The book shows didacticism by teaching morals through simple stories.
words.ex_cn: 这本书通过简单的故事传授道德，体现了说教性。
words.en: Didacticism is a philosophy that emphasizes instructional and informative qualities in literature and other types of art.

words.ex: His conviction that honesty is important never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他坚信诚实很重要，从未改变。
words.en: A conviction is a strong belief or opinion, or the state of being found guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.tr: n. 训戒；警告（等于 admonition）
words.ex: The teacher's admonishment was clear: no more late assignments.
words.ex_cn: 老师的训诫很明确：不能再有迟交的作业。
words.en: A verbal or written warning or reprimand.

words.ex: The teacher admonished the student to finish his homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师劝告学生完成作业。
words.en: To admonish someone means to tell them in a serious way that they have done something wrong.

words.ex: He wore a coat made of badger.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件用獾皮毛制成的外套。
words.en: To badger someone means to repeatedly ask them to do something or to repeatedly question them about something, often in an annoying way.

words.tr: adj. 说教的；过分认真的；简洁的；富于警句的
words.ex: His speech was full of sententious remarks.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲中充满了简洁精炼的格言。
words.en: If you describe someone as sententious, you mean that they try to appear wise, intelligent, and moral, but in a way that is often perceived as pompous or insincere.

words.tr: adj. 装作圣洁的；伪善的
words.ex: He gave a sanctimonious speech about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一番关于诚实的伪善演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as sanctimonious, you disapprove of them because you think that they are trying to appear morally better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 爱讲道的；说教的；爱唠叨的
words.ex: His speech was preachy and full of moral lessons.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了道德说教。
words.en: If you describe someone as preachy, you mean that they try to give people moral advice in a way that is annoying or boring.

words.tr: v. 哄；用好话劝诱；哄骗
words.ex: He tried to coax the cat out from under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄猫从床底下出来。
words.en: To coax someone means to persuade them to do something by gentle persuasion or flattery.

words.tr:
v. 传播；扩散；散布；
n. 传播；蔓延；范围；
words.ex: The virus spread quickly through the city.
words.ex_cn: 病毒在城市中迅速传播。
words.en: To spread something means to open it out or arrange it over a place or surface, so that all of it can be seen or used easily.

words.tr: adj. 流传甚广的；分布广的；
words.ex: The flu became widespread last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天流感流传甚广。
words.en: Something that is widespread exists or happens over a large area, or to a great extent.

words.tr: adj. 絮聒的；饶舌的；多嘴的
words.ex: He is garrulous and talks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他话很多，说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as garrulous, you mean that they talk a lot, especially about things that are not important.

words.ex: Her garrulity made it difficult for anyone to get a word in edgewise.
words.ex_cn: 她的多嘴多舌让任何人几乎无法插话。
words.en: Garrulity is the quality of being excessively talkative, especially about trivial matters.

words.ex: The meeting felt interminable.
words.ex_cn: 这场会议感觉没完没了。
words.en: If you describe something as interminable, you are emphasizing that it continues for a very long time and indicating that you find it boring or annoying.

words.ex: The news will disseminate quickly through social media.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻会通过社交媒体迅速传播。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or distribute something, especially information, widely.

words.ex: The government will promulgate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将公布新规则。
words.en: To promulgate means to make a new law or rule known officially and publicly.

words.tr: adj. 健谈的；滔滔不绝的
words.ex: He is a voluble speaker who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个健谈的人，整天说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as voluble, you mean that they talk a lot with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr:
adj. 杂乱无章的；不规则的
v. 漫步；漫谈；蔓延；“ramble”的现在分词
words.ex: He gave a rambling speech that was hard to follow.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一篇冗长杂乱的演讲，很难理解。
words.en: If you describe a speech or piece of writing as rambling, you are criticizing it for being too long and very confused.

words.tr:
n. 猫叫春声
v. 发出猫叫春一般的声音
words.ex: The cats were caterwauling all night long.
words.ex_cn: 这些猫整晚都在号叫。
words.en: to make a shrill, discordant sound like that of a cat in heat; to complain loudly

words.ex: He can articulate his ideas clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you describe someone as articulate, you mean that they are able to express their thoughts and ideas easily and clearly.

words.tr: n. 善于讲故事的人；健谈者
words.ex: He was known as a raconteur, always able to captivate an audience with his stories.
words.ex_cn: 他以健谈著称，总能用他的故事吸引听众。
words.en: A raconteur is someone who is good at telling stories in an interesting and amusing way.

words.tr: adj. 雄辩的；有口才的；有说服力的
words.ex: He gave an eloquent speech at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上发表了富有感染力的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as eloquent, you mean that they are able to express their ideas and opinions well, so that other people understand them and are influenced by them.

words.tr: n. 韵律；节奏；抑扬顿挫
words.ex: The dancer moved with a steady cadence.
words.ex_cn: 舞者以稳定的节奏舞动。
words.en: The rhythm or sequence of sounds or movements in speech, music, dance, etc.

words.ex: He uses colloquial words when talking with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友聊天时使用口语化的词语。
words.en: Colloquial language is informal language that is used in ordinary conversation rather than in writing or formal speech.

words.tr: adj. 保留的； v. 保留；“reserve”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The seats are reserved for students.
words.ex_cn: 这些座位是为学生保留的。
words.en: If something is reserved, it is kept specially for a particular purpose or person.

words.tr: adj. 沉默寡言的；讳莫如深的
words.ex: He is reticent about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的感受很沉默。
words.en: If you are reticent about something, you are unwilling to talk about it or make your feelings known.

words.ex: His reticence made everyone wonder what he was thinking.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默让所有人都猜不到他在想什么。
words.en: Reticence is the quality of being reticent, reserved, or unwilling to communicate freely.

words.ex: The ball keeps moving because of inertia.
words.ex_cn: 球因为惯性继续移动。
words.en: Inertia is the tendency of a physical object to continue moving in a straight line at a constant speed, or to stay at rest, unless it is acted upon by a force.

words.ex: The inertial navigation system helped the aircraft maintain its course.
words.ex_cn: 惯性导航系统帮助飞机保持航向。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by inertia.

words.ex: He is introspective and often thinks about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他善于内省，经常思考自己的感受。
words.en: If you describe someone as introspective, you mean that they spend a lot of time examining their own thoughts, ideas, and feelings.

words.ex: He gave his acquiescence to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他默许了这个计划。
words.en: Acquiescence is the act of accepting or agreeing to something without protest.

words.ex: The ceremony was solemn and quiet.
words.ex_cn: 仪式庄严而安静。
words.en: Solemn means very serious and not cheerful, often because something important or sad is happening or being remembered.

words.tr: adj.  忧郁的；阴沉的；阴暗的
words.ex: The room had a somber mood.
words.ex_cn: 房间里有一种阴郁的气氛。
words.en: If someone is somber, they are serious or sad.

chapters.name: 一致/相同/模仿/相应/适合/适应

words.tr:
adj. 相对的；相关联的；
n. 亲戚；
words.ex: His success is relative to his hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的成功是相对于他的努力而言的。
words.en: A relative is someone who is part of your family. Parents, siblings, uncles, aunts, grandparents, cousins, nieces and nephews — they're all relatives.

words.ex: The non-relative was asked to leave the family gathering.
words.ex_cn: 非亲属被要求离开家庭聚会。
words.en: Not connected by kinship or family ties; not related.

words.ex: This room is relatively small.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间相对较小。
words.en: In comparison with other similar things or with what you expect.

words.tr:
adj. 有规律的；经常的；常见的；
n. 常客；
words.ex: He goes for a run every morning, a regular habit.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跑步，这是一个有规律的习惯。
words.en: Something that is regular happens or is done at equal intervals or is consistent in pattern or occurrence.

words.tr: adv. 定期地；经常地；有规律地；
words.ex: He visits his grandparents regularly.
words.ex_cn: 他定期去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: At consistent intervals or in a consistent manner.

words.ex: The children noticed regularities in the number patterns.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们注意到了数字模式中的规律。
words.en: Regularities refer to the state or quality of being regular, consistent, or uniform in pattern or arrangement.

words.ex: The government made a new regulation to control pollution.
words.ex_cn: 政府出台了一项新管理措施来控制污染。
words.en: A regulation is an official rule or order.

words.tr: adj. 一致的；始终如一的；
words.ex: His answers are consistent with the data.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案与数据一致。
words.en: Someone who is consistent always behaves in the same way, has the same attitudes towards people or things, or achieves the same level of success in something.

words.ex: There is an inconsistency between his words and actions.
words.ex_cn: 他的言行不一致。
words.en: The quality or state of being inconsistent; lack of consistency.

words.ex: He consistently arrives at school on time.
words.ex_cn: 他一贯准时到校。
words.en: In a way that does not vary; in the same way over time.

words.ex: His answers were inconsistent.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案不一致。
words.en: If you describe someone as inconsistent, you are criticizing them for not behaving in the same way every time a similar situation occurs.

words.ex: The cheese is a derivative of milk.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪是牛奶的派生物。
words.en: A derivative is something which has been developed or obtained from something else.

words.ex: He works hard to emulate his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他努力赶上他的哥哥。
words.en: To emulate someone or something means to try to be like them or to do something in the same way that they do it.

words.ex: The child's emulation of his father made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿父亲的样子让所有人都笑了。
words.en: Emulation is the effort or desire to equal or surpass another in some achievement or quality, often through imitation.

words.ex: The child imitates her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If you imitate someone, you copy what they do or produce.

words.ex: The necklace is an imitation made of plastic.
words.ex_cn: 这条项链是用塑料做的仿制品。
words.en: An imitation of something is a copy of it.

words.tr: adj. 同等的；相等的；相当于
words.ex: Lying is tantamount to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎等于欺骗。
words.en: If you say that one thing is tantamount to a second, more serious thing, you are emphasizing how bad, unacceptable, or unfortunate the first thing is by comparing it to the second.

words.tr:
adj. 一致的；统一的；
n. 制服；
words.ex: The students wear a uniform shirt to school.
words.ex_cn: 学生们穿一致的衬衫去学校。
words.en: A uniform is a special set of clothes which some people, for example soldiers or the police, wear to work in and which some children wear at school. It is also used to describe something that is the same in all parts and does not vary.

words.ex: The paint was applied uniformly on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 油漆均匀地涂在墙上。
words.en: In a way that is the same in all cases and at all times.

words.ex: He showed conformity with the group's rules.
words.ex_cn: 他遵守了小组的规定。
words.en: Conformity is the act of matching attitudes, beliefs, and behaviors to group norms or standards.

words.ex: The music resonates with her emotions.
words.ex_cn: 音乐与她的情感产生共鸣。
words.en: If something resonates, it vibrates and produces a deep, strong sound. If a place or situation resonates, it seems full of a particular quality or feeling.

words.tr: v. 使协调一致；使和谐；配上和音
words.ex: The two singers try to harmonize their voices.
words.ex_cn: 两位歌手试图让他们的声音和谐。
words.en: If two or more things harmonize, they combine in a pleasing way, or if you harmonize them, you make them combine in a pleasing way.

words.ex: The two situations are analogous.
words.ex_cn: 这两种情况是相似的。
words.en: If one thing is analogous to another, the two things are similar in some way.

words.ex: Happy is synonymous with joyful.
words.ex_cn: 快乐与喜悦是同义的。
words.en: If you say that one thing is synonymous with another, you mean that the two things are very closely associated with each other so that one suggests the other or one cannot exist without the other.

words.ex: The scientist tried to replicate the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家试图复制这个实验。
words.en: To replicate something means to do or make something again in exactly the same way.

words.ex: The scientist did a replication of the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家重复了这个实验。
words.en: The act of copying or reproducing something.

words.tr: v. 复制；复印；再做一次；
words.ex: He duplicated the file to save a copy.
words.ex_cn: 他复制了该文件以保存一份副本。
words.en: To duplicate something means to make an exact copy of it.

words.tr:
adj. 平行的；
n. 类似的事物；
words.ex: The two lines are parallel and never meet.
words.ex_cn: 这两条线是平行的，永远不会相交。
words.en: Something that is parallel to something else is similar to it in many ways, or happens at the same time as it.

words.ex: She is flexible with her schedule.
words.ex_cn: 她的日程安排很灵活。
words.en: Able to change or be changed easily according to the situation.

words.ex: The company values flexibility in work hours.
words.ex_cn: 公司重视工作时间的灵活性。
words.en: Flexibility refers to the quality of bending easily without breaking, or the ability to be easily modified to respond to altered circumstances or conditions.

words.ex: The rules are inflexible and cannot be changed.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则是不灵活的，不能更改。
words.en: If you say that someone is inflexible, you are criticizing them because they refuse to change their mind or alter their way of doing things.

words.tr: adj. 恰当的；贴切的；关系密切的
words.ex: His comment was germane to the topic.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论与话题恰当相关。
words.en: Something that is germane to a situation or idea is connected with it in an important way.

words.ex: This room is comparatively small.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间相对较小。
words.en: In comparison with something else, especially something similar; relatively.

words.ex: The comparison of the two phones helped me decide.
words.ex_cn: 对这两部手机的比较帮助我做出了决定。
words.en: When you make a comparison, you consider two or more things and discover the differences or similarities between them.

words.ex: The two events happened simultaneously.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件同时发生了。
words.en: Happening, existing, or done at the same time.

words.tr: v. 容纳；适应；为...提供住宿；
words.ex: The hotel can accommodate 200 guests.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店能容纳200位客人。
words.en: If a building or space can accommodate someone or something, it has enough room for them.

words.tr: n. 对应物；相当之物；副本；
words.ex: The CEO's counterpart in China signed the agreement.
words.ex_cn: 中国方面的对应人物签署了协议。
words.en: Someone's or something's counterpart is another person or thing that has a similar function or position in a different place.

words.ex: The trip is contingent on the weather.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅行取决于天气情况。
words.en: A contingent event or situation depends on something else in order to happen or exist.

words.tr: n. 偶然事故；意外事件
words.ex: He saved money for a contingency.
words.ex_cn: 他存钱以备不时之需。
words.en: A contingency is an event or situation that might happen in the future, especially one that could cause problems.

words.ex: He shows adaptability when things change quickly.
words.ex_cn: 当事情快速变化时，他表现出适应能力。
words.en: The ability to adjust to new conditions or environments.

words.ex: Children are often adaptable to new environments.
words.ex_cn: 孩子通常能适应新环境。
words.en: If someone or something is adaptable, they are able to change their ideas or behaviour in order to deal with new situations.

words.ex: The plasticity of the clay made it ideal for sculpting.
words.ex_cn: 黏土的可塑性使其非常适合雕塑。
words.en: The quality of being easily shaped or molded.

words.ex: We arrived at the opportune moment, just as the meeting was starting.
words.ex_cn: 我们到达得很及时，正好会议刚开始。
words.en: If something happens at an opportune time or is opportune, it happens at the time that is most convenient for someone or most likely to lead to success.

words.ex: The team reached a consensus on the project plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队就项目计划达成了共识。
words.en: A consensus is general agreement among a group of people.

words.ex: The relevance of this topic is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这个主题的相关性是明显的。
words.en: The quality or state of being closely connected or appropriate.

words.tr: n. 无关紧要；不相关的事物；无意义的事物
words.ex: The judge dismissed the evidence as irrelevance to the case.
words.ex_cn: 法官认为该证据与案件无关紧要，予以驳回。
words.en: The quality or state of being unrelated to a matter at hand.

words.tr:
adj. 成比例的；相应的；相称的
v. 使成比例；使适应
words.ex: The punishment should be proportionate to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 惩罚应当与罪行相称。
words.en: If one thing is proportionate to another, it increases or decreases according to the changes in the other thing, and there is a sensible relationship between them.

words.ex: The rich pay disproportionately more taxes.
words.ex_cn: 富人缴纳的税不成比例地更多。
words.en: To an extent that is too large or too small in comparison with something else.

words.ex: The punishment was disproportionate to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 惩罚与罪行不成比例。
words.en: Something that is disproportionate is surprisingly large or small in comparison to something else.

words.ex: He is attuned to the needs of his students.
words.ex_cn: 他熟悉学生的需求。
words.en: If you are attuned to something, you can understand and appreciate it.

words.tr: adj. 适当的；合适的；恰当的；
words.ex: This dress is appropriate for a wedding.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子适合参加婚礼。
words.en: Something that is appropriate is suitable or acceptable for a particular situation.

words.ex: Wearing shorts to the meeting is inappropriate.
words.ex_cn: 穿短裤去参加会议是不合适的。
words.en: If you say that something is inappropriate, you are criticizing it because you think it is not suitable for a particular situation or purpose.

words.ex: The punishment was condign for the crime committed.
words.ex_cn: 这个惩罚对于所犯的罪行来说是应得的。
words.en: Deserved; appropriate; fitting.

words.tr: n. 对位法；惬意（或有趣）的对比
words.ex: The composer skillfully used counterpoint to create a complex musical texture.
words.ex_cn: 作曲家巧妙地运用复调手法创造出复杂的音乐织体。
words.en: In music, counterpoint is the relationship between two or more voices that are independent in contour and rhythm, and interdependent in harmony.

words.ex: He inured himself to the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 他让自己适应了寒冷的天气。
words.en: If you are inured to something unpleasant, you have become used to it so that it no longer affects you.

words.ex: He modulates his voice to sound calm.
words.ex_cn: 他调节自己的声音以显得平静。
words.en: To modulate means to change or adjust something, such as your voice or a piece of equipment, to achieve a desired effect or to make it suitable for a particular situation.

words.tr:
adj. 恰当的；适宜的
adv. 恰当地；适宜地
prep. 关于；至于
words.ex: Your suggestion is apropos to our current needs.
words.ex_cn: 你的建议恰好符合我们当前的需求。
words.en: If something is apropos, it is suitable in a particular situation.

chapters.name: 孤立/狭隘/不一致/排斥/不兼容

words.tr: v. 隔离；使隔热；使隔音；使绝缘
words.ex: The walls insulate the house from cold air.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁将房子与冷空气隔离开。
words.en: To insulate something means to protect it from heat, cold, noise, or electricity by covering it in a material that prevents it from passing through.

words.tr:
n. 离婚；
v. 和…离婚；
words.ex: They filed for divorce after ten years of marriage.
words.ex_cn: 他们结婚十年后申请了离婚。
words.en: Divorce is the formal ending of a marriage by law.

words.tr:
adj. 偏远的；久远的；
n. 遥控器；
words.ex: The village is in a remote area far from the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于远离城市的偏远地区。
words.en: Remote areas are far away from cities and places where most people live, and are therefore difficult to get to.

words.ex: The remoteness of the village made it hard to deliver mail.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄的遥远使得邮寄信件变得困难。
words.en: The state of being far away from other places, buildings, or people; the state of being remote.

words.tr:
adj. 本土的；
n. 土著；本地人；
words.ex: This plant is native to Australia.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物原产于澳大利亚。
words.en: A native of a particular country or region is someone who was born in that country or region.

words.tr: adj. 家庭的；国内的；驯养的；
words.ex: She prefers domestic chores over going out.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢做家务而不是外出。
words.en: Domestic means relating to the home, family, or household affairs. It can also refer to something that is made or produced within a country and not imported.

words.tr: adj. 海岛的；孤立的；思想褊狭的
words.ex: The insular village has no bridge to the mainland.
words.ex_cn: 这个海岛村庄没有桥通向大陆。
words.en: If you describe someone as insular, you are being critical of them because they are unwilling to meet new people or to consider new ideas.

words.tr: adj. 分离的； v. 脱离；拆卸；分离；“detach”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The house is detached from the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子与邻居的房子是分开的。
words.en: If someone is detached, they do not have any emotional interest in a situation and therefore can make fair decisions.

words.tr: n. 分离；拆开；支队；超然；分遣队
words.ex: The detachment of the two teams caused confusion.
words.ex_cn: 两个团队的分离造成了混乱。
