words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.ex: He is a man of great eminence in science.
words.ex_cn: 他在科学界享有很高的声望。
words.en: Eminence refers to a position of great distinction or superiority, especially in a particular field or profession.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；卓越的；出类拔萃的
words.ex: He is a pre-eminent scientist in his field.
words.ex_cn: 他是该领域最杰出的科学家。
words.en: If someone or something is pre-eminent in a group, they are more important, powerful, or capable than other people or things in the group.

words.tr: adj. 无可辩驳的；不能否认的
words.ex: The evidence is irrefutable.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If you describe something such as evidence or a fact as irrefutable, you mean that it cannot be denied or disproved.

words.tr: v. 使根深蒂固；使处于牢固地位；用壕沟围住
words.ex: The habit entrenches itself over time.
words.ex_cn: 这个习惯随着时间的推移变得根深蒂固。
words.en: To establish something very firmly so that it is very difficult to change.

words.ex: He spoke with certitude about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他对于这个答案说话时充满确信。
words.en: A feeling of being certain or convinced about something.

words.tr: adj. 无可责难的；清白无辜的
words.ex: He was blameless in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故中是无罪的。
words.en: If you say that someone is blameless, you mean that they have not done anything wrong.

words.ex: The sunset was spectacular.
words.ex_cn: 日落非常壮观。
words.en: Something that is spectacular is very impressive or dramatic.

words.ex: The team celebrated their triumph after winning the match.
words.ex_cn: 球队在赢得比赛后庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；尚未处理的；
words.ex: He is an outstanding student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名杰出的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as outstanding, you think that they are very remarkable and impressive.

words.ex: His obtuseness in social situations often led to misunderstandings.
words.ex_cn: 他在社交场合的迟钝经常导致误解。
words.en: The quality or state of being obtuse; lack of sharpness or quickness in perception or understanding.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.ex: The loud speaker is too obtrusive.
words.ex_cn: 这个扬声器太突兀了。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is obtrusive, you mean they are noticeable in an unwelcome or inappropriate way.

chapters.name: 广泛的/综合的/标准的/典型的

words.ex: The smell of flowers was pervasive in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花的香味遍布整个花园。
words.en: Something that is pervasive is present or noticeable throughout a place or thing.

words.ex: The smell of bread pervades the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫在整个厨房里。
words.en: If something pervades a place or thing, it is present throughout it.

words.ex: The teacher gave a comprehensive review before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试前给了一个全面的复习。
words.en: Something that is comprehensive includes everything that is needed or relevant.

words.ex: The report shows comprehensiveness in covering all the details.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告在涵盖所有细节方面很详尽。
words.en: The quality of being comprehensive; completeness.

words.tr: adj. 流传甚广的；分布广的；
words.ex: The flu became widespread last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天流感流传甚广。
words.en: Something that is widespread exists or happens over a large area, or to a great extent.

words.tr: adj. 广大的；广阔的；广泛的；大量的；
words.ex: He has extensive knowledge of history.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有广博的历史知识。
words.en: Something that is extensive covers a wide area or includes a lot of things.

words.ex: She has traveled extensively across Europe.
words.ex_cn: 她广泛地游历了欧洲。
words.en: Something that is extensive covers a wide range of details, ideas, or items.

words.ex: The ubiquity of smartphones makes life easier.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的普遍存在让生活更轻松。
words.en: The state or capacity of being everywhere, especially at the same time; omnipresence.

words.ex: The report gives an exhaustive list of all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告给出了所有规则的详尽列表。
words.en: If you describe a study, search, or list as exhaustive, you mean that it is very thorough and complete.

words.ex: The report was praised for its exhaustiveness.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告因其全面性而受到赞扬。
words.en: The quality of being comprehensive and thorough; completeness.

words.ex: She tried to prevail on him to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 她试图劝服他改变主意。
words.en: If a proposal, principle, or opinion prevails, it gains influence or is accepted, often after a struggle or argument.

words.tr: adj. 普遍的；流行的；盛行的；
words.ex: Smoking is prevalent in that country.
words.ex_cn: 在那个国家，吸烟很普遍。
words.en: If a condition, practice, or belief is prevalent, it is common or widespread.

words.tr: n. 普遍性；一般性；通用
words.ex: The universality of human rights is a concept that transcends national boundaries.
words.ex_cn: 人权的普遍性是一个超越国界的概念。
words.en: The quality or state of being universal; the fact of existing or being found everywhere.

words.tr: adj. （指人的行为）非典型的；非通常的；表现奇怪的
words.ex: His uncharacteristic behavior surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他那不典型的行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: If you describe something as uncharacteristic, you mean that it is not typical of the person or thing concerned.

words.tr:
n. 特点；特性；
adj. 典型的；特有的；
words.ex: Honesty is a key characteristic of a good friend.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一个好朋友的关键特点。
words.en: A characteristic is a quality or feature that is typical of someone or something.

words.tr: v. 描述…的特性；以…为特征；
words.ex: This book characterizes the hero as brave and kind.
words.ex_cn: 这本书将主人公描述为勇敢而善良的。
words.en: To describe the character or qualities of someone or something.

words.tr: n. 特性描述；人物性格塑造；
words.ex: The characterization of the hero shows his bravery.
words.ex_cn: 对英雄的特性描述展现了他勇敢的品质。
words.en: The act of describing or representing the qualities or peculiarities of a person or thing.

words.ex: She is the archetypical example of a good student.
words.ex_cn: 她是好学生的典型例子。
words.en: An archetypical example of something is the most typical or representative example of it.

words.tr: adj. 非典型的；不规则的
words.ex: He has an atypical way of solving problems.
words.ex_cn: 他解决问题的方式很不寻常。
words.en: Not representative of a type, group, or class; unusual or irregular.

words.tr: adj. 典型的；有代表性的；
words.ex: This is a typical example of a sunny day.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个晴天的典型例子。
words.en: You use typical to describe someone or something that shows the most usual characteristics of a particular type of person or thing, and is therefore a good example of that type.

words.ex: This experiment is a paradigm of scientific method.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验是科学方法的范例。
words.en: A paradigm is a model or pattern that is considered to be a typical example of something.

words.tr: adj. 纵聚合关系的；典范的
words.ex: The paradigmatic relationship between words shows how they can replace each other in a sentence.
words.ex_cn: 词语之间的纵聚合关系表明它们如何在句子中相互替换。
words.en: If something is paradigmatic, it is an example or model of something.

words.tr:
adj. 有全权的
n. 全权代表
words.ex: The plenipotentiary was given authority to negotiate the treaty.
words.ex_cn: 全权代表被赋予了谈判条约的权力。
words.en: A plenipotentiary is a person, especially a diplomat, who is given full powers by their government to make decisions or take action on their behalf.

words.ex: The treaty will demarcate the new borders between the two countries.
words.ex_cn: 条约将划定两国之间的新边界。
words.en: To set the boundaries or limits of something.

words.ex: The fence shows the demarcation between the two yards.
words.ex_cn: 这道篱笆标明了两个院子的界限。
words.en: The act or process of marking the limits or boundaries of something.

words.tr: n. （有条件的）投降；投降条约
words.ex: The capitulation of the city marked the end of the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市的投降标志着战争的结束。
words.en: The act of surrendering or yielding under specified conditions; a document containing the terms of surrender.

words.tr: n. 概括，重述要点；（生育、生长中对进化等过程的）重演；（尤指奏鸣曲形式中的）再现部
words.ex: The professor's lecture ended with a recapitulation of the main points.
words.ex_cn: 教授的讲座以概括主要观点结束。
words.en: A recapitulation is a summary or brief restatement of the main points of something, especially at the end of a speech, lecture, or piece of writing.

words.tr: adj. 作为象征的；作为标志的；
words.ex: The dove is emblematic of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征。
words.en: If something is emblematic of a particular quality or situation, it is considered to be typical or representative of it.

words.ex: After the chaos, the return to normalcy was a relief.
words.ex_cn: 在混乱之后，恢复正常是一种解脱。
words.en: The state of being normal; the condition of being usual or typical.

words.tr: adj. 典范的；可做模范的；惩戒性的
words.ex: He is an exemplary student who always finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名模范学生，总是完成作业。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as exemplary, you think they are extremely good and suitable to be copied by other people.

words.ex: The tribe's totemic symbols were carved into the wooden poles.
words.ex_cn: 部落的图腾符号被雕刻在木柱上。
words.en: Relating to or resembling a totem or totems.

words.ex: The manager will delegate the task to her assistant.
words.ex_cn: 经理将把这个任务委派给她的助手。
words.en: A delegate is a person who is chosen or elected to vote or make decisions on behalf of a group of people, especially at a conference or a meeting. As a verb, to delegate means to give a task or responsibility to another person, especially someone who is less senior than you.

words.tr: adj. 典范的；典型的；标准的
words.ex: The book uses a canonical example to explain the rule.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使用一个标准例子来解释这个规则。
words.en: According to, ordered by, or conforming to a church canon or canons.

words.tr: adj. 不快乐的；忧郁的；阴暗的
words.ex: The room was cheerless and dark.
words.ex_cn: 房间阴暗而无生气。
words.en: If you describe a place or a thing as cheerless, you mean that it is dull and depressing.

words.ex: The crowd cheered when the team scored.
words.ex_cn: 当球队得分时，观众欢呼起来。
words.en: If people cheer, they shout loudly to show their approval or to encourage someone who is doing something such as taking part in a game.

words.tr: adj. 慵懒的；没精打采的；懒洋洋的
words.ex: He felt lethargic after eating too much.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多后感到昏昏欲睡。
words.en: If you are lethargic, you do not have much energy or enthusiasm.

words.tr: v. 使麻痹；使瘫痪；使无效；使停止活动
words.ex: The accident paralyzed his leg.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他的腿瘫痪了。
words.en: If someone is paralyzed by an accident or an illness, they have no feeling in their body, or in part of their body, and are unable to move.

words.ex: His indolence at work was becoming a serious issue.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中的懒散正成为一个严重的问题。
words.en: Indolence is the state of being lazy or not wanting to do any work.

words.tr: adj. 昏昏欲睡的；困倦的；催眠的
words.ex: The somnolent boy nodded off during class.
words.ex_cn: 那个昏昏欲睡的男孩在课堂上睡着了。
words.en: If you are somnolent, you feel sleepy.

words.tr: adj. 延长的；拖延的；持久的
words.ex: The meeting was protracted because they could not agree.
words.ex_cn: 会议拖得很长，因为他们无法达成一致。
words.en: Something that is protracted lasts for a long time, especially longer than usual or longer than you hoped.

words.ex: He answered the question unwillingly.
words.ex_cn: 他不情愿地回答了问题。
words.en: In a way that shows you do not want to do something.

words.ex: He answered the question unwillingly.
words.ex_cn: 他不情愿地回答了问题。
words.en: In a way that shows you do not want to do something.

words.tr: adj. 酸的； 苦涩的；尖刻的
words.ex: The lemon juice had an acerbic taste.
words.ex_cn: 柠檬汁有酸味。
words.en: If you say something acerbic, or harshly bitter, you are being sharply critical or sarcastic.

words.tr:
adj. 苛刻的；尖刻的
v. 损伤；伤害；“scathe”的现在分词
words.ex: The critic wrote a scathing review of the movie.
words.ex_cn: 评论家写了一篇尖刻的电影评论。
words.en: If you say that someone is being scathing about something, you mean that they are being very critical of it.

words.ex: Her mordancy in criticism was often misunderstood as cruelty.
words.ex_cn: 她批评中的尖酸常常被误解为残忍。
words.en: The quality of being sharply critical or sarcastic.

words.tr: adj. 刻薄的；尖刻的；恶意的
words.ex: His vitriolic words hurt everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他刻薄的话伤害了房间里所有人。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as vitriolic, you disapprove of it because it is full of bitterness and hate, and so causes a lot of distress and pain.

words.ex: Their argument was acrimonious and lasted all night.
words.ex_cn: 他们的争论很尖刻，持续了一整晚。
words.en: If you say that an argument or conversation is acrimonious, you mean that it is bitter and angry because the people involved disagree with each other.

words.ex: The lemon juice is acidic.
words.ex_cn: 柠檬汁是酸的。
words.en: Something that is acidic contains acid or has a pH of less than 7.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；造成伤害的
words.ex: Smoking has deleterious effects on your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is deleterious has a harmful effect on something, especially on a person's health.

words.ex: He has a rare malady that doctors are trying to cure.
words.ex_cn: 他患有一种罕见的疾病，医生们正在努力治疗。
words.en: A malady is a disease or illness.

words.ex: His egregious mistake cost the team the game.
words.ex_cn: 他严重的错误让球队输掉了比赛。
words.en: An egregious error or failure is extremely bad and noticeable.

words.ex: The chemicals are hazardous to health.
words.ex_cn: 这些化学物质对健康有危险。
words.en: Something that is hazardous is dangerous, especially to people's health or safety.

words.tr: adj. 毁灭性的； v. “devastate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The earthquake caused devastating damage to the city.
words.ex_cn: 地震对这座城市造成了毁灭性的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as devastating, you are emphasizing that it is very harmful or damaging.

words.ex: The storm caused disastrous damage to the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴给村庄造成了灾难性的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as disastrous, you mean that it is very unfortunate or unsuccessful.

words.tr:
adj. 有害的；恶意的
v. 中伤；污蔑
words.ex: The virus is malign and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒是有害的，并且传播迅速。
words.en: If you malign someone, you say unpleasant and untrue things about them. If something is malign, it is harmful or evil.

words.tr: adj. 令人厌恶的；令人不愉快的
words.ex: The noisome smell made everyone leave the room.
words.ex_cn: 那股难闻的气味让所有人都离开了房间。
words.en: If you describe something as noisome, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant, especially because it has a very strong or bad smell.

words.tr: adj. 恶臭的；有恶臭的；有臭味的
words.ex: The malodorous garbage was attracting flies.
words.ex_cn: 那堆有恶臭的垃圾招来了苍蝇。
words.en: Having a very unpleasant smell.

words.tr: adj. 猥亵的；淫秽的；诲淫的；好色的
words.ex: The novel was criticized for its salacious content.
words.ex_cn: 这部小说因其淫秽内容而受到批评。
words.en: If you describe something such as a book or joke as salacious, you think that it deals with sexual matters in an unnecessarily detailed way.

words.tr:
adj. 狡猾的；奸诈的；巧妙的
n. 奸诈；狡猾
words.ex: The cunning fox tricked the chicken.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸骗了鸡。
words.en: Someone who is cunning is clever and good at deceiving others in order to get what they want.

words.ex: The refugees lived in abject poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这些难民过着凄惨的贫困生活。
words.en: Abject means extremely bad, unpleasant, and degrading.

words.tr: adj. 卑鄙的；污秽的；肮脏的
words.ex: He made a sordid deal to cheat his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一笔卑鄙的交易来欺骗他的朋友。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as sordid, you mean that it is very immoral or dishonest.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；起破坏作用的
n. 腐蚀性物品
words.ex: The acid is corrosive and can damage metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种酸具有腐蚀性，会损坏金属。
words.en: A corrosive substance is able to destroy solid materials by a chemical reaction.

words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；恶性的；致命的
words.ex: Smoking is a pernicious habit.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是一种有害的习惯。
words.en: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.ex: His provocative words made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 他挑衅的话让所有人都生气了。
words.en: If you describe something as provocative, you mean that it is intended to make people react angrily or argue against it.

words.tr: adj. 好争吵的；有争议的
words.ex: The plan is contentious because many people disagree.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划有争议，因为很多人不同意。
words.en: If you describe something as contentious, you mean that it is the subject of intense argument and disagreement.

words.ex: The contentiousness of the issue prevented any agreement.
words.ex_cn: 这一问题的争论性阻碍了任何协议的达成。
words.en: The quality of being contentious; argumentativeness.

words.ex: The adverse weather delayed the flight.
words.ex_cn: 不利的天气延误了航班。
words.en: If something is adverse, it is harmful or unfavorable.

words.ex: He faced his adversary in the final match.
words.ex_cn: 他在决赛中对阵对手。
words.en: An adversary is someone who you are competing with, or who is opposing you or what you are trying to do.

words.ex: The two lawyers gave adversarial arguments in court.
words.ex_cn: 两位律师在法庭上提出了对抗性的论点。
words.en: Involving or characterized by conflict or opposition.

words.ex: He gave an antagonistic reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了敌对的答复。
words.en: If someone is antagonistic to someone or something, they show hatred or opposition towards them.

words.tr: n. 对抗；对立；敌对状态（行为）
words.ex: There is antagonism between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居之间有敌意。
words.en: Antagonism is a strong feeling of dislike or opposition towards someone or something.

words.ex: There was clear hostility between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间明显存在敌意。
words.en: Hostility is unfriendly or aggressive behaviour towards people or ideas.

words.tr: adj. 好战的；好斗的；爱滋事的
words.ex: He is pugnacious and always argues with his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他好斗，总是和同学争吵。
words.en: Someone who is pugnacious is eager to argue or fight.

words.ex: His pugnacity made him argue with everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的好斗性格让他和每个人争论。
words.en: Pugnacity is the quality of being eager or quick to argue, quarrel, or fight.

words.tr:
adj. 交战的；寻衅的；好战的
n. 交战国；交战团体
words.ex: The two belligerent nations signed a peace treaty.
words.ex_cn: 这两个交战国家签署了和平条约。
words.en: A belligerent person or country is aggressive and eager to fight.

words.ex: The declaration of belligerency marked the official start of hostilities between the two nations.
words.ex_cn: 宣布交战状态标志着两国之间敌对行动的正式开始。
words.en: The state or quality of being belligerent; aggressive or warlike behavior.

words.ex: The company's policies were inimical to the interests of its employees.
words.ex_cn: 公司的政策对员工的利益是有害的。
words.en: If one thing is inimical to another, it prevents the second thing from happening or being successful, or it is harmful to it.

words.ex: He contends that education is the key to success.
words.ex_cn: 他主张教育是成功的关键。
words.en: If you contend with someone or contend with something, you have to deal with a difficult situation or problem. If you contend that something is true, you state or argue that it is true.

words.tr: adj. 抱怨的；爱发牢骚的
words.ex: She had a querulous tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种爱发牢骚的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as querulous, you mean that they complain about things in a rather bad-tempered way.

words.tr: adj. 爱发号施令的；多管闲事的
words.ex: The officious clerk refused to help unless I filled out another form.
words.ex_cn: 那位爱多管闲事的职员拒绝帮忙，除非我再填一份表格。
words.en: If you describe someone as officious, you are critical of them because they are eager to tell people what to do when you think they should not.

words.tr: adj. 再三要求的；纠缠不休的
words.ex: He was importunate in asking for money.
words.ex_cn: 他不停地要求给钱。
words.en: persistent to the point of annoyance

words.tr:
v. 发牢骚；抱怨；轰鸣
n. 怨言；牢骚；轰隆声
words.ex: He grumbles when he has to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不早起时就会抱怨。
words.en: If someone grumbles, they complain about something in a bad-tempered way.

words.tr: n. 意见分歧；纠纷；争执
words.ex: The team had dissension about the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队对新计划有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement among people or groups, especially when it leads to conflict.

words.tr: adj. 好战凶猛的；寻衅的；言词刻毒的
words.ex: He gave a truculent reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了好斗的答复。
words.en: If you say that someone is truculent, you mean that they are bad-tempered and aggressive.

words.ex: He spoke with animus against his rival.
words.ex_cn: 他带着敌意谈论他的对手。
words.en: A feeling of strong dislike or hatred.

words.tr: adj. 攻击性的；有进取心的；侵略性的；
words.ex: The dog showed aggressive behavior toward strangers.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗对陌生人表现出攻击性行为。
words.en: An aggressive person or animal has a quality of anger and determination that makes them ready to attack others.

words.ex: He must confront his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: If you confront a difficult situation or issue, you accept the fact that it exists and try to deal with it.

words.tr:
n. 挑战；
v. 提出挑战；
words.ex: Climbing that mountain is a big challenge.
words.ex_cn: 爬那座山是一个巨大的挑战。
words.en: A challenge is something new and difficult which requires great effort and determination.

words.tr: adj. 有挑战性的； v. 提出挑战；“challenge”的现在分词；
words.ex: The math problem was challenging.
words.ex_cn: 这道数学题很有挑战性。
words.en: If you describe something as challenging, you mean that it tests your ability and determination and that you need to work hard to deal with it or achieve it.

words.tr:
n. 纠纷；争端；
v. 对（某事）有异议；
words.ex: The dispute between the two neighbors was about the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间的纠纷是关于篱笆的。
words.en: A dispute is a disagreement or argument about something important.

words.tr: adj. 无可置辩的；无异议的；
words.ex: He is the undisputed champion of the tournament.
words.ex_cn: 他是这场比赛无可置辩的冠军。
words.en: If you describe a fact or opinion as undisputed, you mean that it is accepted as true or correct by everyone.

words.ex: He is skeptical about the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个新计划持怀疑态度。
words.en: If you are skeptical about something, you have doubts about it.

words.tr: n. 怀疑论者；怀疑宗教主张的人；无神论者
words.ex: He is a skeptic about new health claims.
words.ex_cn: 他对新的健康说法持怀疑态度。
words.en: A skeptic is a person who questions the validity or authenticity of something purporting to be factual.

words.ex: He showed skepticism about the new claim.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个新说法持怀疑态度。
words.en: Skepticism is a questioning attitude or doubt towards one or more items of putative knowledge or belief.

words.tr:
n. 疑问；疑惑；
v. 怀疑；拿不准；
words.ex: I have doubt about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 我对这个答案有疑问。
words.en: If you have doubt or doubts about something, you feel uncertain about it and do not know whether it is true or possible. If you say that something is beyond doubt, you mean that it is definitely true.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；怀疑的；拿不准的；
words.ex: The deal seemed dubious to me.
words.ex_cn: 这个交易在我看来很可疑。
words.en: If you describe something as dubious, you mean that you do not consider it to be completely honest, safe, or reliable.

words.tr: n. 踌躇；不果断；游移不定
words.ex: He shows vacillation when choosing his favorite color.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择最喜欢的颜色时犹豫不决。
words.en: If you vacillate between two alternatives or choices, you keep changing your mind.

words.ex: I suspect it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我猜想明天会下雨。
words.en: If you suspect someone of doing something wrong or dishonest, you believe that they have done it, although you have no proof.

words.ex: He wavers when choosing between two jobs.
words.ex_cn: 他在两个工作之间摇摆不定。
words.en: If you waver, you cannot decide about something or you are uncertain about what you should do.

words.tr: adj. 不动摇的；坚定的；始终如一的
words.ex: She had an unwavering commitment to her goals.
words.ex_cn: 她对她的目标有着坚定的承诺。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude, feeling, or way of behaving as unwavering, you mean that it is strong and firm and does not weaken.

words.tr: adj. 暂定的；不确定的；试验性的；
words.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next week.
words.ex_cn: 我们制定了一个下周见面的暂定计划。
words.en: If you make a tentative suggestion or plan, you make it without being sure that it is right or acceptable.

words.tr:
v. 摇摆；摇动；
n. 影响；支配；
words.ex: The tree branches sway in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 树的枝条在风中摇摆。
words.en: To sway means to move slowly or rhythmically backwards and forwards or from side to side. It can also mean to influence someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 无决断的；犹豫不决的
words.ex: He was irresolute about which job to accept.
words.ex_cn: 他对于接受哪份工作犹豫不决。
words.en: If someone is irresolute, they are uncertain about what to do or are unable to make decisions.

words.tr: n. 优柔寡断；犹豫不决
words.ex: He showed irresolution when choosing his major.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择专业时表现出优柔寡断。
words.en: Irresolution is the state of being uncertain about what to do or not being able to decide quickly.

words.tr: n. 优柔寡断；犹豫不决
words.ex: He showed irresolution when choosing his major.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择专业时表现出优柔寡断。
words.en: Irresolution is the state of being uncertain about what to do or not being able to decide quickly.

words.ex: He continually checks his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他不停地查看手机。
words.en: If something happens continually, it happens without stopping or happening repeatedly over a period of time.

words.ex: The rain was continuous all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨一整天都在下个不停。
words.en: Something that is continuous happens or exists without stopping or being interrupted.

words.tr: adv. 连续地；不断地；连续不断地；
words.ex: The machine works continuously without stopping.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器连续工作，不停止。
words.en: Without interruption; constantly.

words.ex: The rain persisted all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨持续了一整天。
words.en: If you persist in doing something, you continue to do it even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.ex: He made a persistent effort to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他持续努力学习英语。
words.en: Continuing firmly or obstinately in a course of action in spite of difficulty or opposition.

words.ex: His persistence helped him pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他的坚持让他通过了考试。
words.en: Persistence is the determination to do something even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.ex: We need sustainable energy to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要可持续的能源来保护环境。
words.en: If something is sustainable, it can be maintained or continued at a certain rate or level without causing damage or depletion of resources.

words.ex: The factory uses unsustainable methods to save money.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂为了省钱而使用不可持续的方法。
words.en: If something is unsustainable, it cannot continue at the same rate or in the same way.

words.ex: The city plans for sustainability by using solar energy.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市通过使用太阳能来实现可持续性。
words.en: Sustainability is the ability to maintain or support a process continuously over time. In the context of environmental science, it refers to the avoidance of the depletion of natural resources in order to maintain an ecological balance.

words.tr: v. 使（尤指不好的情形、体系、信仰）持续、长存；
words.ex: The system perpetuates inequality among the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这个体系使贫困人群的不平等持续存在。
words.en: To perpetuate something means to cause it to continue, especially for a long time.

words.tr: n. 永恒，不朽；不受时间影响
words.ex: The song has a timelessness that moves everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌有一种永恒的魅力，打动了每个人。
words.en: The quality of being unaffected by the passage of time or changes in fashion; eternal.

words.ex: The teacher gave timely help when I was stuck.
words.ex_cn: 当我遇到困难时，老师及时提供了帮助。
words.en: done or occurring at a favorable or useful time; opportune.

words.ex: The steps must be followed in sequential order.
words.ex_cn: 这些步骤必须按顺序进行。
words.en: Sequential means relating to or following in a sequence.

words.ex: The stars seem eternal in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中的星星看起来是永久的。
words.en: If something is eternal, it lasts forever.

words.ex: The concept of eternality is often discussed in philosophy and religion.
words.ex_cn: 永恒的概念经常在哲学和宗教中被讨论。
words.en: The state or quality of being eternal; endless or infinite duration.

words.ex: He made a permanent change to his lifestyle.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的生活方式做出了永久的改变。
words.en: Something that is permanent exists or happens all the time, or exists for a long time without changing.

words.ex: The effects of the medication are impermanent.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物的效果是暂时的。
words.en: Something that is impermanent does not last forever or for a very long time.

words.ex: Some people believe in immortality after death.
words.ex_cn: 有些人相信死后会有永生。
words.en: The state of being able to live or last forever.

words.ex: The survival of the animals depends on the weather.
words.ex_cn: 这些动物的生存取决于天气。
words.en: The state or fact of continuing to live or exist, typically in spite of an accident, ordeal, or difficult circumstances.

words.ex: His steadfastness never changed, even when things were hard.
words.ex_cn: 即使情况艰难，他的坚定从未改变。
words.en: The quality of being resolutely or dutifully firm and unwavering.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；朝生暮死的
words.ex: The flowers are ephemeral and last only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是短暂的，只持续一天。
words.en: Something that is ephemeral lasts for only a very short time.

words.ex: The ephemera lived only one day.
words.ex_cn: 蜉蝣只活了一天。
words.en: Ephemera refers to things that exist or are used or enjoyed for only a short time.

words.tr: n. 朝生暮死，短命的事物；无常的事物
words.ex: The ephemerality of happiness makes it precious.
words.ex_cn: 幸福的短暂性让它变得珍贵。
words.en: The quality or state of being ephemeral; something that lasts for a very short time.

words.ex: He makes occasional visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他偶尔去看望祖父母。
words.en: Occasional means happening or done sometimes, but not regularly or often.

words.ex: I occasionally walk my dog in the park.
words.ex_cn: 我偶尔在公园遛狗。
words.en: If something happens occasionally, it happens sometimes, but not regularly or often.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；瞬间的；刹那间的
words.ex: The light made a momentary flash.
words.ex_cn: 灯光闪了一下，但只持续了一瞬间。
words.en: lasting for a very short time

words.ex: He waited for a moment before speaking.
words.ex_cn: 他等了一会儿才开口。
words.en: A moment is a very short period of time.

words.tr: adj. 很快消失的；渐消散的；短暂的
words.ex: The evanescent mist disappeared at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 那消散的薄雾在日出时消失了。
words.en: Something that is evanescent quickly disappears or fades away.

words.tr: adj. 不定时发生的；时有时无的；零星的
words.ex: He makes sporadic visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他时不时去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places; scattered or isolated

words.tr: adv. 间断发生地；零星地
words.ex: He visits his grandma sporadically.
words.ex_cn: 他偶尔去看望奶奶。
words.en: If something happens sporadically, it happens occasionally and not regularly or continuously.

words.ex: The joy was transient, like a brief smile.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是短暂的，像一个短暂的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as transient, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

words.ex: The transience of life reminds us to cherish every moment.
words.ex_cn: 生命的短暂提醒我们要珍惜每一刻。
words.en: The state or fact of lasting only for a short time; transitoriness.

words.ex: He took a temporary job during summer.
words.ex_cn: 他在暑假期间做了一份短暂的工作。
words.en: Something that is temporary lasts for only a limited time.

words.tr: adj. 插曲般的；由松散片段组成的；不定期发生的；
words.ex: The movie has an episodic structure, with each scene telling a small story.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影具有插曲般的结构，每个场景讲述一个小故事。
words.en: An episodic piece of writing or film consists of a series of separate events or episodes that are linked together.

words.ex: The impermanence of life teaches us to be kind.
words.ex_cn: 生命的无常教会我们善良。
words.en: The state or fact of lasting for only a limited period of time.

words.ex: The origin of this tradition is unknown.
words.ex_cn: 这个传统的起源不明。
words.en: The origin of something is the point or place where it begins, or the cause from which it arises.

words.ex: His painting shows great originality.
words.ex_cn: 他的画作展现了极大的独创性。
words.en: The quality of being new and original in a way that is not derived from something else.

words.tr: n. 创作者；发起人；创始人
words.ex: He is the originator of this idea.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个想法的提出者。
words.en: The person who creates or starts something, especially a new idea or way of doing something.

words.ex: This tradition originates from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这个传统起源于古代。
words.en: To originate means to have a specific beginning or to start something.

words.tr:
adj. 原来的；有创造性的；原版的；新颖的；
n. 原件；原稿；
words.ex: This is the original book I bought last year.
words.ex_cn: 这是我去年买的那本原版书。
words.en: An original piece of writing or music was written recently and has not been published or performed before.

words.ex: They established a new school in the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们在村里建立了一所新学校。
words.en: To set up or create something, such as an organization or a system, on a firm or permanent basis.

words.ex: He will initiate a new project next week.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下周发起一个新项目。
words.en: To initiate something means to start it or cause it to happen.

words.tr:
adj. 最初的；开始的；
n. 首字母；
words.ex: This is the initial plan for the project.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个项目的最初计划。
words.en: The first letter of a name or word, used to represent the whole name or word.

words.ex: Initially, he didn't like the job.
words.ex_cn: 最初，他不喜欢这份工作。
words.en: At the beginning; at first.

words.ex: We derive the answer from the formula.
words.ex_cn: 我们从公式中得到答案。
words.en: If you derive something such as pleasure or benefit from a person or from something, you get it from them.

words.ex: Five apples constitute a basket.
words.ex_cn: 五个苹果构成一篮子。
words.en: If something constitutes a particular thing, it can be regarded as being that thing.

words.ex: Poverty can engender crime.
words.ex_cn: 贫困会引起犯罪。
words.en: To cause a feeling, situation, or condition to exist.

words.ex: The foundation gives money to poor students.
words.ex_cn: 这个基金会向贫困学生提供资金。
words.en: The foundation of something such as a belief or way of life is the things on which it is based.

words.ex: The project began at its inception.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目从开始时就启动了。
words.en: The inception of something is the start or beginning of it.

words.ex: The class will commence at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 课程将在上午9点开始。
words.en: To begin something; to start.

words.ex: The provenance of this ancient vase is unknown.
words.ex_cn: 这个古花瓶的起源未知。
words.en: The place of origin or earliest known history of something.

words.ex: The song evokes happy memories of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌唤起了对童年的美好回忆。
words.en: To evoke a particular memory, idea, emotion, or response means to cause it to occur.

words.tr: adj. 互相依赖的；相倚的；
words.ex: The two countries are interdependent in trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在贸易上互相依赖。
words.en: If two or more things are interdependent, they depend on each other.

words.ex: He is a dependable friend who always helps.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个可靠的朋友，总是提供帮助。
words.en: Someone or something that is dependable can be relied on to do what you need or expect.

words.ex: Children show dependence on their parents.
words.ex_cn: 孩子对父母有依赖。
words.en: The state of relying on or being controlled by someone or something else.

words.tr:
adj. 依靠的；依赖的；
n. 受赡养者；
words.ex: The child is dependent on his parents for food.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子依靠父母提供食物。
words.en: A dependent person or thing is one that needs the support of another person or thing in order to exist or be successful.

words.ex: The country gained independence in 1960.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在1960年获得了独立。
words.en: Independence is the freedom from control or influence of others, allowing one to make decisions and act on one's own.

words.ex: He tries to synthesize ideas from different books.
words.ex_cn: 他试图综合来自不同书籍的想法。
words.en: To synthesize means to combine different ideas, influences, or objects into a new whole, or to produce a substance by a chemical reaction in plants or animals.

words.tr: adj. 无鉴别力的；不加区别的
words.ex: He is undiscriminating in his choice of friends.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择朋友时不分好坏。
words.en: If you describe someone as undiscriminating, you mean that they do not judge carefully or do not have good taste.

words.tr: adj. 不加选择的；不加区别的；
words.ex: The bombing was indiscriminate and hurt many civilians.
words.ex_cn: 这次轰炸是不加选择的，伤害了许多平民。
words.en: If you describe an action as indiscriminate, you are critical of it because it does not involve any careful thought or choice.

words.ex: Friendship needs reciprocity to last.
words.ex_cn: 友谊需要相互性才能持久。
words.en: A situation in which two people, countries, etc. help each other or behave in the same way to each other.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

words.tr:
adj. 集体的；
n. 集体；
words.ex: The collective decision was made by all members.
words.ex_cn: 这个集体决定是由所有成员做出的。
words.en: done or shared by all members of a group of people

words.tr: adv. 共同地；集体地；总体地；
words.ex: The team worked collectively to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队共同合作完成了项目。
words.en: In a way that is done or shared by all members of a group of people.

words.tr: v. 聚合；合并；长到一起
words.ex: The small ponds coalesce into a large lake.
words.ex_cn: 小池塘合并成一个大湖。
words.en: If two or more things coalesce, they come together and form a single group or system.

words.ex: The convergent series gets closer to a final number.
words.ex_cn: 这个会聚级数逐渐接近一个最终数值。
words.en: Convergent refers to the process or state of coming together or moving toward union or uniformity, especially in the context of ideas, cultures, or scientific phenomena.

words.ex: They mutually agreed to end the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此同意结束争斗。
words.en: In a way that involves shared feelings or actions between two or more people or things.

words.ex: He conflates happiness with wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他把幸福和财富混为一谈。
words.en: To combine two or more things into one, especially in a way that is confusing or misleading.

words.ex: The dentist used an amalgam to fill the cavity.
words.ex_cn: 牙医用汞合金填补了蛀牙。
words.en: An amalgam is a mixture of mercury and another metal, especially one used by dentists to fill holes in teeth. It can also refer to a mixture of different things.

words.ex: The child was compliant and followed all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子很顺从，遵守了所有规则。
words.en: If someone or something is compliant, they act in accordance with rules, standards, or laws.

words.ex: Running a business entails hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经营企业必然需要努力工作。
words.en: If one thing entails another, it involves it or causes it.

words.tr: v. 使牵连其中；涉及；暗示；指明起因
words.ex: The evidence may implicate him in the crime.
words.ex_cn: 证据可能使他牵连进这起犯罪中。
words.en: To show or suggest that someone is involved in something illegal or morally wrong.

words.ex: This rule pertains to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If one thing pertains to another, it relates, belongs, or applies to it.

words.tr: adj. 有共同边界的； 毗连的
words.ex: The two regions are coterminous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个区域是边界相连的。
words.en: Having the same boundaries or limits; sharing a common border.

words.ex: The two teams showed synergy when they finished the project early.
words.ex_cn: 当这两个团队提前完成项目时，展现了协同效应。
words.en: The interaction or cooperation of two or more organizations, substances, or other agents to produce a combined effect greater than the sum of their separate effects.

words.ex: The new plan incorporates feedback from students.
words.ex_cn: 新计划包含了学生的反馈。
words.en: If one thing incorporates another thing, it includes the other thing.

words.tr: adj. 共栖的；共生的；互惠互利的；
words.ex: The clownfish and the sea anemone have a symbiotic relationship.
words.ex_cn: 小丑鱼和海葵有共栖关系。
words.en: Involving interaction between two different organisms living in close physical association, typically to the advantage of both.

words.ex: The two particles show quantum entanglement.
words.ex_cn: 这两个粒子表现出量子纠缠。
words.en: An entanglement is a complicated or difficult relationship or situation.

words.tr: v. 体现；使具体化；包含
words.ex: He embodies kindness and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他体现了善良和耐心。
words.en: To embody means to represent a quality or an idea exactly; to include or contain something.

chapters.name: 功效/有效/胜任/有益于/解决

words.tr:
v. 有益于；有助于；
n. 利益；好处；
words.ex: Exercise benefits your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼有益于你的健康。
words.en: A benefit is something that helps you or improves your life in some way.

words.ex: Eating vegetables is beneficial to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吃蔬菜对你的健康有益。
words.en: Promoting or enhancing well-being; advantageous.

words.ex: The doctor showed beneficence by helping the poor patient for free.
words.ex_cn: 医生通过免费帮助贫困病人展现了仁慈。
words.en: Beneficence refers to the quality or state of doing or producing good; active kindness or charity.

words.tr: adj. 强健的；强壮的；结实的；
words.ex: The dog is robust and runs every day.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗很强健，每天跑步。
words.en: Strong and healthy; vigorous. (of an object) sturdy in construction.

words.ex: This medicine is effective against colds.
words.ex_cn: 这种药对感冒有效。
words.en: Something that is effective works well and produces the results that were intended.

words.ex: She completed the task effectively.
words.ex_cn: 她有效地完成了任务。
words.en: In a way that produces the intended result or a successful outcome.

words.tr: adj. 无效果的；不起作用的；不奏效的；
words.ex: The medicine was ineffective against the cold.
words.ex_cn: 这种药对感冒无效。
words.en: If someone or something is ineffective, they do not achieve the intended result.

words.ex: His competence in math helped him solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学方面的能力帮助他解决了这个问题。
words.en: Competence is the ability to do something well or efficiently.

words.ex: His incompetence caused the project to fail.
words.ex_cn: 他的无能力导致项目失败。
words.en: If you refer to someone's incompetence, you are criticizing them because they are unable to do their job or a task properly.

words.ex: The teacher will determine the winner of the contest.
words.ex_cn: 老师将确定比赛的获胜者。
words.en: If you determine something, you decide it or settle it.

words.ex: He predetermines the outcome before the game starts.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛开始前就决定了结果。
words.en: To decide or settle (something) in advance.

words.ex: He uses an efficient way to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种高效的方法解决数学问题。
words.en: If something or someone is efficient, they are able to do tasks successfully, without wasting time or energy.

words.ex: He works efficiently to finish his tasks.
words.ex_cn: 他高效地完成任务。
words.en: If you do something efficiently, you do it in a way that wastes no time, money, or energy.

words.ex: The new machine improves the efficiency of production.
words.ex_cn: 这台新机器提高了生产的效率。
words.en: Efficiency is the ability to do something or produce something without wasting materials, time, or energy.

words.ex: He thinks this new pill is a panacea for all diseases.
words.ex_cn: 他认为这种新药是治百病的万应药。
words.en: A panacea is a remedy for all diseases or ills.

words.tr: adj. 尖锐的；有力的；精辟的
words.ex: His trenchant criticism left no room for doubt.
words.ex_cn: 他尖锐的批评让人没有怀疑的余地。
words.en: If you say that someone's speech or writing is trenchant, you mean that it is very clear and effective, often in criticizing something.

words.ex: His trenchancy made the truth clear.
words.ex_cn: 他的尖锐言辞让真相变得清晰。
words.en: If you say that someone's speech or writing is trenchant, you mean that it is very clear, effective, and forceful.

words.ex: This medicine is efficacious for colds.
words.ex_cn: 这种药对感冒有效。
words.en: An efficacious method or treatment is one that has the ability to produce a desired effect or result.

words.ex: The efficacy of the medicine is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物的效果是明显的。
words.en: The ability to produce a desired or intended result.

words.tr:
adj. 预防性的
n. 预防剂；避孕用品
words.ex: He took a prophylactic pill before traveling.
words.ex_cn: 他旅行前吃了一颗预防药。
words.en: A prophylactic is a measure taken to prevent disease or another unwanted outcome.

words.ex: A quiet room is conducive to studying.
words.ex_cn: 安静的房间有助于学习。
words.en: If one thing is conducive to another thing, it makes the other thing likely to happen.

words.ex: The curative treatment helped him recover quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种医疗治疗帮助他迅速康复。
words.en: Curative means having the ability to cure or heal, especially of a disease or medical condition.

words.ex: The doctor suggested a natural remedy for the cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议了一种治疗感冒的天然疗法。
words.en: A remedy is a cure or a way of making something better.

words.ex: The experience was a salutary lesson in the importance of preparation.
words.ex_cn: 这次经历是一个关于准备重要性的有益教训。
words.en: A salutary experience or warning is one that has a good effect or influence, especially by showing you the bad results of a particular action or behaviour.

words.tr: n. 补药；滋补品；奎宁水
words.ex: He drank a tonic to feel better.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了一杯滋补剂来感觉好些。
words.en: A tonic is a medicine that makes you feel stronger, healthier, and less tired.

words.tr: adj. 有效率的；认真的；有条理的
words.ex: She gave a businesslike reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 她对这个问题给出了一个高效的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone's approach as businesslike, you mean that they deal with things in an efficient way without wasting time.

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.tr: v. 参与；从事；吸引；与…建立密切关系；
words.ex: He engages in community volunteer work.
words.ex_cn: 他参与社区志愿工作。
words.en: To engage means to occupy, attract, or involve someone or oneself in a particular activity or situation.

words.ex: His recipe for success is hard work and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的秘诀是努力工作和耐心。
words.en: A recipe is a list of ingredients and a set of instructions that tell you how to cook something.

words.ex: He resolved the problem with a simple plan.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个简单的计划解决了问题。
words.en: If you resolve to do something, you make a firm decision to do it.

words.tr: adj. 有益健康的；环境宜人的
words.ex: The air in the mountains is salubrious.
words.ex_cn: 山里的空气有益健康。
words.en: A salubrious place is pleasant, healthy, and good for you.

words.ex: He overcame his fear of speaking in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了当众演讲的恐惧。
words.en: If you overcome a problem or a feeling, you successfully deal with it and control it.

words.ex: The new law will supersede the old one.
words.ex_cn: 新法律将取代旧法律。
words.en: If something is superseded by something newer, it is replaced because it has become old-fashioned or unacceptable.

words.tr: v. 取代；迫使…离开家园；
words.ex: The new robot will displace the workers on the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 这个新机器人将取代装配线上的工人。
words.en: To displace something or someone means to take their place or to force them to leave their usual place or role.

words.ex: The team will oust the coach after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 球队在输球后将撤换教练。
words.en: If someone is ousted from a position of power, job, or place, they are forced to leave it.

words.tr:
n. 代用品；代替物；
v. 替代；
words.ex: Honey is a good substitute for sugar.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是糖的良好代用品。
words.en: A substitute is something or someone that takes the place or function of another.

words.ex: He surmounted his fears to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了恐惧，在公众面前发言。
words.en: If you surmount a problem or difficulty, you deal successfully with it.

words.ex: Smartphones supplanted landline phones.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机取代了固定电话。
words.en: To supplant someone or something means to take the place of them, often by being more powerful or effective.

words.tr:
v. 补充；与…相辅相成；
n. 补足物；补语；余角；
words.ex: The red scarf complements her blue coat.
words.ex_cn: 这条红围巾补充了她的蓝外套。
words.en: To complement something means to make it complete or perfect by adding something to it.

words.tr:
n. 附属物；
adj. 附属的；
words.ex: The printer is an adjunct to the computer.
words.ex_cn: 打印机是电脑的附属物。
words.en: Something that is added or attached to something else but is not essential to it.

words.tr:
v. 补充；
n. 补充物；附加费；
words.ex: He supplements his income by teaching part-time.
words.ex_cn: 他通过兼职教学来补充收入。
words.en: A supplement is something that is added to something else in order to make it complete or better.

words.tr: v. 使不知所措；使无法解决；击败；压垮；淹没
words.ex: The homework overwhelms her every night.
words.ex_cn: 每天晚上的作业让她感到不堪重负。
words.en: To overwhelm means to bury or drown beneath a huge mass of something, or to defeat someone completely.

words.ex: The new car outstrips the old one in speed.
words.ex_cn: 这辆新车在速度上超过了旧车。
words.en: To outstrip means to go faster or to do better than someone or something else.

words.ex: His talent overshadowed his brother's achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他的才华使他兄弟的成就黯然失色。
words.en: If an unpleasant event or feeling overshadows something, it makes it less happy or enjoyable.

words.tr:
adj. 可代替的；可互换的
n. 代替物
words.ex: Money is fungible because you can use it for anything.
words.ex_cn: 货币是可互换的，因为你可以用它做任何事。
words.en: If something is fungible, it can be exchanged or substituted for something else of the same kind, and it will make no practical difference.

words.ex: He upended the bucket to drain the water.
words.ex_cn: 他把桶倒过来把水倒出。
words.en: To upend something means to turn it upside down or to change it completely.

words.ex: He tried to retaliate by spreading rumors.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过散布谣言来报复。
words.en: If you retaliate when someone harms or annoys you, you do something which harms or annoys them in return.

chapters.name: 悲伤/失望/忧郁/悲观/羞愧/畏惧

words.ex: He is pessimistic about the future.
words.ex_cn: 他对未来持悲观态度。
words.en: If someone is pessimistic, they expect that bad things will happen in the future or that something will have a bad result.

words.ex: His pessimism made him expect the worst.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲观主义让他总是预期最坏的结果。
words.en: Pessimism is the belief that bad things are going to happen or that something is going to turn out badly.

words.ex: He is diffident when he speaks in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班面前说话时很腼腆。
words.en: If you are diffident, you are rather shy and do not enjoy talking about yourself or being noticed by other people.

words.ex: The storm was formidable and destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴很可怕，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as formidable, you mean that you feel slightly frightened by them because they are very great or impressive.

words.tr: adj. 使人畏缩的；吓人的； v. “daunt”的现在分词；
words.ex: The math test seemed daunting to him.
words.ex_cn: 这次数学考试让他感到畏缩。
words.en: Something that is daunting makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.tr: adj. 耸人听闻的；极好的；
words.ex: The newspaper published a sensational story about a ghost.
words.ex_cn: 这家报纸刊登了一篇关于幽灵的耸人听闻的消息。
words.en: A sensational event or situation is so remarkable that it causes great excitement and interest.

words.tr: n. 追求轰动效应；哗众取宠
words.ex: The newspaper uses sensationalism to attract readers.
words.ex_cn: 这家报纸使用煽情主义来吸引读者。
words.en: Sensationalism is the use of sensational subject matter, style, or methods, or the condition of being sensational.

words.tr: v. 使石化；使僵化；吓呆
words.ex: The lightning petrified the tree into stone.
words.ex_cn: 闪电把树变成了石头。
words.en: To petrify means to make someone so frightened that they are unable to move or think.

words.ex: She was aghast when she saw the mess.
words.ex_cn: 她看到那片狼藉时惊呆了。
words.en: If you are aghast, you are filled with horror and surprise.

words.ex: His timidity made him afraid to speak in class.
words.ex_cn: 他的胆怯让他不敢在课堂上发言。
words.en: The quality or state of being timid; lack of courage or self-confidence.

words.ex: He is timorous when speaking in front of people.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前说话时很胆怯。
words.en: If you describe someone as timorous, you mean that they are nervous and lack courage or confidence.

words.ex: He sat in pensiveness, staring at the window.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在那里沉思，凝视着窗户。
words.en: The state of being deep in thought, often with some sadness.

words.ex: The violin played a plaintive melody.
words.ex_cn: 小提琴演奏了一首哀伤的旋律。
words.en: A plaintive sound or voice expresses sadness.

words.tr: adj. 忧郁的；抑郁的；患忧郁症的；
words.ex: He looked melancholic after the rain stopped.
words.ex_cn: 雨停后，他看起来忧郁的。
words.en: A melancholic person is someone who is often sad or depressed.

words.ex: He remained passive during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持被动。
words.en: Accepting or allowing what happens or what others do, without active response or resistance.

words.tr: adj. 黑暗的；幽暗的；忧郁的；沮丧的
words.ex: The room was gloomy with no windows.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间没有窗户，很黑暗。
words.en: If a place is gloomy, it is almost dark so that you cannot see very well. If people are gloomy, they are unhappy and have no hope.

words.tr: adj. 感情脆弱的；易落泪的；多愁善感的
words.ex: She was feeling maudlin after watching the sentimental movie.
words.ex_cn: 看完那部感人的电影后，她感到非常伤感。
words.en: If you describe someone as maudlin, you mean that they are being sad and sentimental in a foolish way, perhaps because of drinking alcohol.

words.ex: The ground is damp after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后地面是潮湿的。
words.en: Something that is damp is slightly wet, often in a way that is unpleasant.

words.ex: The rain dampened the sound of the drums.
words.ex_cn: 雨减弱了鼓声。
words.en: To dampen something means to make it slightly wet, or to make it less strong or intense.

words.ex: The sweater shrinks in hot water.
words.ex_cn: 这件毛衣在热水中会收缩。
words.en: If something shrinks or you shrink it, it becomes smaller.

words.ex: He showed cowardice when he ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他在打架时逃跑，表现出了懦弱。
words.en: Cowardice is the lack of courage to face danger, difficulty, opposition, or pain.

words.tr: adj. 悲哀的；可怜的；郁郁不乐的
words.ex: Her lugubrious expression made everyone feel sad.
words.ex_cn: 她那悲哀的表情让每个人都感到难过。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is lugubrious, you mean that they are sad and solemn.

words.tr:
n. 忏悔室；告解所
adj. 自白的；忏悔的
words.ex: He went to the confessional to tell his sins.
words.ex_cn: 他去告解室坦白自己的罪过。
words.en: A confessional is a small, enclosed booth in a church where a priest sits to hear confessions.

words.tr: v. 使羞惭；使不安；使窘迫
words.ex: He was abashed when he forgot his lines.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记台词时，他感到尴尬。
words.en: If someone is abashed, they feel embarrassed and ashamed.

words.tr: adv. 不畏惧地；不害躁地
words.ex: He unabashedly loves pizza.
words.ex_cn: 他毫不掩饰地爱披萨。
words.en: In a manner that is not embarrassed or ashamed.

words.ex: He felt awkward when he forgot his friend's name.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记朋友的名字时，他感到很尴尬。
words.en: If you describe a situation as awkward, you mean that it is embarrassing or difficult to deal with.

words.ex: He felt embarrassment when he tripped in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前绊倒时感到窘迫。
words.en: A feeling of self-consciousness, shame, or awkwardness.

words.ex: He gave a jeremiad about the bad weather.
words.ex_cn: 他抱怨了糟糕的天气。
words.en: A jeremiad is a long, mournful complaint or lamentation; a list of woes.

words.tr:
v. 皱眉；蹙额
n. 皱眉；蹙额
words.ex: He frowns when he hears bad news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到坏消息时会皱眉。
words.en: If you frown, you bring your eyebrows together so that there are lines on your face above your eyes, often because you are annoyed or worried.

words.ex: He bemoans the loss of his old car.
words.ex_cn: 他抱怨失去了他的旧车。
words.en: If you bemoan something, you express sorrow or dissatisfaction about it.

words.ex: The loud noise caused him vexation.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让他感到烦恼。
words.en: The state of being annoyed, frustrated, or worried.

words.tr: n. 良心的责备；后悔；悔恨
words.ex: He felt no compunction about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他撒谎骗朋友时毫无愧疚。
words.en: A feeling of guilt or moral scruple that prevents or follows the doing of something bad.

words.ex: He recoiled when he saw the snake.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到蛇时，他退缩了。
words.en: If something makes you recoil, you move your body quickly away from it because it frightens, offends, or hurts you.

words.ex: He built his endurance by running every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天早晨跑步来增强耐力。
words.en: The ability to endure an unpleasant or difficult process or situation without giving up.

words.ex: He had to endure the cold winter without a coat.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不在没有外套的情况下忍受寒冷的冬天。
words.en: To endure means to suffer something difficult, unpleasant, or painful, or to continue to exist for a long time.

words.ex: His tenacity helped him finish the marathon despite the pain.
words.ex_cn: 他的坚韧让他即使疼痛也完成了马拉松。
words.en: The quality or fact of being able to grip something firmly; the quality or fact of being very determined and not giving up easily.

words.tr: adj. 紧握的；顽强的；坚决的；强的（记忆力）
words.ex: The child held the toy with tenacious hands.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用紧握的手抓住玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as tenacious, you are admiring their determination to do something and their refusal to stop trying even when it is difficult.

words.ex: I can't tolerate loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 我无法容忍巨大的噪音。
words.en: If you tolerate a situation or person, you accept them although you do not particularly like them.

words.ex: The government showed toleration for different religions.
words.ex_cn: 政府对不同的宗教表现出容忍。
words.en: The willingness to allow something that one does not necessarily agree with or like.

words.ex: His tolerance for different opinions is impressive.
words.ex_cn: 他对不同观点的宽容令人印象深刻。
words.en: The ability or willingness to tolerate the existence of opinions or behaviour that one dislikes or disagrees with.

words.tr:
n. 辩论；讨论；
v. 辩论；讨论；
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: If you maintain something, you continue to have it, and do not let it stop or grow weaker.

words.ex: This bag is durable and lasts for years.
words.ex_cn: 这个包很耐用，可以用很多年。
words.en: Something that is durable is strong and lasts a long time without breaking or becoming weaker.

words.ex: The durability of this plastic makes it good for outdoor use.
words.ex_cn: 这种塑料的持久性使它适合户外使用。
words.en: The ability of something to last a long time without significant deterioration.

words.ex: The bridge can withstand strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥能经受住强风。
words.en: If something or someone withstands a force or action, they survive it or do not give in to it.

words.ex: The teacher will not condone cheating in exams.
words.ex_cn: 老师不会容忍考试作弊。
words.en: To condone something means to accept or allow behavior that is considered wrong.

words.ex: His firmness in decision made everyone trust him.
words.ex_cn: 他做决定时的坚定让每个人都信任他。
words.en: The quality of being firm in structure or purpose.

chapters.name: 命令/权威/独裁/自主/强制/严厉

words.tr: adj. 要求高的；费力的； v. 需要；“demand”的现在分词；
words.ex: The job is demanding because it needs long hours and high focus.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作要求高，因为它需要长时间工作和高度专注。
words.en: Requiring much effort or attention; exacting.

words.tr: adj. 严格的；缜密的；严密的；
words.ex: The teacher is rigorous about homework deadlines.
words.ex_cn: 老师对作业截止日期要求严格。
words.en: If you are rigorous in something, you are very thorough and strict in the way you do it.

words.ex: The math proof requires rigor.
words.ex_cn: 这个数学证明需要严谨。
words.en: Rigor is a situation in which people are made to follow rules in a very strict way.

words.ex: He solves math problems rigorously.
words.ex_cn: 他严格地解决数学问题。
words.en: In a thorough, strict, or extremely careful manner.

words.tr: adj. 教条的；武断的；固执己见的
words.ex: He is dogmatic about his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己信念非常固执。
words.en: If you say that someone is dogmatic, you are critical of them because they are convinced that they are right, and refuse to consider that other opinions might also be justified.

words.ex: He is undogmatic in his teaching style.
words.ex_cn: 他的教学风格不教条。
words.en: Not dogmatic; not bound by or committed to a particular doctrine or set of beliefs.

words.tr: adj. 刻板的；坚硬的；严格的；
words.ex: He has a rigid attitude toward rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的态度很刻板。
words.en: not able to be changed or adapted; not able to be bent or moved; stiff

words.tr: n. 坚硬；严格；刚直；死板
words.ex: The rigidity of the metal made it hard to bend.
words.ex_cn: 金属的刚性使其难以弯曲。
words.en: The quality or state of being rigid; stiffness; inflexibility.

words.ex: The teacher gave an authoritative answer.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了一个权威性的回答。
words.en: If something is authoritative, it is respected and accepted as true or correct because it comes from a reliable source.

words.ex: The country suffers from authoritarianism.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家遭受着专制主义的困扰。
words.en: Authoritarianism is a political system characterized by strong central power and limited political freedoms.

words.ex: The manager will authorize the payment tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 经理明天将批准这笔付款。
words.en: To give official permission for something to happen, or to give someone official permission to do something.

words.tr:
adj. 要求严格的；要求小心仔细的；苛求的
v. 强求；急需；要求；“exact”的现在分词
words.ex: He is an exacting teacher who wants perfect work.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个要求严格的老师，要求完美无缺的作业。
words.en: requiring a lot of effort, care, or attention

words.tr: adv. 确切地；正是；准确地；
words.ex: He arrived exactly at 8 o'clock.
words.ex_cn: 他正好在八点到达。
words.en: In a precise manner; accurately.

words.tr: adj. 严重的；严厉的；非常困难的；
words.ex: The storm caused severe damage to the houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴对房屋造成了严重的破坏。
words.en: If something is severe, it is very bad or very serious.

words.ex: He was severely injured in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故中严重受伤。
words.en: If something is done severely, it is done in a very great or intense degree.

words.tr: n. 自主权；自治权；自治；
words.ex: The region demands autonomy from the central government.
words.ex_cn: 该地区要求从中央政府获得自主权。
words.en: Autonomy is the ability or condition of being self-governing; independence in one's thoughts or actions.

words.tr: adj. 自治的；有自治权的；自主的；
words.ex: The region has autonomous control over its education system.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区对其教育系统拥有自治权。
words.en: An autonomous organization, country, or region is independent and has the freedom to govern itself.

words.tr: adj. 专卖的；专利的；所有权的
words.ex: The company uses proprietary software to protect its data.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司使用专有软件来保护其数据。
words.en: Relating to an owner or ownership; exclusive rights of possession, use, or control.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet is compulsory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是必须的。
words.en: If something is compulsory, you must do it because of a rule or law.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.tr: adj. 自由决定的；酌情行事的；便宜行事的
words.ex: He spent his discretionary money on a new phone.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的可自由支配的钱花在了一部新手机上。
words.en: If something is discretionary, it is available for use as someone chooses, rather than according to a set plan or rule.

words.tr: adj. 强制性的；义务的；必须的；
words.ex: Wearing a helmet is obligatory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是强制性的。
words.en: If something is obligatory, you must do it because of a rule or law.

words.tr: v. 使负义务；使有责任；强制
words.ex: The law obligate him to pay taxes.
words.ex_cn: 法律迫使他缴税。
words.en: To obligate someone means to make it necessary for them to do something, especially because of a law, rule, or agreement.

words.tr:
adj. 极重要的；
n. 紧急的事；
words.ex: It is imperative to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水非常重要。
words.en: If it is imperative that something is done, that thing is extremely important and must be done.

words.ex: The teacher's strictness makes students follow rules.
words.ex_cn: 老师的严格使学生遵守规则。
words.en: The quality or condition of being strict.

words.tr: adj. 爱挑剔的；过分讲究的
words.ex: He is fastidious about keeping his room clean.
words.ex_cn: 他非常讲究保持房间整洁。
words.en: Very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail.

words.ex: He shows fastidiousness in cleaning his room every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天打扫房间时都很挑剔。
words.en: The quality of being very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail.

words.ex: The sailors cleaned the stern of the boat.
words.ex_cn: 水手们打扫了船尾。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behavior as stern, you mean that they are severe or strict.

words.ex: The teacher punished the student harshly.
words.ex_cn: 老师严厉地惩罚了那个学生。
words.en: In a severe or cruel manner; with severity or cruelty.

words.tr: adj. 压迫的；沉重的；难以忍受的；闷热的
words.ex: The oppressive heat made it hard to breathe.
words.ex_cn: 令人窒息的炎热让人难以呼吸。
words.en: If you describe a society, its laws, or customs as oppressive, you think they treat people in an unfair and cruel way and prevent them from having opportunities and freedom.

words.tr: adj. 过分挑剔的；苛求的
words.ex: He is finicky about what he eats.
words.ex_cn: 他对吃的东西很挑剔。
words.en: If you say that someone is finicky, you mean that they are very difficult to please because they want everything to be exactly right.

words.ex: The autocratic leader made all decisions without asking others.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁的领导人独自做出所有决定，从不询问他人。
words.en: If you describe someone as autocratic, you are criticizing them because they have complete power and make decisions without asking anyone else's advice.

words.ex: The imperious queen demanded immediate obedience.
words.ex_cn: 这位专横的女王要求立即服从。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperious, you mean that they have a proud manner and expect to be obeyed.

words.ex: The country values its sovereignty.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家重视它的主权。
words.en: Sovereignty is the power that a country has to govern itself or another country or state.

words.tr:
adj. 苦行的；禁欲主义的
n. 苦行者；禁欲者
words.ex: He lives an ascetic life with no luxury.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，没有任何奢侈。
words.en: An ascetic person has a way of life that is simple and strict, usually because of their religious beliefs.

words.ex: This car is economical because it uses little fuel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车很经济，因为它耗油少。
words.en: Using money, resources, or time in a careful and effective way.

words.ex: Driving alone is uneconomical because of high fuel costs.
words.ex_cn: 独自开车因为燃油费用高而不经济。
words.en: If you say that something is uneconomical, you mean that it does not make a profit or that it is not efficient in its use of resources.

words.tr: adj. 清醒的；严肃的；素淡的；
words.ex: He stayed sober after drinking only water.
words.ex_cn: 他只喝了水，保持清醒。
words.en: If you are sober, you are not drunk. If you are sober, you are serious and thoughtful.

words.tr: adj. 有节制的；饮食有度的
words.ex: He is abstemious with sugar and eats little dessert.
words.ex_cn: 他对糖很节制，吃很少的甜点。
words.en: Someone who is abstemious avoids doing too much of something enjoyable, especially eating or drinking.

words.ex: He shows abstemiousness by eating little and avoiding sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他通过少吃并避免吃糖来表现节制。
words.en: The quality of being moderate in eating and drinking, especially in the consumption of alcohol.

words.tr: adj. 简朴的；严厉的；苦行的；紧缩的
words.ex: The room has austere walls with no decorations.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的墙壁朴素，没有任何装饰。
words.en: If you describe something as austere, you approve of its plain and simple appearance.

words.tr: n. 紧缩；艰苦朴素；节俭
words.ex: The government implemented austerity measures to reduce the budget deficit.
words.ex_cn: 政府实施了紧缩措施以减少预算赤字。
words.en: Austerity is a situation in which people's living standards are reduced because of economic difficulties.

words.ex: He practices abstinence from alcohol.
words.ex_cn: 他戒酒。
words.en: The practice of restraining oneself from indulging in something, typically alcohol or sex.

words.ex: He practiced stoicism by staying calm during hardship.
words.ex_cn: 他在逆境中保持冷静，践行斯多亚学派的哲学。
words.en: Stoicism is the endurance of pain or hardship without the display of feelings and without complaint.

words.tr: n. 吝啬；小气；过度节俭
words.ex: His parsimony led to a reputation for stinginess.
words.ex_cn: 他的吝啬导致了他被认为是个小气鬼。
words.en: Parsimony is the quality of being very unwilling to spend money.

chapters.name: 笨拙/幼稚/年轻/艰苦/勤恳

words.ex: The child gave a naive smile when he believed the story.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子相信这个故事时，他露出了天真的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as naïve, you think they lack experience and so expect things to be easy or people to be honest or kind.

words.ex: His naivety made him trust strangers easily.
words.ex_cn: 他的天真使他很容易相信陌生人。
words.en: Naivety is the quality of being naive; innocence or lack of experience, wisdom, or judgment.

words.tr:
n. 尽力；尝试；
v. 尽力；奋力；
words.ex: His endeavor to finish the project took all his energy.
words.ex_cn: 他为完成这个项目付出了全部努力。
words.en: An endeavor is an attempt to do something, especially something new or original.

words.ex: The nascent industry is growing quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个新生的产业正在迅速发展。
words.en: Nascent things or processes are just beginning, and are expected to become stronger or to grow bigger.

words.tr: adj. 天真无邪的；无辜的；
words.ex: The innocent child smiled at the stranger.
words.ex_cn: 那个天真无邪的孩子对陌生人笑了。
words.en: If someone is innocent, they did not commit a crime which they have been accused of.

words.tr: adj. 未成熟的；无处世经验的；乳臭未干的
words.ex: The new recruits were callow and inexperienced.
words.ex_cn: 新兵们年轻而无经验。
words.en: If you describe someone as callow, you mean that they are inexperienced and immature.

words.tr:
adj. 青少年的；幼稚的；
n. 少年；
words.ex: The book is written for juvenile readers.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是为青少年读者撰写的。
words.en: A juvenile is a child or young person who is not yet old enough to be considered an adult.

words.ex: He gave an unsophisticated answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个不老练的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unsophisticated, you mean that they are simple and not complicated, often in a way that is considered positive because it is natural or honest.

words.tr: adj. 精密复杂的；老练的；
words.ex: The phone has a sophisticated camera.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个精密复杂的摄像头。
words.en: A sophisticated person is intelligent and knows a lot, so that they are able to understand complicated situations. A sophisticated machine, device, or method is more advanced or complex than others.

words.ex: The sophistication of the machine allows it to work very precisely.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的精密使其能够非常精确地工作。
words.en: Sophistication refers to the quality of being sophisticated, which includes complexity, refinement, and worldly experience.

words.tr: adj. 装模作样的；笨手笨脚的；爱管闲事的；胡乱的; v. 笨手笨脚；跌跌撞撞地前进；模糊不清地说...
words.ex: His bumbling smile made everyone feel he was pretending to be friendly.
words.ex_cn: 他装模作样的微笑让所有人都觉得他是在假装友好。
words.en: If you describe someone as bumbling, you mean that they behave in a confused, disorganized way, making mistakes and usually not achieving anything.

words.ex: The onerous workload made her tired every day.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量让她每天都很累。
words.en: If you describe a task as onerous, you dislike having to do it because you find it difficult or unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 笨重的；难处理的；臃肿的；庞大的
words.ex: The box was unwieldy and hard to carry.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子又大又笨重，很难搬。
words.en: An unwieldy object is difficult to move or handle because of its size, shape, or weight.

words.ex: As a tyro in the field, he found the learning curve quite steep.
words.ex_cn: 作为这个领域的新手，他发现学习曲线相当陡峭。
words.en: A tyro is someone who is new to and therefore inexperienced at a particular activity.

words.ex: He is diligent in doing his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都很勤奋地做作业。
words.en: Someone who is diligent works hard and is careful and thorough.

words.tr: adj. 空洞的；枯燥乏味的；不成熟的；缺乏营养的
words.ex: His jejune remarks made no sense to the audience.
words.ex_cn: 他幼稚的言论让听众无法理解。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as jejune, you are criticizing them for being very simple and unsophisticated.

words.ex: He is clumsy and dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他很笨拙，把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: A clumsy person moves or handles things in a careless, awkward way, often so that things are knocked over or broken.

words.ex: The ungainly boy tripped over his own feet.
words.ex_cn: 这个笨拙的男孩被自己的脚绊倒了。
words.en: If you describe a person, animal, or vehicle as ungainly, you mean that they look awkward or clumsy, often because they are big.

words.ex: The old system is cumbersome and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这个旧系统复杂而低效。
words.en: Something that is cumbersome is large and heavy and therefore difficult to carry, wear, or handle.

words.ex: The truck suffered an overload and broke down.
words.ex_cn: 这辆卡车因超载而抛锚了。
words.en: To load or burden someone or something excessively.

words.ex: He laboriously wrote the letter by hand.
words.ex_cn: 他费力地用手写这封信。
words.en: In a way that requires a lot of effort and time.

words.ex: He is a conscientious student who always finishes his homework on time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个尽责的学生，总是按时完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is conscientious is very careful to do their work properly.

words.tr: adv. 孜孜不倦地；勤勉地
words.ex: He sedulously practices piano every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都勤勉地练习钢琴。
words.en: If you do something sedulously, you do it carefully and thoroughly, paying great attention to detail.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.tr: n. 艰难，艰苦，艰辛，奋斗
words.ex: The arduousness of the hike made him tired.
words.ex_cn: 徒步的艰难让他感到疲惫。
words.en: The quality of requiring great physical or mental effort; difficulty.

words.tr: adj. 自发的；自然产生的；
words.ex: The children gave a spontaneous cheer.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们自发地欢呼起来。
words.en: Something that is spontaneous is not planned but happens or is done because of a sudden impulse or natural feeling.

words.ex: His spontaneity made the party fun.
words.ex_cn: 他的自发性让派对变得有趣。
words.en: The condition of being spontaneous; impulsive or natural action or behavior.

words.tr: adj. 顽固的；执拗的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: He is obdurate and refuses to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他固执己见，拒绝改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obdurate, you mean that they are determined not to change their mind or attitude in spite of efforts to persuade them.

words.ex: His obduracy in the face of evidence was astounding.
words.ex_cn: 面对证据，他的执拗态度令人震惊。
words.en: Obduracy is the quality of being very determined not to change your beliefs, feelings, or actions, especially in a way that seems unreasonable.

words.ex: The app has an intuitive design.
words.ex_cn: 这个应用程序具有直观的设计。
words.en: An intuitive idea or feeling is based on an instinctive emotional response rather than on conscious thought.

words.ex: I trusted my intuition and chose the right answer.
words.ex_cn: 我相信自己的直觉，选了正确的答案。
words.en: Intuition is the ability to understand or know something immediately, without the need for conscious reasoning.

words.ex: It seems counterintuitive, but less sleep can make you tired.
words.ex_cn: 这看起来违反直觉，但睡得少会让你更累。
words.en: Counterintuitive means contrary to what one would intuitively expect.

words.ex: He made an impetuous decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他冲动地决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as impetuous, you mean that they are likely to act quickly and suddenly without thinking or being careful.

words.ex: The cat made an instinctive jump to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 猫本能地跳开以躲避狗。
words.en: An instinctive feeling, action, or idea is one that you have or do without thinking or reasoning.

words.ex: Honesty is an inherent quality of a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是好领导固有的品质。
words.en: Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.

words.ex: Birds are inherently able to fly.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类固有地能够飞行。
words.en: In a way that is a natural or essential part of something.

words.ex: Babies have an innate ability to cry.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿生来就有哭泣的能力。
words.en: An innate quality or ability is one that you were born with, not one you have learned.

words.ex: He is stubborn and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很顽固，不肯改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is stubborn is determined to do what they want and is very unwilling to change their mind.

words.ex: He stubbornly refused to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他固执地拒绝改变主意。
words.en: In a manner that shows determination not to change one's attitude or position on something, especially in spite of good reasons to do so.

words.tr: n. 顽固；执拗；坚持到底
words.ex: His pertinacity helped him finish the hard task.
words.ex_cn: 他的执着帮助他完成了这项困难的任务。
words.en: The quality of holding firmly to a purpose, belief, or action; stubbornness.

words.tr: adj. 天生的；先天的；天赋的
words.ex: He has an inborn talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 他天生就有音乐才能。
words.en: An inborn quality or ability is one that you have had naturally since birth.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；固执的；顽固的；
words.ex: He is obstinate and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很执拗，不肯改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obstinate, you are being critical of them because they are very determined to do what they want, and refuse to change their mind or be persuaded to do something else.

words.ex: The painting has a simple aesthetic appeal.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有一种简单的审美吸引力。
words.en: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty.

words.tr: adj. 有利的；吉祥的；吉利的
words.ex: The weather was propitious for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: If something is propitious, it is likely to lead to success, or it indicates a good chance of success.

words.tr: adj. 不吉利的；不顺遂的
words.ex: The weather was unpropitious for the outdoor event.
words.ex_cn: 天气对户外活动不利。
words.en: If you describe something as unpropitious, you mean that it is likely to lead to failure or be unfavorable.

words.ex: She wore an elegant dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条优雅的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe a person or thing as elegant, you mean that they are pleasing and graceful in appearance or style.

words.ex: The forest remained pristine and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林保持原始且未被破坏。
words.en: Something that is pristine is in its original condition and has not been spoiled or damaged.

words.ex: He is a paragon of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他是诚实的典范。
words.en: A paragon is someone who is considered to be a perfect example of a particular quality.

words.tr: adj. 典型的；精髓的；精华的
words.ex: He is the quintessential teacher, patient and kind.
words.ex_cn: 他是典型的教师，耐心而和善。
words.en: Representing the most perfect or typical example of a quality or class.

words.tr: adj. 无可挑剔的；无瑕疵的；
words.ex: Her impeccable manners impressed everyone at the dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她无可挑剔的礼仪让晚宴上的每个人都印象深刻。
words.en: If you describe something as impeccable, you are emphasizing that it is perfect and has no faults.

words.ex: It was an auspicious day for their wedding.
words.ex_cn: 那天是他们婚礼的吉日。
words.en: If you describe something as auspicious, you mean that it is a sign of future success.

words.tr: v. 重述要点；简要回顾
words.ex: Can you recapitulate the main points of the lecture?
words.ex_cn: 你能重述一下讲座的主要要点吗？
words.en: If you recapitulate something, you say it again briefly, or you give a summary of it.

words.tr: n. 概括，重述要点；（生育、生长中对进化等过程的）重演；（尤指奏鸣曲形式中的）再现部
words.ex: The professor's lecture ended with a recapitulation of the main points.
words.ex_cn: 教授的讲座以概括主要观点结束。
words.en: A recapitulation is a summary or brief restatement of the main points of something, especially at the end of a speech, lecture, or piece of writing.

words.ex: He did revision for his math test last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚为数学考试进行了复习。
words.en: The act or process of revising; a revised or new version, as of a book or other written material.

words.ex: He is a revisionist historian who questions old stories.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位修正主义历史学家，质疑旧的故事。
words.en: A revisionist is someone who advocates or practices revision, especially of a political or historical nature, often challenging the accepted views or interpretations.

words.ex: He will restore the old bike.
words.ex_cn: 他将修复这辆旧自行车。
words.en: To restore something means to bring it back to its original condition or to a state of health, efficiency, or good management.

words.tr:
adj. 恢复健康的；促使康复的；
n. 有助恢复健康的事物；滋补品；
words.ex: The tea has a restorative effect on tired people.
words.ex_cn: 这种茶对疲劳的人有恢复健康的作用。
words.en: A restorative is something that makes you feel healthier, stronger, or more energetic after you have been feeling ill, weak, or tired.

words.ex: The city plan will revitalize the old town.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市计划将使老城区复兴。
words.en: To revitalize something means to give it new life or energy.

words.ex: The revival of traditional music brought joy to many people.
words.ex_cn: 传统音乐的复兴给许多人带来了快乐。
words.en: The process of something becoming popular or active again after a period of inactivity or decline.
